Table 1: ICO at a glance 
 
1. Federal Agency Name: AFWERX Prime, AFRL/RGP 
 
2. Federal Agencies Capable of Issuing Contracts/Agreements: DoD users approved by 
AFWERX to leverage the AFWERX Prime ICO. 
 
3. Innovative Capabilities Opening (ICO) Type: This is an ICO with Calls. This ICO will remain 
open until the AFWERX Prime program has no further requirements to obtain new solutions 
or new capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential 
technological advances. This technique is for the publication of an umbrella solicitation that 
contains the basic information but does not request Pitch Decks or proposals with its initial 
issuance. This type of opening functions as the framework for future Calls by identifying the 
basic terms and administrative information of the ICO. The ICO will be amended to issue 
Calls with focus areas defined by AFWERX. It is anticipated that the AFWERX Prime ICO 
will be updated at least annually, and this umbrella ICO will be open in perpetuity until 
canceled by the Air Force. Of note, the Government will not accept white papers under this 
ICO. Pitch Decks and Proposals shall only be submitted in response to Calls. 
 
4. Calls: Calls will be issued that detail specific Areas of Interest (AOI), consistent with 
AFWERX Prime mission and objectives . Each Call will identify the instructions for 
submitting solutions, proposal instructions, timelines, and other related information. 
 
5. General Information 
 
The purpose of this ICO is to provide the overarching solicitation structure for which future 
Calls will be issued. The purpose of each Call will be to competitively solicit solutions for 
prototype and fielding resulting from their initial submissions in response to the calls posted 
on sam.gov associated with this ICO. 
 

FA228024R0007 - Page 2  
6. Background & Authority 
 
AFWERX Prime aims to accelerate and “prime” emerging commercial markets by 
incorporating military interests to help advance new technologies. This benefits both the 
commercial industry and military capabilities. 
 
In addition to funding, Prime leverages other unique Department resources, like test 
infrastructure, certification authorities, interagency relationships, and early operational use 
cases, bringing the Department of the Air Force’s full value proposition to bear by becoming 
an early adopter to de-risk emerging markets. 
 
This ICO will be used to award Other Transactions for Prototype Project (OTP) agreements 
IAW 10 U.S.C. § 4022. 
 
OTP agreements issued against this competitive solicitation must satisfy at least one of the 
following conditions: 
 
- There is at least one non-traditional defense contractor or nonprofit research 
institution participating to a significant extent in the prototype project 
- All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are 
small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors. 
- At least one third of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds 
provided by sources other than the Federal Government. 
- The senior procurement executive for the agency determines in writing that 
exceptional circumstances justify the use of a transaction that provides for 
innovative business arrangements or structures that would not be feasible or 
appropriate under a procurement contract, or would provide an opportunity to 
expand the defense supply base in a manner that would not be practical or feasible 
under a contract. 
 
7. ICO Vision 
 
The purpose of this ICO is to provide for the rapid solicitation and award of AFWERX Prime 
sponsored technology areas of interest. This is accomplished through issuing this umbrella 
ICO which will remain open until AFWERX deems the solicitation no longer necessary. Calls 
issued under this ICO solicitation will define specific areas of interest, the open period when 
offers may be submitted, and the points of contact related to those interest areas. 
 
The Government reserves the right to award an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 
10 U.S.C. § 4022, including prototype and follow-on production, or no contract instrument at 
all, as a result of this solicitation. Awards can be for all or some of the submitted solutions. 
Follow-on production contracts may be issued if the award was a result of this competitive 
solicitation and the prototype project has been determined successful. 
 
8. ICO Definitions 
 
a. “Call” A Call is an amendment to an umbrella ICO defining technical areas of 
interest, submission instructions, timelines, points of contact, and other specific 

FA228024R0007 - Page 3  
information. The Call is a request for response from prospective industry partners. 
 
b. “Open Period” refers to the date that a Call is open for offerors to submit solutions. 
Solutions will be evaluated as soon as practicable (i.e., as they are received) and 
awards may be issued during the open period. Evaluations and awards may be 
made after the closing date for those submissions received prior to the closing date 
and time provided within the Call. Solutions submitted after the closing date will not 
be considered. 
 
c. “Innovative Capabilities Opening” (ICO) is a competitive procedure agreements 
officers may use to acquire prototypes as provided in 10 U.S.C. § 4022. 
 
d. "Other Transaction” refers to the statutory authority to enter into transactions other 
than procurement contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements. The DoD has the 
authority to enter into Other Transactions for Research Projects (10 U.S.C. § 4021) 
and Other Transactions for Prototype Projects (10 U.S.C. § 4022). 
 
e. “Prototype Project” is defined at 10 U.S.C. § 4022(e)(5) The definition of a "prototype 
project" in the context of an OT is as follows: (A) a prototype project addresses a 
proof of concept, model, or process, including a business process, (B) reverse 
engineering to address obsolescence, (C) a pilot or novel application of commercial 
technologies for defense purposes, (D) agile development activity, (E) the creation, 
design, development, demonstration of technical or operational utility, or (F) 
combinations of the foregoing. 
 
Although assistance terms are generally not appropriate in OT agreements, ancillary 
work efforts that are necessary for completion of the prototype project, such as test 
site training or limited logistics support, may be included in prototype projects. A 
prototype may be physical, virtual, or conceptual in nature. A prototype project may 
be fully funded by DoD, jointly funded by multiple federal agencies, cost-shared, 
funded in whole or part by third parties, or involve a mutual commitment of resources 
other than an exchange of funds. 
 
f. “Nontraditional Defense Contractor” is defined in 10 U.S.C. § 3014 as an entity that 
is not currently performing and has not performed, for at least the one-year period 
preceding the solicitation of sources by the Department of Defense for the 
procurement or transaction, any contract or subcontract for the Department of 
Defense that is subject to full coverage under the cost accounting standards 
prescribed pursuant to section 1502 of title 41 and the regulations implementing 
such section. This includes all small business concerns under the criteria and size 
standards in 15 U.S.C. § 632 and 13 C.F.R. Part 121. 
 
g. “Nonprofit Research Institution” means a nonprofit institution, as defined in 15 
U.S.C. § 3703 as an organization owned and operated exclusively for scientific or 
educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of 
any private shareholder or individual. 
 
h. “Small Business Concerns” is defined in the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. § 632) 

FA228024R0007 - Page 4  
and 13 CFR Part 121. 
9. ICO Procedure 
 
All Solutions submitted in response to Calls will be in response to and governed by the 
procedures and guidelines as defined in this ICO. Calls will be issued and follow the 
two-step methodology described below - 
 
a. Step 1 - Pitch Deck Submission: Offerors shall submit a 10 slide Pitch Deck 
summarizing the offeror’s proposed technical approach to meet the objectives 
defined within the Call. 
 
i. Offerors submissions will be evaluated to determine whether the submission 
is selectable or non-selectable. 
 
1. Selectable submissions are those that are eligible, technically 
feasible, and demonstrate importance to the agency's objectives 
defined within each Call. Selectable rated submissions may be 
eligible for Step 2 – Request for Proposal based on availability of 
funds. Selectable submissions may progress into Step 2 anytime 
within a year after the closing date of the Call. 
 
2. Non-selectable submissions are those that are not eligible, are not 
technically feasible, or do not demonstrate importance to the 
agency's objectives defined within each Call. Non-selectable 
submissions will not move to Step 2 at any time. Offerors may 
request feedback upon notification of non-selectable status. 
 
b. Step 2 - Request for Proposal (RFP): Those offerors whose Pitch Deck is evaluated 
and determined to be selectable may be invited to submit a full written proposal 
following the instructions provided in Request for RFP. Awards will result from 
successful evaluation and negotiation of proposals received in response to Step 2 of 
the Call, and are subject to the availability of funds.

ii. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the proposed

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY.  This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations.  The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement.  The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method.

The intended contract is a firm-fixed price.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following in support of the Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 20.

VISN 20 has a need for a single award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for Intra Enterprise and Depot Express Package Tracking System licenses. This will be a brand name or equal requirement.

Background: The VA Northwest Health Network, Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN 20), is responsible for providing health care to Veterans in the states of Alaska, Washington, Oregon, most of the state of Idaho, and one county each in Montana and California. We cover 817,417 square miles, approximately 23% of the US. Our eight facilities currently operate over 1,100 inpatient beds for acute medical/surgical, mental health, nursing home, and rehabilitative care. 

Six of the eight facility Supply Chain Management departments need a replacement contract vehicle that provides Package Tracking System Licenses and Warranty/Replacement Program to continue the use of the infrastructure and workflow processes that have been put into place over the past couple of years. The system provides Supply Chain Management staff and recipients of expected packages with a real-time view of package tracking. The system also creates a record of the full chain of custody from receiving/request through pickup/delivery, inducing attempted deliveries. Use of cordless scanners, barcode printers, workstation and mobile applications, the real-time system increases the efficiency of Supply Chain Management operations, provides visibility of urgent or miss-delivery, and allows recipients a quick and user-friendly way to check the status of their expected delivery. The desktop version of the system software for is TRM approved and the mobile version is authorized by Mobile Technology and Endpoint Security Engineering Team on iOS devices.

Scope: VA intends to award a VISN-wide contract for Package Tracking System licenses and an associated warranty/replacement program. The Package Tracking System shall integrate with existing cordless scanners, barcode printers, and mobile application infrastructure to scan and track packages being delivered to the VA facility from any external carrier and internally within the facility. The Package Tracking System shall include signature capture and must be accessible via computer/workstations and iOS mobile devices. The system must provide a real-time, end-to-end view of package tracking workflows. The system shall maintain a comprehensive record of the full chain of custody, from receipt or request through pickup and delivery. The system shall allow the VA to retain all the historical data and allow recipients of expected package view only access of the tracking data. The system warranty/replacement program shall provide seamless replacement or warranty service for cordless scanners and barcode printers as needed.

Licenses and Warranty/Replacement Program: 

Intra Enterprise platform, computer/workstation, and mobile licenses

Package tracking workflow licenses

Warranty/replacement program for existing cordless scanners and barcode printers

Estimated quantities for each year are as follows:

Contractor Point of Contact: The contractor shall provide telephone number(s) and contact person(s) to be used by the facility to make calls for system-related inquiries, request problem solving solutions and warranty/replacements during normal business hours, 8 am to 4 pm Pacific Time, excluding federal holidays.

Performance Monitoring: This contractor will be monitored by Government POC through tracking the access to the package tracking platform and licenses, and by monitoring the response time for the warranty/replacement program as needed.

Period of Performance: The period of performance shall be one twelve-month base period plus four additional twelve-month option period as stated below:

Place of Performance: Contract performance shall take place at the contractor’s location(s); the system will be accessed from the VISN 20 locations stated below, to include Community-based Outpatient Clinics (not listed below) and remote VA employee locations.

Potential candidates having the capabilities necessary to provide the stated services at a fair and reasonable price are invited to respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to Jennifer Robles at jennifer.robles1@va.gov  no later than April 29, 2026, 3PM, Mountain Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. 

RESPONSES SHOULD INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION:  Company name, address, SAM UEI, and business size; point of contact name, phone number, and e-mail address; whether services are presently offered on a current GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract, NASA SEWP, or any other Federal contract.  NAICS Code 541519, 150 employees, is applicable to determine business size standard. 

VAAR 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting will apply to this requirement in accordance with VAAR 819.711(b) if market research indicates a SDVOSB/VOSB set-aside or sole source award is appropriate. SDVOSB/VOSBs are asked to indicate whether they can comply with the requirements set forth in VAAR 852.219-75 should a set-aside or sole source award be considered. Full text available here: https://www.va.gov/oal/library/vaar/vaar852.asp#85221976. 

Any questions or concerns may also be directed via email to Jennifer Robles at jennifer.robles1@va.gov.

Disclaimer and Important Notes:  This Sources Sought Notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. The Government will treat any information received as proprietary and will not share such information with other companies.  Any organization responding to this Sources Sought Notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this announcement.  There is no solicitation available at this time.

STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)

NAVY Strategic Systems Programs (SSP) Nuclear Weapons Systems (NWS)

Support Services

Part 1

General Information

1.0 General Requirements – Applicable to All Contract Line Item Numbers (CLIN)

1.1 Implementation of the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) Memo

The following SOW language supplements Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Clause 252.204-7012 (MAY 2024) (DEVIATION 2024-O0013, REVISION 1) cited in Section I in accordance with the requirements of Navy Marine Corps Acquisition Regulation Supplement (NMCARS) ANNEX 16-STATEMENT OF WORK LANGUAGE IMPLEMENTING “THE DIB” MEMO  : 

1.1.1 System Security Plan and Plans of Action and Milestones Reviews (Contract Data Requirements List)

     a.  Within thirty (30) days of contract award, the Contractor shall make its System Security Plan(s) for its covered contractor information system(s) available for review by the Government at the contractor’s facility. The System Security Plan(s) shall implement the security requirements in DFARS clause 252.204-7012 (MAY 2024) (DEVIATION 2024-O0013, REVISION 1), which is included in this contract. The Contractor shall fully cooperate in the Government’s review of the System Security Plan(s) at the Contractor’s facility.

     b.  If the Government determines that the System Security Plan(s) does not adequately implement the requirements of DFARS clause 252.204-7012 (MAY 2024) (DEVIATION 2024-O0013, REVISION 1) then the Government shall notify the Contractor of each identified deficiency. The Contractor shall correct any identified deficiencies within thirty (30) days of notification by the Government. The contracting officer may provide for a correction period longer than thirty (30) days and, in such a case, may require the Contractor to submit a plan of action and milestones (POAM) for the correction of the identified deficiencies. The Contractor shall immediately notify the contracting officer of any failure or anticipated failure to meet a milestone in such a POAM. 

     c.  Upon the conclusion of the correction period, the Government may conduct a follow-on review of the System Security Plan(s) at the Contractor’s facilities. The Government may continue to conduct follow-on reviews until the Government determines that the Contractor has corrected all identified deficiencies in the System Security Plan(s).

 

     d.  The Government may, in its sole discretion, conduct subsequent reviews at the Contractor’s site to verify the information in the System Security Plan(s). The Government will conduct such reviews at least every three (3) years (measured from the date of contract award) and may conduct such reviews at any time upon thirty (30) days’ notice to the Contractor.

1.1.2 Compliance to National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-171   

     a.  The Contractor shall fully implement the Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Security Requirements (Requirements) and associated Relevant Security Controls (Controls) in NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-171 (Rev. 2) (NIST SP 800-171), or establish System Security Plan(s) and POAMs that varies from NIST 800-171 only in accordance with DFARS clause 252.204-7012 (DEVIATION 2024-O0013, REVISION 1), paragraph (b)(2), for all covered contractor information systems affecting this contract.

     b.  Notwithstanding the allowance for such variation, the contractor shall identify in any System Security Plan and POAM their plans to implement the following, at a minimum: 

          (1) Implement Control 3.5.3 (Multi-factor authentication). This means that multi-factor authentication is required for all users, privileged and unprivileged accounts that log into a network. In other words, any system that is not standalone should be required to utilize acceptable multi-factor authentication. 1.1.3 Cyber Incident Response

1.1.4 Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS) Outreach.

Use of this alternative approach shall also be the subject of a separate agreement negotiated between NCIS and the Contractor.

Statement of Work (SOW) 
Medical Staff Professional Support Services 
 
1. PROJECT TITLE:  The Indian Health Service (IHS)/Albuquerque Area, Albuquerque Service 
Unit (ASU) has a requirement for medical provider credentialing services located in 
Albuquerque, New Mexico. The Government contemplates to award a single award resulting 
from this solicitation. 
 
2. BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: An effective, timely, and accurate credentialing and privileging 
service to ensure the ASU provides safe patient care. The purpose is to ensure that clinical staff 
(physicians, advance practice providers, allied health professionals, etc.) remain properly 
credentialed, privileged, and compliant with relevant regulatory, payer, and organizational 
standards, the contractor shall provide medical staff credentialing and privileging support 
services. 
 
3. SCOPE:  The services sought includes the appropriate credentialing and privileging of medical 
and allied professional staff of permanent, contractors, students, volunteers, and telehealth 
providers. Services provided must meet the requirements specified in the medical staff bylaws, 
Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC) accreditation standards and all 
other applicable Federal, State and other regulatory agencies. Awardee must be familiar with 
credentialing and privileging requirements for family medicine, pediatrician, internal medicine 
physicians, advanced practice nurses, dentists, psychologists, psychiatrists, and telehealth 
providers. 
 
4. HOURS: Requires 32 hours per week/52 weeks a year, Monday through Friday 0800-1630, 
excluding all federal holidays. 
 
5. APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS:  ASU Medical Staff Bylaws; Governing Board Bylaws; 
AAAHC requirements; CMS requirements 
 
6. TASKS:  The Contractor shall provide: 
 
a. Knowledge and familiarity with electronic credentialing software programs, such as 
MD Staff 
b. Clear communication on all credentialing activities with the facility Clinical Director, 
Albuquerque Area Credentialing Consultant, and CEO 
c. Coordinates the initial and reappointment application process for all credentialed 
providers and reviews supporting documentation.  
d. Initiates and accepts all applications and verifies education, training, licensure, 
specialty boards, National Practitioner Data Bank reports, and professional 
references. 
e. Ensures the clinical privileges requested are consistent with education and training 
requirements within their specific specialty. Assists in development and maintenance 
of privileging forms, templates, and criteria (in consultation with medical staff 
leadership) consistent with bylaws, regulatory, and accrediting standards. 

DRAFT
f. Assembles all verified information and prepares the credentialing file for the Medical 
Executive Committee and Governing Board, within the timeframes dictated by the 
bylaws of the organization. 
g. Monitor and track the expiration dates of professional licensure, DEA licensure, 
prescribing licensure, basic life support certification, and obtaining primary source 
verification on all initial applications, reappointment applications and upon renewal 
of license. Notifies the medical staff leadership on any adverse findings. 
h. Notifies each credentialed staff member approximately 3 months before the 
expiration of the individual’s term of appointment of the need to begin and complete 
the reappointment process. 
i. Provide monthly performance reports including credentialing volume, cycle times, 
backlog, outstanding tasks, risk areas, and recommended process improvements to the 
Clinical Director. 
j. Support internal or external audits of credentialing files; provides files, 
documentation, and explanations as required. Assist in regulatory reviews (CMS or 
AAAHC) as needed. 
k. Follows the Privacy Act and service unit bylaws, rules, and regulations pertaining to 
confidentiality and protection of the material and maintenance of the files. 
 
7. GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED EQUIPMENT AND INFORMATION:  Because the work will 
be done remotely, there will be no Government furnished equipment. The Government will 
provide access to the credentialing software program. The contractor will provide any computer 
workstations necessary to complete the work. 
 
8. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE:  The contractor will be working remotely.   
 
9. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The period of performance is for a one-year base period, plus 
four one-year option periods if exercised.  
 
10. SECURITY:  The work stated in this SOW requires IT clearance for access to email and 
credentialing software program. The contractor does not need access to the facility or to patient 
health information. 
 
11. The contractor will comply with the following listed regulations: 
 
a. Privacy Act, 5 U.S.C. 552a- Office of Privacy and Civil Liberties | Privacy Act of 
1974 
b. Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)- eCFR :: 45 CFR Part 
164 -- Security and Privacy 
c. CFR 42 Part 2- eCFR :: 42 CFR Part 2 -- Confidentiality of Substance Use Disorder 
Patient Records 
 
12. Indemnification and Governing Law- Indemnification, Liability, Statue of Limitations: Any 
provisions in the Terms of Service (TOS) related to indemnification and filing deadlines are 
hereby waived, and shall not apply except to the extent expressly authorized by law. Liability for 
any breach of the TOS as modified by this amendment, shall be determined under the Federal 

DRAFT
Tort Claims Act, or other governing federal authority. Federal statute of limitations provisions 
shall apply to any breach or claim. 
 
Governing Law: Any arbitration, mediation or similar dispute resolution provision in the TOS is 
hereby deleted. The TOS and this amendment shall be governed by and interpreted and enforced 
in accordance with the laws of the United States of America without reference to conflict of 
laws. To the extent permitted by federal law, the laws of the State of New Mexico will apply in 
the absence of applicable federal law.

DARPA and the Performer are bound to each other by a duty of good faith and best research effort in achieving the goals of the Program.

The Parties agree that the principal purpose of this Agreement is for the Government and the Performer to provide for a coordinated effort to advance research and technology goals of the program and not primarily for the acquisition of property or services for the direct benefit or use of the Government. ARTICLE II:	TERM

A.	Term of this Agreement

The Program commences upon the date of the last signature hereon and continues for (INSERT NUMBER OF MONTHS) (xx) months.    Provisions of this Agreement, which, by their express terms or by necessary implication, apply for periods of time other than specified herein, shall be given effect, notwithstanding this Article.

B.	Termination Provisions

The Government may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the Performer, provided that such written notice is preceded by consultation between the Parties.  The Performer may request Agreement termination by giving the Government sixty (60) days written notification of their intent to do so.  If the Performer decides to request termination of this Agreement, the Government may, at its discretion, agree to terminate.  The Government and the Performer should negotiate in good faith a reasonable and timely adjustment of all outstanding issues between the Parties as a result of termination, which may include non-cancelable commitments.  In the event of a termination of the Agreement, the Government shall have paid-up rights in Data as described in Article VIII, Data Rights. The Performer, with DARPA participation and review, will prepare a final Annual Program Plan.

	

(b)	The Annual Program Plan provides a detailed schedule of research activities, commits the Performer to meet specific performance objectives and describes the milestones. DARPA-SN-26-62
Request for Information
DARPA-SN-26-62
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)
Tactical Technology Office (TTO)
Responses due June 1, 2026, by 4:00 PM Eastern Time (ET).
This Request for Information (RFI) from the Tactical Technology Office (TTO) within the Defense 
Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) seeks information on graphene production and use in 
load-bearing structures for aerospace applications. 
Responses to this RFI will be used to gather data for future possible programs. 
Intellectual or other privileged or proprietary information contained in a response to this RFI will not be 
distributed outside of the U.S. Government. In the event that a new DARPA program is developed in 
response to this RFI and a solicitation is issued, no intellectual or other proprietary information received 
in response to this RFI will be divulged to entities outside of the U.S. Government.
BACKGROUND:
Graphene is a relatively new two-dimensional material with exceptional strength, high thermal and 
electrical conductivity, and very  low weight.  DARPA is interested in exploring the use of graphene as an 
ingredient in aerospace structures to increase strength, stiffness, and/or flexibility while reducing weight. 
DESCRIPTION:
DARPA is interested in understanding the state-of-the-world and state-of-the-art for graphene production 
and manufacturing for potential use in load-bearing structures.  
This RFI seeks information on: 
1. The largest size (length, width, thickness)  of graphene sheets available for use in structural parts 
today.
2. Potential solutions to scale up the size and manufacturability of graphene sheets for aerospace 
structures.
3. Use of graphene in the design and manufacturing of load-bearing structure—i.e., static and 
fatigue strength/stiffness (in plane compression/tension, out of plane and interlaminar strength, 
shear strength), part size, manufacturing techniques, etc.  This can be as the main material, as an 
additive to other material or adhesives, or as a layer/ply in a composite part.
4. Test data that can substantiate the use of graphene as a structural material.
5. An estimate of weight reduction potential for graphene /graphene composite hybrid from 
traditional carbon composite/metallic structure.
6. An estimate of cost to produce aerostructures incorporating graphene.  This can be expressed as 
dollar-per-pound ($/lb), or some other measure as deemed appropriate. 
REQUESTED INFORMATION: 

DARPA-SN-26-62
Responses are welcome from all capable sources including, but not limited to, private or public 
companies, individuals, universities, University-Affiliated Research Centers (UARCs), Federally Funded 
Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs), not-for-profit research institutions, U.S. Government-
sponsored laboratories, large and small businesses, and nontraditional defense contractors. 
DARPA requests responses that address all technical areas below:
1. Current capability to manufacture graphene sheets in large sizes compatible with aerospace load-
bearing structures at any quantity.
2. Current capability to join together multiple graphene sheets to make larger structures.
3. Barriers to manufacturing graphene sheets in large sizes compatible with aerospace load-bearing 
structures at production-level quantity and quality.
4. Current capability to use graphene in manufacturing of load bearing structure. This can use 
graphene as the main material, as an additive to other material or adhesives, or as a layer/ply in a 
composite part.
5. An estimate of weight reduction for the same strength in a load bearing structure part.
6. An estimate of manufacturing costs for graphene aerostructures.
For the purposes of this RFI, DARPA is expressly not interested in the following:
1. Modeling or analysis techniques used for graphene material.
2. Theoretical assertations on the merits of graphene that are absent substantiating data.
3. Use of graphene to replace more orthodox methods of senor construction and integration unless 
specifically tied to load bearing structures.
4. Use of carbon nanotube material or particles in these applications.
SUBMISSION FORMAT:
This announcement contains all information required to submit a response. No additional forms, kits, or 
other materials are needed.
General Guidelines: 
1. Respondents to this RFI are encouraged to be as succinct as possible, while also providing 
actionable insight.
2. All submissions must be written in English.
3. White papers shall not exceed five (5) single-sided written pages using 11-point font with 1” 
margins all around. No smaller than 8-point font may be used for figures, tables, and charts. 
4. Electronic submittal shall be in Microsoft Word, Microsoft PowerPoint, or PDF. 
5. All documents submitted must be clearly labeled with the DARPA RFI number (DARPA-SN-26-
62), respondent organization, and white paper title.
6. To the maximum extent possible, respondents are encouraged to send non-proprietary 
information. 
oRespondents are responsible for clearly identifying proprietary information. Submissions 
containing proprietary information must have the cover page and each page containing 

DARPA-SN-26-62
such information clearly marked with a label such as “Proprietary” or “Company 
Proprietary.” NOTE: “Confidential” is a classification marking used to control the 
dissemination of U.S. Government National Security Information as dictated in Executive 
Order 13526 and should not be used to identify proprietary business information.
7. Do not include elaborate brochures or marketing materials; only include information relevant to 
the areas identified under Requested Information.
8. Use of a diagram(s) or figure(s) to depict the essence of the response is permitted and counted 
towards page count.
9. Send unclassified submissions to DARPA-SN-26-62@darpa.mil. DO NOT SUBMIT 
CLASSIFIED INFORMATION TO THIS ADDRESS. It is not expected that the inclusion of 
higher classification information will be necessary for response to this RFI and submitters are 
specifically discouraged from including such information.
10. Submissions sent through other mediums, channels, or after the prescribed deadline will not be 
considered. Early responses are encouraged.
All white papers shall contain the following sections which are included in the page count:
A. Cover Sheet. Provide the following information:
a. Response Title.
b. Technical point of contact name, organization, telephone number and email address (The 
contact information should include the respondent’s technical and/or administrative 
points of contact (names, addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, and e-mail addresses) 
to enable potential clarification discussions.
c. Indicate the Key Challenge(s) addressed by this response.
d. Indicate classification level of response (e.g., Unclassified, Unclassified/CUI, Secret 
Collateral).
B. Technical Description. Address all  of the technical areas listed under Requested Information as 
stated in this RFI. Graphics within the technical descriptions are encouraged to the extent that 
they aid in succinctly describing the concepts.
C. Graphic Overview Slide. If desired, include a single PowerPoint slide that graphically depicts the 
main ideas of the response. This will not count against the five (5) single-sided written pages. 
D. Bibliography/References. 
All technical and administrative correspondence and questions regarding this announcement and how to 
respond to this RFI should be sent to DARPA-SN-26-62@darpa.mil. E-mails pertaining to this RFI that 
are sent directly to individual DARPA Program Managers will not receive a response. No telephone 
inquiries will be accepted.
NOTE: DARPA may conduct individual discussions with respondents as necessary to gain a full 
understanding of the technical and partnership models submitted. DARPA will contact respondents 
individually via e-mail. 

DARPA-SN-26-62
ELIGIBILITY
DARPA invites white paper submissions from all those engaged in related research activities and 
appreciates responses from all capable and qualified sources, including, but not limited to, universities, 
UARCs, FFRDCs, private or public companies, and U.S. Government research laboratories, large and 
small businesses, and nontraditional defense contractors. 
DISCLAIMERS AND IMPORTANT NOTES:
1. This RFI is NOT a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Program Solicitation (PS), nor a Request for 
Quotations (RFQ).
2. This is an RFI issued solely for market research information and new program planning purposes; 
it does not constitute a formal solicitation for proposals. 
3. Responses received are not offers and will not be accepted by the Government to form a binding 
contract or agreement nor will responses bind DARPA to any  further actions related to this topic, 
including requesting follow-on proposals from respondents to this RFI.  
4. Responding to this RFI  is voluntary and is not required to propose to a subsequent solicitation (if 
any) on this topic.  
5. DARPA will not provide reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to this RFI.  
Respondents are soley responsible for all costs associated with responding to this RFI.
6. Respondents are advised that DARPA is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the 
response, information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any 
information submitted under this RFI.
7. DARPA will disclose submission contents only for the purpose of review. Submissions may be 
reviewed by the Government (DARPA and other Government partners), FFRDCs, and Scientific, 
Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) support contractors bound by appropriate non-
disclosure agreements.
8. All information received in response to this RFI will be treated as confidential business 
information. Responders should properly mark their responses with a label such as “Proprietary” 
or “Company Proprietary”  where applicable. All information received in response to this RFI 
that is marked “Proprietary” or “Company Proprietary” will be handled accordingly.  
9. No questions concerning this RFI and the requirements for future solicitation(s) will be 
considered.  
Point of Contact:
DARPA/TTO
DARPA-SN-26-62@darpa.mil

3. Description of Supplies/Services.  The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) is seeking 
approval to extend mission-essential contractor support for its Emergency 
Management Program. This extension directly supports near-term operations 
such as World Cup 2026, America 250 and Sail 250 as well as sustained 
operations in support of the U.S. border security, facilitation of commerce, and 
response to contingency. The four (4) contract full-time equivalent employees 
are essential for providing continuity of program management, contingency 
response, and expert facilitation and training. 
 
4. Identification of Statutory Exception and Rationale.  
 
The statutory exception is: 
 
GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(ii) Only one source is capable of providing the products, services, or 
solution required at the level of quality required because the products, services, or solutions 
are unique or highly specialized.  
Rationale:  
 Harkcon, Inc. is currently performing these services via Order# 70Z02321FMPE00100, 
and the Contractor’s General Services Administration schedule # 47QRAD20D1158, 
which expires on 04/06/2026.  Additionally, the USCG seeks to continue services on the 
existing requirement to ensure no lapse of services occur.  Hence, a new competitive 
solicitation is anticipated to be released in FY26 to ensure a follow-on procurement is 
awarded by no later than 08/05/2026. 
 
 The contractor possesses unique qualifications and that the nature of the acquisition 
requires a sole-source extension to avoid unacceptable mission degradation and ensure 
continuity of critical government operations. The incumbent contractor personnel hold 
essential Tier 1 and above security clearances, a fundamental and non-negotiable 
requirement for their direct support of classified activities, including continuity of 
operations (COOP) planning and national security war gaming exercises. This level of 
access, combined with their established integration within the U.S. Coast Guard's (USCG) 
Office of Emergency Management and Disaster Response, represents a unique and 
specialized qualification that cannot be readily replicated by a new vendor without 
incurring significant delays for security processing and indoctrination, thus introducing 
unacceptable risk.  
 
Furthermore, the four incumbent full-time equivalent (FTE) contractor employees provide 
mission-essential continuity for program management, expert facilitation, and 
contingency response training. The loss of this institutional knowledge and specialized 
expertise during the period of performance would create a critical capabilities gap. This

to the network, increasing the risk of cybersecurity attacks.  
(2) Proposed sole source contractor.  Due to the bid protest filed by Open San 
Consulting (dba OSC Edge) and GCyber LLC, SAIC is the only responsible 
source at this time that can fulfill this requirement without risk of a substantial 
break in Platform services support to the DISA J6 C4E.   
(3) A sole source extension modification is necessary due to post-award protests filed 
in response to the award of the follow-on BPA, HC102825A0001.  
 
   
5.  COST/PRICE FAIR AND REASONABLE DETERMINATION: During source selection of 
solicitation number 832267288, a cost/price evaluation was conducted in accordance with FAR 
15.404.  The contract prices were determined to be reasonable for the base and all option periods.  
The proposed cost/prices for the extension will be compared to the current TO prices as well as 
the Independent Government Cost Estimate and the proposed prices for the follow-on effort to 
determine fair and reasonableness.    
 
6.  MARKET RESEARCH: This is an extension to the existing TO to ensure continued support 
until the post-award protest and transition period of the follow-on contract, HC102825A0001, 
are complete.  Market research was conducted for the follow-on contract, which was completed 
within the last 12 months.  The market research identified potential sources which enabled the 
follow-on contract to be conducted as a competitive small business set-aside.  
 
7.  ANY OTHER SUPPORTING FACTS: Not Applicable

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) OUTDOOR RECREATION ACCESS 
MANAGEMENT FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF THE AIR FORCE: RECORD KEEPING, 
RECREATION ACCESS, SMALL FORESTRY PRODUCT PERMITS 
 9 Feb 2026 
 
1.0 INTRODUCTION. This is a non-personal services contract to provide access management, permit 
issuance, and record keeping for outdoor recreation and wood product harvesting on military installations 
controlled by the Department of Air Force (DAF). The Government shall not exercise any supervision or 
control over the Contractor performing the services herein. Contractor employees shall be accountable 
solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government.  
1.1 Description of Need. The objective of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to provide 
services to support and manage outdoor recreation access for authorized persons on DAF 
installations. The Sikes Act (16 U.S.C. 670 et seq.) requires military installations to allow access for 
hunting, fishing, trapping and other compatible activities to the maximum extent practicable. 
Additionally, the DAF requires a system to manage public access to installations to harvest firewood 
and other forest products on a fee basis. An Outdoor Recreation Access Management System is how 
the DAF intends to issue and manage permits to individuals for access to installations for the purpose 
of hunting, fishing, trapping, and other dispersed outdoor recreation activities. The Outdoor 
Recreation Access Management System shall also provide for safety and accountability for outdoor 
recreationists on DAF installations and ranges. Record-keeping services required include user 
registration, permit sales, permit printing, customer support, and access records on ingress/egress by 
permit holders on DAF installations.  
2.0 SCOPE. The Contractor shall create, operate, and maintain an DAF Outdoor Recreation Access 
Management System for numerous DAF installations. The Contractor shall provide a system to monitor 
and control access, ensure public safety, and facilitate the collections of permit fees and deposit of fees 
into the DAF collection accounts by interface into the Department of Treasury Pay.gov network. The 
Contractor shall assist authorized users of the Outdoor Recreation Access Management System with the 
following operations: 1) issue hunting/fishing/recreational permits, 2) track recreation user access to 
installations and ranges, 3) issue permits for attaining firewood or other forest products, and 4) 
communicate important announcements regarding rules, open and restricted areas, and safety awareness 
to authorized participants. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, 
transportation, tools, materials, supervision and other items and non-personal services necessary to 
operate the Outdoor Recreation Access Management System and small forest product sales system as 
defined in this PWS. 
2.1 Applicable Installations. The DAF’s current need applies to the following installations: 
1. Altus AFB  
2. Barksdale AFB  
3. Beale AFB  
4. Goodfellow AFB 
5. Grand Forks AFB  
6. JBSA-Camp Bullis 
7. Offutt AFB  
8. Robins AFB 
9.  Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson 

 
2 
 
10. Little Rock AFB 
11. Columbus AFB 
 
2.2 Applicable Policy and Guidance. DAF policy and guidance for outdoor recreation access and 
permit issuance to the public can be found in Department of Air Force Manual (DAFMAN) 32-7003 
– Environmental Conservation. For each military installation, the installation Integrated Natural 
Resources Management Plan (INRMP) identifies the allowable outdoor recreation uses and allowable 
participants, and the activities that may require a permit. Small forest product sales permits guidance 
is also found in DAFMAN 32-7003 and addressed in the installation INRMP.  
2.3 Optional Additional Installations. The DAF can add additional installation(s) in base and/or 
optional years. Each additional installation must include Basic and any additional Premium Services 
(see section 3.2 below) that are required. The request for additional installation(s) and premium 
services is provided to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) for review and cost estimation 
before submitting change request to the Contracting Officer (CO). Once this is approved, then a funds 
request is processed through AFCEC for the service agency.   
3.0 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS. 
3.1 Outdoor Recreation Access Management System Service. The following are key components 
of the required service: 
3.1.1 Content Management Interface (CMI). A CMI needs to be integrated within the web-
based service that allows Installation Administrators and staff (i.e. natural resources managers, 
law enforcement) to control all variables within the Outdoor Recreation Access Management 
System. The management interface will allow authorized personnel differing degrees of access 
based on security groups. This access must be restricted to each individual installation and may 
include but is not limited to: accounts, permit data, survey data, modify/update text on web pages, 
upload maps and reports, apply administrative holds, validate users, create permits with price and 
rules, customer prompts, notifications via email/text, forms, surveys, duplicate entries, reports, 
game harvest information, digital signatures and input fields for Body and Subject on notification 
templates. 
3.1.2 Public Facing Interface. All public users, without having to login, shall be able to access 
each specific installation web page, by computer or mobile device, to view only the specific 
outdoor recreation information, installation permits, and draw/lottery opportunities that are 
automatically populated on the web page from the permit and lottery creation tool within the 
CMI. For example, users wanting to hunt on Grand Forks AFB will go to the Grand Forks AFB 
outdoor recreation web page and only see information and permits available for Grand Forks 
AFB without reference or links for permits/lotteries or information at other installations.  
3.1.2.1 User Account Creation. Users desiring an account will be required to input required 
information to create an account, to include their name, address, phone number, date of birth 
and email before acquiring required permits. A successful account registration email shall be 
sent automatically after user registration. The system shall prevent duplicate accounts by the 
same user. Registered account users shall be able to see all the permits and lotteries available 
without having to login but shall be required to login to add permits to their cart. All users will 
be able to digitally sign and save permits from the website. To accommodate future 
administrative changes and new installation security requirements, the service must have the 
ability to force registered users to update their profile information before the user can execute a 

 
3 
 
new transaction. All pages that users enter information in/on will be protected by a secure 
socket layer. 
3.1.2.2 User Transaction Capability. Users shall be able to purchase single or multiple 
permits/licenses/products for themselves and other users in one transaction. All users shall be 
allowed to purchase multiple permits or draw/lottery applications within one session and will 
be able to add/purchase permits or draw/lottery applications for other user parties (e.g. group 
hunts) during the single session transaction. Administrators shall have the ability to limit 
product access based upon the category of user, such as permits issued only to youth, disabled 
persons or active-duty military only. Returning users shall have the ability to copy, clone or 
duplicate a prior permit as input into a new permit. For example, the user may create a current 
year annual permit by duplicating last year’s annual permit. Users shall also have the capability 
to select online help hyperlinks for assistance with making a payment. 
3.1.2.3 Ability to Create a Permit Voucher. For installations that require validation of the 
eligibility of a user to participate in activities on the installation, the Outdoor Recreation Access 
Management System shall have the capability for the user to create a voucher in lieu of permit 
issuance. For this capability, a user will enter all the information required for the permit they 
seek and be able to display and print that information labeled as a permit voucher to be 
presented to the Installation Administrator for validation. Upon validation of user authorization, 
the Installation Administrator shall be able to activate the voucher as a valid permit for the user. 
3.1.3 Area Scheduling. The user interface shall provide the areas available to public users for 
outdoor recreation activities and the access restrictions applicable to those areas. This service is to 
be available without the use of interactive mapping; the scheduling function will allow narrative 
description of the area or reference to electronic images of maps uploaded and maintained by 
Installation Administrators, as directed by the COR. 
3.1.4 Permit Issuance Service. Permits shall be made available for public end-users with or 
without an account. A login account does not have to be required for permit purchase. The CMI 
will allow installation staff to create any number of permits for either a fee or for free through 
various methods i.e. first come, first serve sale, lottery drawing, limited quota sale, annual permit 
sales. The permit service shall allow an individual (account user or non-account user) to buy 
multiple permits under a single transaction, to include account users or non-account users. Users 
shall be able to email the permit themselves and/or download the permit. The information 
collected on permits shall be reported at the back end for authorized Installation Administrators to 
view and export. The Installation Administrators will supply the Contractor with a permit 
template for incorporation into the web-based system and for printing. All non-account public 
users shall be able to retrieve all active permits and lottery tickets anytime by the specific 
installation they purchased their permit or lottery ticket. 
3.1.5 Permit Payment Service. The Contractor shall provide a payment acceptance service for 
permit purchases. The Contractor shall provide all components and services necessary to allow 
credit card purchases of permits through the website. This service shall have the following 
features and capabilities: 
3.1.5.1 Secure and encrypted communications, 
3.1.5.2 Ability to accept all major credit card and debit cards as payment, 

 
4 
 
3.1.5.3 Ability to interface with and forward user to the Department of Treasury Pay.gov portal 
for payment of user fees into the appropriate Pay.gov accounts, 
3.1.5.4 Ability to split payments in one transaction such that outdoor recreation fees and forest 
product fees can be directed to different Pay.gov accounts, 
3.1.5.5 Ability to send an email receipt to permit purchasers along with the permit. 
3.1.6. Customer Support and Help Desk Service. The Contractor shall maintain a list of 
primary points of contact for interface with each installation.  The Contractor shall provide the 
designated installation points of contact on the website, for customers to acquire technical 
assistance and ask questions by telephone and/or email (i.e. Help Desk Service). Customers shall 
be able to leave messages if support is not immediately available and receive assistance within 
two work weekdays (Monday thru Friday). 
3.1.7 Regulatory, Safety, and Proficiency Controls. The Outdoor Recreation Access 
Management System web interface shall allow for posting additional criteria concerning 
installation regulations, safety information, and special controls applicable to permits. These 
controls shall be integrated into the permit application process and automatically approved at the 
time of purchase. For example, to obtain a Robins AFB fishing permit, a Georgia fishing license 
number must be provided before transaction is authorized. Other controls shall establish a 
notification system to the Installation Administrator and require approval by the administrator 
before the transaction is authorized. For example: Grand Forks AFB requires an archery 
proficiency test prior to issuing bow hunting permits; as such, the Installation Administrator 
would confirm that the applicant has passed the proficiency test before a permit is issued. 
3.1.8 Administrative Back-end Interface. Based on the varying degrees of administrative 
privileges (read/write), the service shall allow access for multiple and simultaneous Installation 
Administrators. Each designated Installation Administrator shall only be granted access to their 
own installation information, customers, transactions, lotteries and permits and shall not see other 
installation customers or information unless another installation manager gives that user 
administrative back-end permission. With “write” administrative privileges, an Installation 
Administrator shall grant other Installation Administrators the ability to create permits with 
diverse procedures, create lotteries with numerous parameters, modify/update web pages in real-
time, provide customer service for users needing changes made to information (email, address, 
phone number) and query real-time data for viewing. If the Installation Administrator needs to 
change the type of permit held by a customer, the administrator shall have the ability to clear an 
individual permit from the system and generate a new permit. Some DAF administrators will only 
require read-only administrative privileges to view transactions. Persons with “read” 
administrative privileges shall only be able to query and view real-time data. 
3.1.9 Installation Administrator Training. The Contractor shall provide a minimum of six 
hours of training support to the designated Installation Administrator in the use of the Outdoor 
Recreation Access Management System at each participating installation within the first year of 
operation. The Contractor shall make training available to each participating installation with 
documentation explaining the use and functions of the Outdoor Recreation Access Management 
System. 
3.1.10 Ability of Authorized Permit Holders to Sponsor Others.  The Outdoor Recreation 
Access Management System shall allow for a permit to be issued that lists the names of persons 

 
5 
 
to be sponsored by an authorized permit holder. At some installations, as directed by the COR, 
the Government may limit access for outdoor recreation activities to certain categories of

Justification for Single Source Awards IAW FAR 13.106-1 
For 
Over Micro-Purchase Threshold but Not Exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold 
 
 
Acquisition Plan Action ID:  36C261-26-AP-2878 – BD CATO Subscription & IV Prep Support 
 
 
1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration,Regional 
Procurement Office West, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 21, for the VeteransIntegrated Service 
Network (VISN) 21, VA Central California Health Care System (VACCHCS), 2615 E Clinton Ave, Fresno, 
CA 93703-2223. 
 
JOFOC: NCO 21- 932 
2237: 570-26-3-555-0108 
 
2. Brief Description of Supplies/ Services required and the intended use/Estimated Amount: The VA 
Central California Health Care System, Fresno, requires a service contract that provides preventive 
maintenance, corrective maintenance, parts replacement, software support, and server support for 
its BD IV Prep solution. These services ensure that the IV Prep system— and its integrated 
components such as the BD CATO software and IV Prep Gravimetric Pack— remain fully operational, 
compliant with manufacturer specifications, and capable of supporting sterile compounding 
workflows essential to safe medication preparation. Continued functionality of this system is 
required to maintain gravimetric accuracy, safeguard medication preparation processes, and ensure 
uninterrupted pharmacy operations. The estimated amount for the required services is  
One (1)  Year subscription - $95,436.00 (CATO $89,136 + IV Prep $6,300) 
3. Unique characteristics that limit availability to only one source, with the reason no other supplies 
or services can be used: CareFusion Solutions, LLC— a subsidiary of Becton Dickinson (BD)— is the 
sole manufacturer, service provider, and authorized maintenance entity for the BD Pyxis IV Prep 
system and its associated software, including BD CATO. The company does not authorize or certify 
any third‑party vendors to perform installation, service, support, or maintenance on these systems. 
Because BD retains exclusive control of all proprietary components, software code, updates, 
patches, and service tools, no external vendor possesses the technical data, permissions, or OEM 
authorization required to maintain or repair the IV Prep platform. Any maintenance or service 
performed by a non‑BD technician would immediately void the system’s warranty and would not be 
supported by CareFusion Solutions, LLC. As a result, only the manufacturer is able to provide the 
comprehensive maintenance, parts, software support, and system expertise required to keep the BD 
IV Prep solution operational and compliant with safety and performance standards, making 
CareFusion Solutions, LLC the only viable source for these services. 
 
 

 
Revision: 02 
Effective Date: 12/30/2025 Page 2 of 2 
Acquisition ID# 36C261-26-AP-2878 
4. Description of market research conducted and results or statement why it was not conducted: 
Market research for this requirement was completed under Market Research Acquisition ID 
36C261-25-AP-3414, dated June 2, 2025, and included a review of VetCert, SAM.gov, GSA 
Advantage, and FPDS to determine whether any vendors other than the OEM could provide 
authorized support for the BD Pyxis IV Prep system. Although numerous vendors were listed under 
NAICS 541519, none were identified as authorized or certified to service, maintain, or support BD 
Pyxis systems. FPDS records confirmed that similar requirements— such as Contract 
36C26123P0241— were previously procured directly from CareFusion Solutions, LLC, validating that 
the OEM has historically been the sole capable source for these services. To further verify market 
availability, the Government contacted BD directly, and the OEM confirmed that no third-party 
vendors are permitted or certified to provide installation, maintenance, or software support for BD 
Pyxis IV Prep or its associated components. Based on these findings, the market research concluded 
that CareFusion Solutions, LLC remains the only source able to meet the technical, proprietary, and 
support requirements of this procurement. 
  
5. Contracting Officer's Certification: Purchase is approved in accordance with FAR13.106-1(b). I 
certify that the foregoing justification is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge and 
belief.

Edward Hunter Date

NOTICE DATES: April 16, 2026 – July 31, 2026
TOPIC AREA: Strategic Systems
1.0 PURPOSE
Between the dates listed above, the DARPA NGMM program1 will be actively reviewing the ERIS Marketplace for 
innovative, post-competitive, awardable solutions that exercise the early-stage version of the NGMM 3D Assembly 
Design Kit (3D-ADK) for mixed-material 3D-heterogeneously integrated (3DHI) microsystem design with 
commercial Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. This is an active and immediate search for solutions. 
Submissions will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the Government reserves the right to make one or more awards 
prior to the closing date of this notice.
2.0 PROBLEM & SCOPE
The NGMM program is developing new EDA capabilities, and the first comprehensive multi-physics enabled 3D-
ADK, for the design of advanced mixed-material 3DHI microsystems. Enabling efficient EDA workflows, built 
around a robust 3D-ADK, is essential to the NGMM program and the sustainability of the resultant high-mix/low-
volume pure-play advanced packaging capability. DARPA is interested in awardable solutions to exercise and 
evaluate the early-stage release of the 3D-ADK and EDA workflow.
Current Obstacle: For 3DHI designs, existing EDA tools and ADK infrastructure are insufficient to achieve 
architectural exploration studies where system level trades and performance can be quickly simulated with 
relative precision and detailed design capabilities where co-design activities with concurrent analysis and 
optimization can be employed for full assembly sign-off.
Desired Research Focus: We are seeking solutions, informed by a relevant 3DHI design aligned with the 
NGMM technology roadmap 2,3 and that will comprehensively exercise the NGMM 3D-ADK and EDA 
capabilities, to support architectural trade studies and verify design functionality and performance to the 
sign-off phase. Figure 1 shows the planned offerings on the technology roadmap for the NGMM center. As 
the goal of the effort is to validate the NGMM design infrastructure, proposed solutions should align to the 
NGMM 3D-ADK as much as is practical.
1 Holmes, M., et al., “The Defense Advanced Research Agency’s (DARPA) Next Generation Microelectronics Manufacturing 
(NGMM) Program,” International Conference on Compound Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology, New Orleans, May 21, 
2025.
2 “MTO Spark Tank,” YouTube, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FNPwnqWJd6c, July 2025.
3 “NGMM Summit,” Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, https://www.darpa.mil/events/rewinds/ngmm-
summit/presentations, October 2025.

Figure 1: NGMM offerings to enable design and manufacturing of 3DHI microsystems. Supported materials 
include Si, glass, GaN, InP, GaAs, SiC, and yttrium iron garnet.
3.0 DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND EXPERTISE
While all submissions will be evaluated against the standard criteria published in the ERIS Master Solicitation, 
the DARPA NGMM program is specifically looking for solutions that demonstrate strength in the following areas. 
These are not new evaluation criteria but rather highlight the specific attributes of interest for this opportunity.
Advancing the State of the Art (Technical Innovation):
Proposed solutions should reflect a next-generation, innovative 3DHI design that provides substantial 
performance benefits over conventional 2D designs composed of a single material. The 3DHI design is 
expected to have two or three layers of components vertically integrated using the planned NGMM center 
offerings shown in Figure 1. The most compelling solutions will be those that align with the NGMM 
integration capabilities, 3D-ADK, offering innovative methods to enable the comprehensive evaluation 
and validation of design flows and models.
Team Capability (Expertise and Vision):
We are seeking teams with significant expertise in mixed-signal, mixed-materials design with modern, 
multi-physics EDA tools. Teams should have a proven track record of designing microelectronics 
utilizing compound semiconductors and silicon, as well as working with multiple foundries and multiple 
design kits to develop advanced microsystems. Additionally, experience with 3DHI or mixed-materials 
2.5D integration is strongly preferred. 
Defining the Problem & Current State of the Art:
Strong submissions will demonstrate a deep understanding of the problem space, in which existing EDA 
and ADK infrastructure have limited support for comprehensive 3DHI device simulation and verification 
on a reasonable timescale. Proposers should clearly define the scope of the technical challenge their 3DHI 
design addresses and compare their proposed solution to the current state of the art.

Impact (Defense and Commercial Use Case):
Submissions should discuss how the proposed solution will demonstrate the significant performance 
advantages of 3DHI microsystems and improve the robustness and effectiveness of the NGMM 3D-ADK 
and EDA workflows through a candidate design flow aligned with directly relevant Department of War 
and/or dual use applications.
4.0 HOW TO RESPOND
This notice is a call for solutions to be flagged for review. 
For Existing Awardable Solutions:
If you have a solution already in the ERIS Marketplace that aligns with this need, send an email 
to ERIS@darpa.mil with:
Subject Line: Shopping Notice Response: DARPA-SN-26-69 - [Your Company Name]
Body: The Title and Video URL of your existing awardable solution.
For New Submissions:
If you have a new solution, please submit it to the 'Strategic Systems' Topic Area via the ERIS portal. The full 
description for that topic area is: 
Developing advanced technologies for improved resilience, efficiency, and effectiveness of 
strategic systems. This topic area supports technologies for critical infrastructure and military 
command-and-control systems (networks and applications across strategic, command, 
operational, and tactical edges).
To ensure it is associated with this notice, please use the following format for your video title:
Video Title Format: DARPA-SN-26-69: [Your Solution Title]
(Example: DARPA-SN-26-69: AI Accelerator Analysis Tool)
After submitting, please also send a notification email to ERIS@darpa.mil with:
Subject Line: Shopping Notice Response: DARPA-SN-26-69 - [Your Company Name]
Body: The Title of your new submission and its Date of Submission.
Solutions submitted during this window that are deemed "awardable" through the standard ERIS assessment process 
will be included for consideration by NGMM.
5.0 RESOURCES
ERIS Master Solicitation: SAM.gov Link
To Submit a New Solution: DARPAConnect ERIS Portal

Intro 
 
 
Welcome to Wide Area Workflow e-Business Suite. This demonstration contains audio narrative. Please adjust your volume 
accordingly. 
Step 1 
 
 
This is an overview of posting an offer for a solicitation to the Solicitation Portal. Proposal Manager logs in to PIEE to access, 
the Solicitation application. The Proposal Manager must be logged in to submit an offer. 
 

Posting Offer Page 2 of 8 
 
Built with Tanida Demo Builder 
www.demo-builder.com  
 
Step 2 
 
 
Select the Solicitation icon. 
Step 3 
 
 
The Home screen of the Solicitation Portal displays. The Proposal Manager selects the Search link to find the Solicitation they 
intend to post an offer against. 
 

Posting Offer Page 3 of 8 
 
Built with Tanida Demo Builder 
www.demo-builder.com  
 
Step 4 
 
 
Proposal Manager enters search criteria to find the solicitation they want to submit an offer against and then selects Search. 
The Solicitation Search Criteria are as follows: 
• Solicitation Number - Enter the complete solicitation number 
• Open Date - Enter a start and end date to find solicitations that were posted to the site within the range 
• Response Date - Enter a start and end date to find solicitations where the Response Due Date is within the range 
• Product or Service Code - Enter the Product or Service codes as a comma-delimited list, or use the lookup feature to populate 
one or more codes 
• NAICS - Enter the NAICS codes as a comma-delimited list, or use the lookup feature to populate one or more codes 
• Set Aside Code - Select a set Aside code to find solicitations that are set aside 
• Place of Performance Zip Code - Enter the Zip Code of the Place of Performance 
• Contracting Office DoDAAC - Enter a DoDAAC to find Solicitations that were issued by that Contracting Office 
• Status - Select a status of Open, Closed or Both 
Step 5 
 
 
On the search page filtering Solicitations with an Open status then click the Search button to view all open Solicitations. 
 

Posting Offer Page 4 of 8 
 
Built with Tanida Demo Builder 
www.demo-builder.com  
 
Step 6 
 
 
The search results display. Select the Solicitation Number link to open the solicitation 
Step 7 
 
 
The solicitation displays. The information is view only.  
 

Posting Offer Page 5 of 8 
 
Built with Tanida Demo Builder 
www.demo-builder.com  
 
Step 8 
 
 
Scroll down to see the Contract Information and Attachments. The Attachments can be viewed by selecting the File link. Scroll 
back up to the top of the screen and click the Offer tab. 
Step 9 
 
 
Click the Offer tab to Add and review current offers on the Solicitation. Click the Add button to add an offer to the Solicitation. 
 

Posting Offer Page 6 of 8 
 
Built with Tanida Demo Builder 
www.demo-builder.com  
 
Step 10 
 
 
Proposal Manager selects the applicable CAGE Code for which they are submitting the offer. The list is prefiltered based on the 
CAGEs in the Proposal Manager’s profile.  
Step 11 
 
 
Proposal Manager uploads the attachments that comprise their offer by selecting the Choose Files link.  
 

Posting Offer Page 7 of 8 
 
Built with Tanida Demo Builder 
www.demo-builder.com  
 
Step 12 
 
 
 After entering all necessary information enter a Signature Date and Click the Signature button.  
Step 13 
 
 
The Sign Document pop-up will be displayed requiring the user to enter a Digital Pin and OTP. Click the Sign and Submit button 
to continue. 
 

Posting Offer Page 8 of 8 
 
Built with Tanida Demo Builder 
www.demo-builder.com  
 
Step 14 
 
 
After successfully adding the Offer a success message of the submission will be displayed and the offer displayed collapsed. 
Users may expand and view all offers on a Solicitation. 
End 
 
 
This concludes our demonstration.

4. IDENTIFICATION OF THE AUTHORITY AND CIRCUMSTANCE THAT JUSTIFIES LIMITING THE SOURCE. 
FAR 8.405-6(a)(1)(i)(C) -- In the interest of economy and efficiency, the new work is a logical follow-on to 
an original Federal Supply Schedule order that was not previously issued under limited-sources 
procedures. 
5. DESCRIPTION OF THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY S NEEDS. 
AWP is a General Services Administration (GSA) Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) order, awarded 
competitively on 30 September 2020. The task order was awarded as a Firm Fixed Price contract with a 
base year, four option years through 29 September 2025. The current order is extended by 6 months 
utilizing 52.217-8 Option to Extend Services, which expires on 29 March 2026.  Contractor shall assume 
Applications Service Provider (ASP) responsibilities for the Agile AWP products. The Contractor shall 
provide Operations & Maintenance (O&M) and software/website development services to support and 
sustain the AWP products (as referenced in Table 1.1) across multiple security domains. Operations shall 
include support activities and execution of tasks that enable AWP II to achieve performance and service 
levels in an efficient and cost-effective manner. The Contractor shall prepare and deliver software, 
source code, and documentation (per CDRL A019: Software Product Specification) for each baseline 
update or release. The Software Product Specification (SPS) shall include executable software, source 
files, and software support information/documentation. The Government Program Management Office 
(PMO) anticipates the need for software development to address emerging requirements but cannot 
specify details at this time. 
 
The Discovery Catalog has been incorporated into the Globe baseline, and will still require updates to 
content, useability and UI/UX enhancements.  The Contractor will provide content management support 
for Discovery Catalog that includes review of new content requests and maintenance of existing 
content.  On the Secret and TS domains Globe Lite has been incorporated into the Globe baseline and 
has replaced mGlobe as 
search. 
 
This justification is a result of addressing critical tasking required to meet national security requirements 
in support of the war fighter and meet ongoing mandatory security requirements. The maintenance 
activities found under these services include corrective, adaptive and perfective. Under corrective 
maintenance, this will identify, isolate, and rectify a fault or problem to restore a system or application 
to an operation state. In addition, this will provide further development support to fix identified defects, 
which falls under corrective maintenance. The adaptive maintenance provides modifications to keep a 
system or application usable in a changed or changing environment. The perfective maintenance 
delivers a modification to improve system or application performance or maintainability. Under adaptive 
and perfective maintenance, these funds will also be used for crisis support (such as Israel-Gaza and 
Ukraine-Russia).

Statement of Work 

Five & six year Fire Extinguisher Maintenance

Southeast Louisiana Veterans Healthcare System (SLVHCS)

2400 Canal St, New Orleans, LA 70119

Purpose

The Department of Veterans Affairs facility located at 2400 Canal Street, New Orleans, LA 70119 currently requires a new contract for the 5/6-year preventive maintenance of fire extinguishers to ensure safety and adherence to regulatory standards. Several fire extinguishers within the facility are due for their mandatory 5/6-year maintenance, as required by NFPA 10 regulations. This preventive maintenance is crucial for maintaining the operational efficiency and compliance of fire safety equipment.

Scope

Existing preventive maintenance services for fire extinguishers are either expired or insufficient to meet current NFPA 10 standards, which require regular inspection, testing, and maintenance of fire extinguishers, including specific 5/6-year maintenance intervals. Without a proper maintenance contract, fire extinguishers may become non-functional, posing significant fire hazards and non-compliance risks.

Assessment:

Current Need: The Department of Veterans Affairs facility at 2400 Canal Street, New Orleans, LA 70119 urgently requires a comprehensive maintenance contract for fire extinguishers due for their 5/6-year maintenance to ensure adherence to NFPA 10 standards. This contract should include comprehensive services such as inspection, testing, hydrostatic testing, recharging, and replacement of defective components, ensuring that all fire extinguishers are always in optimal working condition. Securing this contract is crucial for maintaining a safe and secure workplace environment.

Maintenance/Services:

5lbs ABC fire extinguisher 6-year maintenance recharge including parts (5) each

10lbs ABC fire extinguisher 6-year maintenance recharge including parts (75) each

5 lb CO2 fire extinguisher (hydrotest) (20) each
