SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE
Information Technology Support Services (ITSS)
Executive Secretariat (S/ES) – ExecTech
U.S. Department of State

This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) as outlined in FAR 15.201(d).  The purpose of this notice is to accomplish market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, and to identify qualified and experienced HubZone, WOSB or SDVOSB businesses capable of and interested in providing the services described herein.  The purpose of this notice is to identify qualified and experienced vendors capable of providing Information Technology Support Services (ITSS) for the U.S. Department of State, Executive Secretariat (S/ES), ExecTech Office.

This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Request for Proposal (RFP). Additionally, there is no obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described within this notice now or in the future. The Government does not intend to award any contract(s) based solely on the submission of this notice. Respondents are advised that the Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this notice, nor will it compensate respondents for any costs incurred in the development/furnishing of a response. The Government will not entertain telephone calls or questions for this notice.  Please note that a decision not to submit a response will not preclude a vendor from participating in any future solicitation.

Information Technology Support Services are currently being provided by Improvix Technologies Inc, under Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) 19AQMM19A0208.  The remaining 2 active task orders are due to expire May 15, 2026.  The Government intends to compete the Department of State Information Technologies Support Services (ITSS) BPA under either HubZone, WOSB or SDVOSB socioeconomic factor based on the results of this SSN.  The intent is to award a single BPA, with ceiling between $100Mil to $150Mil for a period of five (5) years (a one-year base period and four (4) one-year options).

1. BACKGROUND
The Executive Secretariat (S/ES) serves as the Secretary of State’s principal mechanism for policy coordination, crisis management, and authoritative communication across the Department of State and the interagency community. Within S/ES, ExecTech provides mission-critical, executive-level IT services supporting senior leadership.

ExecTech operates a 24x7x365 environment across classified and unclassified systems, delivering white-glove IT services that support global travel, crisis response, and continuity-of-government operations.

The majority of ExecTech’s ITSS services include:

ExecTech primarily focuses on enabling executive leadership decision-making and mission execution through secure, reliable, and always-available information technology services. These services support both foreign policy and administrative operations in a high-tempo, global environment, ensuring the Secretary of State, Department Principals, and Executive Secretariat leadership can operate without interruption. ExecTech emphasizes responsiveness, discretion, and operational resilience to support crisis response, international travel, continuity-of-government operations, and senior-level engagements.

 ExecTech is committed to building, operating, and sustaining a robust, secure IT infrastructure across classified and unclassified environments. This infrastructure enables executive communications, collaboration, mobility, and secure information flow across multiple locations and enclaves. In addition, ExecTech provides dedicated, on-site deskside support to ensure real-time, hands-on assistance for executive users and mission-critical staff support that cannot be performed remotely due to security, system integration, and operational requirements. ExecTech also prioritizes strengthening the technical readiness of its supported workforce through standardized onboarding, executive user training, documentation, and just-in-time, in-person support tailored to senior leaders and high-tempo operations.

A core element of ExecTech’s mission involves integrating security, risk management, and compliance into all technology services. ExecTech achieves this by embedding cybersecurity, privacy, and secure-by-design principles into system engineering, service delivery, and operations. ExecTech works closely with Department stakeholders to ensure compliance with federal and Department IT, cybersecurity, records management, and accessibility requirements, while continuously modernizing systems to reduce risk and technical debt.

Additionally, ExecTech oversees and supports enterprise IT governance, portfolio planning, and mission operations for S/ES. This includes aligning IT investments with mission priorities, supporting executive governance forums, managing vendor performance, and enabling Congressional, litigation, and records-management support. ExecTech collaborates across bureaus to ensure a cohesive, accountable, and mission-aligned approach to executive IT services.

ExecTech ITSS Functional Areas

ExecTech ITSS services are organized across the following functional areas:

Front Office Operations
Provides executive-level administrative, programmatic, and operational IT support, including governance coordination, resource planning, staffing transitions, executive reporting, and continuity of operations.

Executive Support Services
Delivers white-glove customer support, executive communications, mobile and flyaway kit support, VTC services, account and asset lifecycle management, and direct engagement with senior leaders across all environments.

Service Delivery & Engineering
Designs, integrates, secures, and operates networks, infrastructure, applications, automation, and digital platforms, using Agile and modern engineering practices to support mission execution and system reliability.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Mission Operations
Ensures continuous authorization, cybersecurity risk management, compliance, IT governance, financial oversight, records and knowledge management, Congressional and litigation support, and overall operational integrity.

2. SCOPE / REQUIRED CAPABILITIES

As ExecTech’s mission, technology footprint, and operational tempo have expanded in scope, complexity, visibility, and criticality, the Executive Secretariat (S/ES) requires industry partners capable of delivering enterprise-scale, mission-critical Information Technology Support Services (ITSS). The operating environment demands secure, resilient, and highly responsive IT services that support executive leadership, crisis response, global travel, continuity-of-government operations, and sustained operations across both classified and unclassified environments.

To meet these requirements, ExecTech seeks vendors with demonstrated experience providing integrated advisory, engineering, operational, cybersecurity, and governance capabilities, including but not limited to the following:

Ad Hoc Advisory & Executive IT Advisory Services

Experience providing on-demand advisory support to senior executive IT leadership within a federal environment, including advising on operational, technical, and governance challenges unique to executive-level IT support.

Demonstrated understanding of federal budget cycles, acquisition processes, security clearance requirements, and inter-bureau coordination mechanisms impacting IT services.

Experience advising on IT service delivery models, executive support frameworks, and operational IT strategies aligned with federal policies, Department of State standards, and enterprise architecture.

Special Projects & Surge Operations

Experience executing special projects and surge operations requiring familiarity with the Department of State operational environment, including diplomatic security requirements, executive travel support, classified communications, and crisis response.

Ability to rapidly scale staffing, technical capabilities, and operational support to meet time-sensitive, high-visibility mission demands.

Quality Control, Performance Management & Continuous Improvement

Experience developing and implementing quality control and performance management processes for IT services supporting executive or mission-critical operations.

Ability to define, track, and report service performance metrics, customer satisfaction indicators, and operational risk measures.

Experience supporting inspection readiness, audits, and continuous service-improvement initiatives.

Customer Engagement, Communications & Training Support

Experience delivering customer-focused communications supporting executive IT services, including service updates, briefings, dashboards, and executive-level reporting.

Ability to develop and maintain user documentation, job aids, and training materials tailored to senior leaders and mission-critical staff.

Experience applying UI/UX-informed approaches to improve usability, accessibility, and adoption of executive-facing digital tools and platforms.

Enterprise Systems Administration & Directory Services

Demonstrated experience managing Active Directory (AD) architectures, including user and group management, organizational units (OUs), domain controllers, forests, and trust relationships.

Experience administering Windows and Linux server environments, including system hardening, patching, performance monitoring, and lifecycle management.

Familiarity with storage virtualization technologies and integration with platforms such as VMware and Hyper-V.

Network Engineering & Infrastructure Operations

Strong understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and the ability to troubleshoot complex network issues across distributed environments.

Experience configuring and managing network security controls, including firewalls, routing, segmentation, and access controls.

Ability to design, operate, and secure network infrastructure supporting both classified and unclassified systems.

Security Engineering, Backup & Data Protection

Experience implementing security controls to protect systems, data, and communications, including firewall management and data-protection mechanisms.

Demonstrated capability designing and implementing backup, archiving, and recovery strategies, including routine recovery testing to ensure operational resilience.

Proficiency with SAN, NAS, and DAS storage solutions, including performance optimization and capacity planning.

Automation, Scripting & Configuration Management

Experience using scripting languages (e.g., PowerShell) to automate administrative, operational, and compliance-related tasks.

Familiarity with configuration management and automation tools to improve consistency, reduce manual effort, and enhance system reliability.

Cloud Engineering & DevOps

Demonstrated experience deploying and managing cloud resources and services within major cloud service providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, Google Cloud).

Experience with CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) solutions (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation).

Understanding of cloud networking concepts, including virtual networks/VPCs, subnets, routing, and security groups.

Capability to monitor cloud performance, optimize resource utilization, and manage operational costs in accordance with federal and Department policies.

Mission-Critical Application & Platform Support

Experience supporting and maintaining mission-critical applications, including monitoring system uptime, performance, and responsiveness.

Familiarity with Department-specific systems such as SPB/ Cascades, Microsoft Power Apps, and other apps including applying security patches, performing system health checks, and implementing data backup and recovery procedures to protect sensitive information.

Video Teleconferencing (VTC) & Executive Communications

Demonstrated experience supporting enterprise and executive-level Video Teleconferencing (VTC), including managing multiple bridge types, classified and unclassified sessions, and high-visibility executive engagements at TS Level.

Ability to provide just-in-time, on-demand VTC support for senior leadership, including troubleshooting and cross-stakeholder coordination.

Cybersecurity, Risk Management & Compliance

Demonstrated capability supporting cybersecurity risk management, continuous authorization, and incident response in accordance with FISMA, NIST, FedRAMP, and Department of State policies.

Ability to demonstrate compliance with 19 FAM 101.1-3(A) (Primary Cyber Laws, Regulations, and Executive Orders), including reporting through mechanisms such as the ECISO Cybersecurity Scorecard.

Experience addressing and remediating findings identified by the Bureau of Diplomatic Security’s Cyber Threat Analysis Division (DS/CS/CTA), including remediation of vulnerabilities identified during FISMA High-Value Asset (HVA) assessments.

Demonstrated organizational experience conducting Assessment and Authorization (A&A) activities in accordance with NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5, including experience supporting Department systems using tools such as Archangel.

Ability to support continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, audit readiness, and inspection activities across multiple systems and environments.

General Scope Requirements

Vendors responding to this Sources Sought Notice should demonstrate the ability to:

Strategically manage complex IT infrastructure, systems, and security operations within the federal government’s regulatory and operational framework, including classified and sensitive but unclassified environments.

Provide integrated engineering, operations, automation, cybersecurity, and advisory support aligned with executive-level mission requirements.

Support high-availability, high-visibility systems with minimal tolerance for downtime or service degradation.

Oversee intake, prioritization, lifecycle management, financial tracking, and performance reporting for IT services and initiatives.

Develop, implement, and maintain quality control, compliance, and continuous-improvement processes aligned with Department-specific requirements.

Deliver technically strong solutions while maintaining a customer-focused, service-oriented approach appropriate for executive and mission-critical environments.

3. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

This requirement requires access to classified information.   Therefore, the interested offerors, including all entities which comprise a joint venture must possess a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) active Top-Secret Facility Clearance Level (FCL) and all personnel shall maintain up to Top-Secret clearances, depending on the role as outlined in the Labor Categories. Uncleared individuals specifically authorized by the COR may perform on-site in DOS facilities, only on unclassified portions

B.2  STATEMENT OF WORK 
 
Background: 
The North Florida/South Georgia Veterans Health System has a requirement to bi-annually 
measure and verify the required air changes and differential air pressure of numerous rooms 
(i.e., Operating Rooms, isolation rooms (aka Negative Pressure Rooms), sterile supply storage, 
sterile supply processing, Re-usable Medical Equipment (RME) cleaning and storage rooms) 
and document compliance with JAHCO, Infection Control and CDC procedures and directives. 
 
Objective:  
A qualified contractor must be brought in to: Perform bi-annual air change measurements and 
calculations to determine the number of air changes per hour and differential pressure 
relationships with adjacent spaces for negative pressure or positive pressure rooms and provide 
a report in spreadsheet format (CSV file). 
 
Scope of Work: 
• Coordinate all work with the Contracting Officers Representative (COR) 
• Measure all rooms to determine volume (LxWxH) in cubic feet 
• Measure supply air volume – in Cubic Feet per Minute (CFM) 
• Measure return air or exhaust air volume – CFM 
• Calculate air changes per hour 
• Determine if room is positive (+0.01In. W.C. minimum) or negative (-0.01In. W.C. 
minimum) 
• Number of rooms: 
o Malcolm Randall VAMC - 210 
o Gainesville Dermatology Clinic - 2 
o Gainesville Pain Clinic - 2 
o Lake City VAMC - 50 
o The Villages OPC - 20 
o Tallahassee OPC - 25 
o Jacksonville OPC – 45 
• Deliverables: provide a report in spreadsheet (CSV file) format showing: location, room 
number, use/type, measurements, calculations, required number of air changes, 
pressure relationships and pass/fail air changes and differential pressure.    
 
Qualifications/Certifications 
• The contractor shall have a valid NEBB Professional Certification. 
• The contractor must be qualified and have the required levels of professional and 
technical experience to perform the work required by this statement of work. 
• Equipment utilized must be calibrated with NIST traceable certificates. 
 
 
Safety Regulations 
• All OSHA safety regulations shall be observed during the project. 
• The VA Safety Officer shall have full authority to see that the contractor obeys all safety 
rules and regulations relative to the fulfillment of this project. 
• Provide the necessary barricades/signage where required. 
 
Scheduling and Hours of Work 
• All work in areas involved shall be scheduled with the COR. 
• Work in Operating Rooms will have to be done after all cases are complete 1700 – 2200 
or on the weekends when not in use. 

36C24826Q0146

• Work in isolation rooms will have to be completed when they are not in use – on first 
shift, Monday thru Friday, 0800 – 1600. 
• Storage rooms - on first shift, Monday thru Friday, 0800 – 1600 
• Sterile Processing spaces – 0700-1000 Monday thru Friday or on the weekends.

Strategic systems programs (SSP) office manager (OM) and senior executive service (SES) executive assistant (EA) support services fy27-fy31

1.0	Product Service Code (PSC)  

The applicable Product Service Code (PSC) is R499 SUPPORT- PROFESSIONAL: OTHER.

2.0	North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code	

The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541611 – Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services.  

3.0	Contracting Office Address

Strategic Systems Programs (SSP)

1250 10th Street, Suite 4600

Washington DC 20374

4.0	Synopsis

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (SSN) announcement.  SSNs are issued to assist the Agency in performing market research to determine industry interest and capability.  No proposals are being requested or accepted with this synopsis.  THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. Therefore, no proposals are being requested or accepted in response to this SSN. 

5.0	Purpose

In accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, SSP is conducting market research to determine if sources are capable of successfully performing the requirements identified in this SSN. Specifically, SSP is seeking capable firms to provide comprehensive support services in office management and services in executive assistance to SSP Senior

Executive Service Leadership. 

The contract type will include Firm Fixed Price, Term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINS).  The Period of Performance (POP) will include a base year FY27 effort from 18 March 2027 – 17 March 2028, and four (4) corresponding one-year option periods. 

NOTE: Given the highly technical nature of SSP’s mission set as a major weapons systems command and corresponding technical requirements, respondents must provide recent and relevant past performance data (as detailed below) to demonstrate and substantiate the respondent’s ability to successfully execute requirements detailed in this SSN. 

6.0	White Paper Capability Statement Credentials

a.  SSP is seeking detailed, complete, and thorough White Paper capability statements from interested firms who can demonstrate and document, with evidentiary support, that they 1) possess the minimum qualifications and experience identified in paragraph 7.0 which are critical to the successful execution of the requirements, and 2) demonstrate recent and relevant experience, as the Prime contractor (or subcontractor) performing the same/similar efforts of the same/similar scope, size, and complexity to the enclosure (1) SSN PWS requirements identified in paragraph 8.0.  Interested firms must demonstrate their existing capability, or potential to acquire the capability, to meet the enclosure (1) SSN PWS requirements by the time of contract award, estimated to be 18 March 2027.

6.1	Small Business Concerns

IAW FAR Subpart 19.2 Polices, SSP seeks to provide maximum practicable opportunities in its acquisitions to small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone small business, small disadvantaged business, and women-owned small business concerns.  Small Business Concerns who possess the minimum qualifications and experience identified in paragraph 7.0 and who can demonstrate its concerns’ capability (or ability to obtain the capability by the contract award date) to execute the complete requirements identified in the enclosure (1) SSN PWS in paragraph 8.0, as well provide the requisite past performance experience detailed in Section 9.0, are encouraged to respond to this SSN.  

If a small business concern intends to partner with another entity, the small business concern must identify which specific enclosure (1) PWS efforts/tasks it intends to perform, as well as the specific efforts/tasks the partner will perform, with the substantiating data required in this SSN supporting the identified partnering roles and responsibilities.  NOTE: 100% of the enclosure (1) PWS and SSN requirements must be addressed in any submitted partnering submittal, if obtainable. 

NOTE:  In the event this contract is set aside for small business concerns, the small business concern agrees that it will be in strict compliance and conformance with the percentage payment limitations for services, supplies, or construction (as applicable) to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting and state such in their response.  

7.0	Minimum Qualifications / Experience Requirements

Interested firms shall document and submit specific and evidenced / demonstrated possession of the minimum qualifications and experience requirements in the technical areas identified in Factors 1 through 5 in descending order of importance listed below which are critical to the successful execution of the enclosure (1) SSN PWS requirements in paragraph 8.0.  This experience shall be documented as specified in paragraph 9.0. 

Factor 1: Technical Approach

Evaluators will assess the extent to which the Offeror demonstrates a clear, efficient, and effective approach to providing Office Manager and SES Executive Assistant support services.

Subfactors

Understanding of Requirements

Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of the scope of work, including administrative management, executive support, workflow coordination, correspondence management, calendar and meeting support, and task prioritization for senior leadership.

Shows awareness of the operational environment, stakeholder interactions, and mission priorities.

Methodology and Processes

Provides detailed processes for task management, document control, scheduling, travel coordination, and communication protocols.

Describes quality control measures, escalation procedures, and internal checks to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and confidentiality.

Outlines how the Offeror will ensure continuity of operations during staff absences or turnover.

Use of Tools and Technology

Demonstrates effective use of office productivity tools, government systems (e.g., Defense Travel System (DTS)), and collaboration platforms.

Shows how technology will be leveraged to streamline workflows, track tasks, and support executive decision-making.

Factor 2: Key Personnel Qualifications

Evaluators will assess the qualifications, experience, and capabilities of proposed personnel for Office Manager and SES Executive Assistant roles.

Subfactors

Relevant Experience

Experience supporting SES.

Demonstrated history of managing complex calendars, high-volume correspondence, and sensitive information.

Experience coordinating high-visibility meetings, events, and engagements.

Education and Skills

Relevant education or training in administrative management, business operations, or related fields.

Proficiency in government systems and Microsoft Office Suite.

Professional Competencies

Communication skills, both written and verbal.

Ability to exercise discretion, judgment, and professionalism in a senior executive environment.

Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and operate under tight deadlines.

Factor 3: Staffing Plan and Management Approach

Evaluators will assess the Offeror’s ability to recruit, retain, manage, and oversee personnel to ensure uninterrupted, high-quality support.

Subfactors

Recruitment and Retention Strategy

Ability to source highly qualified administrative professionals with relevant experience.

Retention strategies to minimize turnover and maintain continuity.

Transition and Onboarding Plan

Clear plan for onboarding personnel, including training, knowledge transfer, and familiarization with government processes.

Approach to minimizing disruption during contract transition.

Supervision and Oversight

Management structure for monitoring performance, addressing issues, and ensuring compliance with contract requirements.

Approach to performance feedback, coaching, and continuous improvement.

Factor 4: Past Performance

Evaluators will assess the Offeror’s record of providing similar administrative, office management, and executive support services.

Subfactors

Relevance of Past Performance

Experience performing similar work for DoN agencies

Demonstrated success supporting senior executives or high-visibility offices.

Quality of Past Performance CPARS Ratings

Very good or exceptional CPARS ratings

Customer satisfaction, responsiveness, and ability to meet deadlines.

Evidence of reliability, professionalism, and quality of deliverables.

Problem Resolution

Demonstrated ability to identify issues early, communicate effectively, and implement corrective actions.

Factor 5: Quality Control Plan

Evaluators will assess the Offeror’s approach to ensuring consistent, high-quality performance.

Subfactors

Quality Assurance Processes

Methods for monitoring task completion, accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with government standards.

Risk Management

Identification of potential risks (e.g., staff turnover, workload surges) and mitigation strategies.

Continuous Improvement

Approach to incorporating feedback, improving processes, and enhancing service delivery over time.

8.0	Description of Requirements  

See enclosure (1) SSN PWS Requirements.  

8.1	Quantity of Personnel Required / Place of Performance

14 Full Time Equivalent (FTE) personnel who will provide on-site support at the Washington Navy Yard location, and 1 FTE personnel who will provide on-site support at the Florida location. 

9.0	Evidentiary Qualifications/Experience Documentation Requirements

Interested firms must possess the requisite minimum qualifications and experience identified in paragraph 7.0 and demonstrated relevant and recent experience as it relates to the enclosure (1) PWS requirements in paragraph 8.0. White Paper Capability statements must include all of the content and details identified below:

specifications, schemes, composition, descriptions, methods of calculations, instructions and other

the technology required to manufacture cannon, such as delivery of documentation, training of 
personnel, instructions, consultations and acquainting of specialists with the most economical 
method of using this technology in the manufacture of cannon.

NOTICE TYPE: Sources Sought / Market Research 
Notice ID: SS-26-PHX-020 
 
1. PURPOSE 
This is a Sources Sought Notice issued for market research purposes only in accordance 
with FAR Part 10. This is not a solicitation and does not constitute a commitment by the 
Government. 
The Phoenix Area Indian Health Service (IHS) is conducting market research to determine 
the availability and capability of: 
• Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEE) 
• Other Small Business Concerns 
• Other than Small Business Concerns 
capable of providing a brand-name requirement for: 
Core Strengths / Strength Deployment Inventory (SDI) 2.0 platform subscription, 
assessment credits, and associated support services (OEM: Crucial Learning). 
The Government intends to use the results of this notice to determine the appropriate 
acquisition strategy, including potential set-aside determinations under the Buy Indian Act 
and/or FAR Part 19. 
 
2. REQUIREMENT OVERVIEW 
The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract with: 
• Base Year: 12 months; two 12-month Option Years 
The Contractor shall provide a three-year subscription/licensure solution that includes: 
• SDI 2.0 assessment credits 
• Annual subscription access to the Core Strengths platform (Business Plan up to 
2,500 users) 
• Reporting, team analytics, and data export capabilities 
• Access to SDI-related tools, user guides, and training-support materials 

• Implementation and customer support services 
The platform must support enterprise-wide use, including portability of individual results, 
team comparisons, and consolidated reporting across multiple locations. 
 
3. IMPORTANT BRAND-NAME NOTICE 
This requirement is for a brand-name product: 
Core Strengths / Strength Deployment Inventory (SDI) 2.0 
Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): Crucial Learning 
Interested vendors must demonstrate their capability to provide the required SDI 2.0 
platform, licensing, assessment credits, and associated services. 
• Vendors who are not the OEM (Crucial Learning) shall provide documentation (e.g., 
Letter of Supply or authorization letter) from Crucial Learning confirming their 
authorization to provide the required SDI 2.0 products and services to the Federal 
Government. 
• Responses that do not include proof of authorization may be considered non-
responsive. 
 
4. TECHNICAL CAPABILITY REQUIREMENTS 
Interested firms must demonstrate capability to provide: 
A. Platform and Licensing 
• Access to the SDI 2.0/Core Strengths platform 
• Subscription licensing supporting up to 2,500 users 
• Annual assessment credits 
B. Functional Capabilities 
• Electronic administration of assessments 
• Individual and team reporting 
• Portability of user profiles across teams 
• Consolidated analytics across multiple locations 

• Exportable data (e.g., PDF , CSV/Excel formats) 
C. Implementation and Support 
• Platform setup and administrative access 
• Ongoing customer and technical support 
• Access to training-support materials and user guides 
D. Experience and Past Performance 
• Experience providing SDI 2.0/Core Strengths or equivalent OEM-authorized 
solutions 
• Experience supporting enterprise-wide implementations 
• Experience with Federal or healthcare organizations (preferred but not required) 
 
5. NAICS CODE 
NAICS Code: 541611 – Administrative Management and General Management 
Consulting Services 
Size Standard: $24.5M 
Respondents may recommend an alternative NAICS code with justification. 
PSC Code: R408 – Program Management/Support Services 
 
6. BUY INDIAN ACT NOTICE AND DEFINITIONS 
The IHS Contracting Officer will give priority to Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises 
(ISBEE) in accordance with the Buy Indian Act. 
This Sources Sought Notice is being issued, in part, to determine whether this requirement 
may be set aside for ISBEE firms. 
Respondents asserting ISBEE status shall: 
• Identify ownership and control structure 
• Demonstrate compliance with ISBEE requirements 
• Describe how the firm will perform the primary and vital contract requirements 

• Identify subcontractors and percentage of work to be performed 
 
7. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS 
Responses shall not exceed 7 pages and shall include: 
• Company name, address, and SAM UEI number 
• Business size and socioeconomic status 
• Capability statement addressing Sections 3 and 4 
• Proof of authorization from Crucial Learning (if not OEM) 
• FSS Contract Number, if applicable 
• Relevant past performance 
Submit responses electronically to: 
Dekovan Cook 
Supervisory Contract Specialist 
Dekovan.Cook@ihs.gov 
Subject Line: SS-26-PHX-020 Core Strengths / SDI 2.0 Sources Sought – PAIHS 
Submission Deadline: As stated in SAM.gov 
Interested parties are encouraged to review the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW) 
for detailed requirements. 
 
8. DISCLAIMER 
This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The 
Government will not reimburse any costs incurred in responding. 
The Government reserves the right to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy based 
on responses received. 
 
END OF NOTICE

Statement of Work (SOW) 
Phoenix Area Indian Health Service (PAIHS) 
Core Strengths / Strength Deployment Inventory (SDI) 2.0 
 
Date: 2026-03-03 
1. General Information 
1.1 Title of Project 
Core Strengths / Strength Deployment Inventory (SDI) 2.0 —  Subscription/Licensure and Assessment Credits 
1.2 Background 
PAIHS requires continued access to the SDI 2.0/Core Strengths platform to support relationship awareness, team 
effectiveness, leadership development, and conflict resolution across the Phoenix Area and its service units. The 
SDI 2.0 framework is currently in use and PAIHS has trained facilitators prepared to implement and sustain the 
program. Continuity of the SDI model, reporting, and historical profiles is required to avoid duplication of cost 
and delays that would result from changing frameworks. 
1.3 Scope 
The Contractor shall provide a three-year subscription/licensure solution that includes: (1) SDI 2.0 assessment 
credits, (2) annual subscription access to the SDI/Core Strengths platform (Business Plan up to 2,500 members), 
(3) access to SDI-related tools and user guides, and (4) training-support materials and customer support 
necessary for successful implementation. The platform must enable electronic administration of assessments, 
reporting, portability of individual results across teams, and consolidated analysis across multiple PAIHS 
locations. 
1.4 Period of Performance 
Base Period: 12 months from date of award. 
Option Period 1: 12 months. 
Option Period 2: 12 months. 
Note: Each performance period includes platform subscription access and the annual quantity of assessment 
credits shown in Section 2. Options may be exercised at the Government’s discretion in accordance with the 
contract. 
1.5 Type of Contract 
Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). 
1.6 Place of Performance / Government Users 
Electronic access for Government users located throughout PAIHS, including employees who work 
remotely/telework. PAIHS locations include: 

• Phoenix Area Indian Health Service – Phoenix, AZ 
• Uintah-Ouray Service Unit – Fort Duchesne, UT 
• Desert Visions/Nevada Skies Youth Treatment Centers – Sacaton, AZ and Wadsworth, NV 
• Hopi Health Care Center – Polacca, AZ 
• Colorado River Service Unit – Parker, AZ 
• Whiteriver Service Unit – Whiteriver, AZ 
• Phoenix Indian Medical Center – Phoenix, AZ 
• Fort Yuma Service Unit – Winterhaven, AZ 
• Elko Service Unit – Elko, NV 
1.7 Kickoff / Post-Award Conference 
Performance shall not begin until the Contracting Officer (CO) has conducted a kickoff meeting or notified the 
Contractor in writing that a kickoff meeting is not required. 
2. Requirements and Deliverables 
2.1 Subscription, Credits, and Core Capabilities

2.2 System and Functional Requirements 
Online assessments accessible via modern web browsers and usable by Government personnel. 
Role-based administrative access for designated Government administrators/facilitators. 
Portability of individual profiles/results across multiple teams and over time within the subscription 
term. 
Ability to generate individual and group/team reports; ability to create an unlimited number of teams

2.3 Training Support Materials 
The Contractor shall provide access to training-support materials for Government facilitators and end users, 
such as guides, job aids, and platform training resources. Any live training, if ordered, shall be identified as a

2.4 Deliverable Schedule and Acceptance 
Within 10 business days after award (or as negotiated), provide administrative access and instructions

confirms reporting/export functions operate as required.

4.1 Privacy and Data Handling 
The Contractor shall identify what user information and assessment data elements are collected, stored, 
processed, and exported by the platform. 
Assessment data shall be used only for providing the contracted services and shall not be sold, mined, or 
used for marketing. 
Upon request, the Contractor shall provide data export(s) of Government results in a mutually agreed 
format to support continuity and records needs. 
The Contractor shall notify the CO/COR promptly of any suspected or confirmed security incident 
affecting Government data, in accordance with contract terms. 
4.2 Information Security 
The Contractor shall implement appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to 
protect Government data handled or stored within the platform. 
If the service is categorized as a cloud/IT service by the Government, the Contractor shall support any 
applicable Federal security requirements identified in the contract (e.g., documentation needed for 
security review). 
4.3 Section 508 Accessibility

Section 508 requirements to the extent required

Except as provided herein, all terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. 
 
RESPONSES TO QUESTIONS FROM POTENTIAL OFFERORS: 
Question 1 
Regarding personnel biosketches: Will NIH formatted biosketches be acceptable via inclusion in 
an appendix to the technical proposal or should they be uploaded electronically to NIH? 
 
Response to Question 1 
NIH-formatted biosketches or resumes for all key personnel are required. Offerors shall include 
these documents as an appendix to the technical proposal. No separate electronic submission to 
NIH is required. 
 
Question 2 
On Page 22 of Attachment 4 Section 1, 3) Mandatory Qualification Criteria (MQC): We are 
unsure about what should be included in this section of the technical proposal. Should this 
section provide a list of the documentation for our USDA inspections, AAALAC approval letter, 
Select Agent permit, etc. with the actual documents included in an Appendix? 
 
Response to Question 2 
The wording “MQC” is not succinctly defined in the RFP, but it is in included below.  All of the 
documentation the vendor provided above in question 2 is appropriate and should also include 
the following: 
 
The project requirements include comprehensive housing, care, and technical support for Non-
Human Primates (NHPs) essential to vaccine and therapeutic development. The selected 
contractor will be required to deliver all necessary services, qualified personnel, materials, 
equipment, and facilities, including those capable of handling up to 500 NHPs annually. Key 
technical requirements include providing Biosafety Level-2 (BSL-2) and Biosafety Level-3 
(BSL-3) animal holding facilities, with specialized capabilities, such as a dedicated Tuberculosis 
(TB) suite equipped with GFE PET/CT scanning for ABSL-3 level studies. The selected 
contractor must ensure strict adherence to NIH and federal animal care and biosafety standards. 
Deliverables include regular reports on animal care, veterinary services, and technical 
procedures, as well as detailed records of all activities conducted under the contract. Of 
particular importance is the maintenance of a secure and compliant environment, ensuring the 
humane treatment of NHPs, and the capability to support long-term and high-containment 
infectious disease studies.  
This acquisition will have a mandatory qualification that Offerors must demonstrate their facility 
is within 60 minutes from the VRC NIH Bethesda campus via reasonable transportation methods 

AMENDMENT #1 RFP No. 75N93024R00029                                                                         3 
 
(e.g. automobile) on a routine basis. The 60-minute proximity requirement is essential to 
ensuring the stability of research materials, timely sample processing, and efficient facility 
oversight. 
Many materials, such as immunizations and therapeutics, have strict stability limits and must be 
prepared under controlled conditions at VRC by scientific staff within one hour before being 
transported for administration. Similarly, sample integrity depends on rapid processing to 
maintain viability for analysis. According to International Society for Biological and 
Environmental Repositories (ISBER) best practices, specimens should be processed as quickly as 
possible, as even brief exposure to warm environments can cause macromolecular degradation, 
compromising research outcomes. 
 Additionally, study quality assurance and semi-annual facility inspections by the VRC IACUC 
require feasible travel logistics without excessive costs or scheduling burdens. This time-based 
requirement ensures research continuity, compliance, and operational efficiency.  
The components listed below are critical to this acquisition and stabilizing research materials. 
These components include integrity of research material, integrity and processing of samples and 
feasibility of required visits.  
1. Integrity of research material: Many research studies involve preparation of materials such as 
immunizations and therapeutics that have limited stability and must be administered within 
one hour of thawing, preparation, dilution, resuspension etc. There are often limitations in 
availability of appropriate laboratory space and equipment for performing these preparations 
at the contractor site. Requirements of this nature for preparation can include but, are not 
limited to, need for: Biosafety cabinets/sterile environment, water bath/bead bath for thawing 
materials, pipettes, etc. Therefore, the ability to prepare these materials at VRC and transport 
them to the contractor site and administer within the stability time frame is required. 
2. Integrity and processing of samples: Many of the samples that are collected for research 
studies require processing before they may be analyzed and/or stored for future analysis. 
Some of these processing procedures require fresh tissues or samples which have limited 
viability under room temperature or refrigerated conditions. Additionally, researchers and 
designated staff must be able to process samples in a timely fashion during their available 
work hours; required processing and sample analysis can be lengthy. 
3. Feasibility of required visits: The VRC IACUC must perform semi-annual facility 
inspections. These visits require scheduling designated time, and transportation of IACUC 
member to the contractor site. Therefore, a distance requirement of 60 minutes from VRC 
maintains a feasible length of time for performing this activity, not requiring additional travel 
expenses or approvals for members.

proposal document (see Attachment 4, Section 1.3). Should we include past performance here? 
 
Response to Question 3 
 
A. Facility within 1-hour radius of NIH Bethesda 
B. Required federal regulatory compliance documentation and certifications 
C. ABSL-2/3 operational capability and regulatory approval documentation for operation 
D. Ability to meet strict sample transport timelines 
E. Valid IACUC/IBC, Safety, and animal welfare compliance  
F. Past Performance or reference to location within proposal 
 
Yes. Any other past performance information should be included in this section of the proposal. 
 
Question 4 
How are bidders supposed to link the new online biosketches to their submissions? Are we 
expected to include PDFs of the Biosketch and Supplement forms, but only after they are 
"Certified" (basically e-signed) through SciEnv by the owner of the account, or is an alternative 
method supposed to be used? 
 
Response to Question 4 
 
The Government is unaware of any specific technical system requirements for submitting 
biosketches. In the absence of explicit instructions or guidance in the RFP, it would be 
reasonable to expect the offeror to determine the most appropriate and efficient method for 
providing the required information in support of their proposal. Ideally, the information should

Challenge Based Acquisition (ChBA) 
Phase 1 Questions and Answers - February 27, 2026 
Page 1 of 32 
No. Reference Question FAA Answer 
1 Section 5.a.i, 
Factor 1 
The FAA's requirements may allow other companies who may have less 
experience than us to qualify. For example, we have completed such 
projects for $250K that could be used for reference.  Another company 
may have an IDIQ with a ceiling of $10M per year and completed a 
reference project for only $50K and still qualify. Effectively the other 
company would be accepted with a $50K project and our company 
would be excluded for its $250K project. 
The FAA's evaluation criteria and process for Factor 1 
were carefully selected and will not be changed except 
as noted in the updated Announcement. All corporate 
experience examples must be recent and relevant per 
the requirements in Section 5.a.i. Also, Footnote 3 
defines how Offerors must calculate the Annual Dollar 
Amount for ordering vehicles (e.g., IDIQs). 
2 Section 5.a.i, 
Factor 1 
Would the FAA consider restructuring Factor 1 as a pass/fail threshold 
(e.g., a minimum validated score of 30,000 points) rather than only 
accepting the (10) highest scoring Offerors? Offerors meeting the 
threshold would have their Factor 2 Concept Papers evaluated; those 
that do not would be eliminated. 
No. Factor 1 will not be restructured to pass/fail. 
3 Section 5.a.i, 
Factor 1 
Would the FAA consider allowing Offerors to include experience from a 
“significant subcontractor” , defined as performing at least 20% of the 
ATLAS effort, subject to reasonable limits that maintain prime 
accountability? 
The Offeror itself will have privity of contract with the 
FAA and will solely be responsible for contract 
performance. Therefore, it is essential for the FAA to 
assess the Offeror’s experience to ensure the Offeror 
can perform this highly complex project successfully. 
However, the FAA has updated the Announcement 
based on feedback received. Offerors may now utilize 
experience performed by proposed subcontractors, 
teaming partners or affiliates (including parent 
companies or wholly owned subsidiaries), but such 
experience may only constitute a maximum of 25% of 
the total points claimed and earned by the Offeror in 
Factor 1. Additionally, to claim and earn points for 
experience that is not the Offeror’s direct experience, 
the Offeror must include a separate narrative that 
adequately demonstrates meaningful participation by 
the proposed subcontractors, teaming partners or 
affiliates (including parent companies or wholly owned 
subsidiaries) on the ATLAS program. Offerors must also 
complete Column F in the updated Attachment 2 – 
Self-Score Model to clearly indicate which entity 
performed the cited contract or task order example.

Challenge Based Acquisition (ChBA) 
Phase 1 Questions and Answers - February 27, 2026

4 Section 5.b, Down-
select Decision 
Given that Phase 2 and Phase 3 are weighted more heavily and are 
technical in nature, would the FAA consider increasing the relative weight 
of Factor 2 in the Phase 1 down-select to ensure the Offeror pool 
advancing to Phase 2 reflects the strongest technical approaches, not 
just the largest corporate portfolios. 
The Announcement has been updated to clarify how 
the FAA will make the Phase 1 down-select decision.  
5  Given the SOO’s emphasis on achieving Continuous Authorization to 
Operate (cATO) by embedding security controls natively into the 
development and operational fabric and the Phase 1 requirement to 
demonstrate ‘tools and approach, ’ is FAA seeking: (1) primarily a systems

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Veteran’s Administration (VA) Office of Research and Development, Regional Procurement Office – East in Pittsburgh, PA intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Janelle Sue Taylor, PhD based in Toronto, Ontario on behalf of the VA Puget Sound Healthcare System. The requirement is to provide research assistance for planned VA medical studies. The planned studies focus on Ethnographic Methodological Expertise for research study titled “CONSERVE-CKM: Study on Care of Patients with Advanced Kidney Disease.” The planned studies follow preliminary studies based on the same subject. 

This service contract covers services including providing content and methodological expertise in ethnographic research methods, health systems implementation, and advanced kidney disease. The contractor shall provide research support, guidance, and training across the life of the study and will work under the supervision of the VA Principal Investigator (PI) to serve as an ethnographic, methodological, and content expert in ethnography and health system processes for kidney disease. 

Vendor will collaborate with the PI and meet with the research team and collaborators monthly to complete the tasks below. 

Tasks and Deliverables

Task 1 – Guidance and Training for Qualitative Interviews

 

Provide input and ethnographic content expertise on training of interviewers and development of interview guides for qualitative interviews with Veterans, caregivers and clinicians that elicit care processes and factors that promote or hinder effective delivery of healthcare and outcomes for patients with advanced kidney disease who are unsure or do not wish to forgo dialysis. As interviews will be conducted longitudinally, approach should elicit changes in experiences and processes over time. The Vendor will also provide guidance on sampling strategy to allow for depth and nuance in elucidation of emergent themes related to the care of these Veterans. 

Task 2 – Guidance and Training for Clinical Field Observations

Provide input and ethnographic content expertise on training of project staff in field observations and approaches to field observations of care interactions between Veterans, caregivers, and clinicians. As field observations will be conducted in a variety of settings (i.e. home, emergency departments, hospital) and modalities (i.e., in-person, phone, video) in which care occurs, approaches will need to be adapted to each setting and modality. 

Task 3 – Guidance and Training for Field Observations of Lived Experiences with Kidney Disease

Provide input and content expertise on training project staff in field observations of lived experiences of patients with kidney disease. As lived experiences of kidney disease is highly varied and will include a diversity of times, settings and activities, approaches will need to be facile and dynamic for each patient.

Task 4 - Guidance and Training in Artifact Collection and Review

Provide guidance on strategy for artifact collection and review of artifacts shared by patients that reflect their experience of kidney disease and care. A range of artifacts may be provided by patients (e.g. photos, writing, objects) and strategies for interviewing patients about what these artifacts represent will need to be broad and comprehensive. 

Task 5 – Guidance for Data Management and Analytical Plan

Provide guidance on development of data management and analysis plans. The Vendor will guide the project team on organizing and preparing collected data for analysis. The Vendor will train staff to manage and analyze primary data collected, and review aggregated deidentified data to assist with evaluation of current care approaches. The analytical plan should include coding strategies and approaches to thematic synthesis that will result in trustworthy, rigorous, and credible conclusions and recommendations for care related to Veterans who are unsure or wish to forgo dialysis.

Task 6 – Guidance on presentation of findings

Vendor will guide the project team to prepare presentations and final reports for the project sponsor. Vendor can co-author manuscripts for peer-reviewed publications and will be notated with their non-VA affiliation.  

Deliverables

The requirement will take place at a VA facility in Puget Sound, WA. The sole source is pursuant to RFO 6.103-1 Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, however; any responsible source who believes it is capable of meeting the requirement may submit a capability statement and supporting documentation to the contracting office no later than Tuesday, April 21, 2026, (10:00 AM, EST). Interest/capability statements may be sent to Michael Haydo at Michael.haydo@va.gov. No telephone responses will be accepted. A determination not to compete the proposed requirement based upon the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

Page 1 of 5 
 
Pre-solicitation Notice  
 
Type: Pre-Solicitation  
Notice Number: 75N92026R00008 
Title: Study Coordinating Center for the Lung Health Cohort Study 
Classification Code: A – Research & Development  
NAICS Code: 541715, Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering and Life Sciences 
(except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology).  
Posted Date: April 16, 2026  
Primary Point of Contact:  Lynn Furtaw, Contracting Officer, Lynn.Furtaw@nih.gov 
 
Contracting Office Address 
Department of Health and Human Services, National Institutes of Health, National Heart, Lung 
and Blood Institute, Rockledge Dr. Bethesda, MD, Office of Acquisitions 6705 Rockledge Dr RKL2, 
Bethesda, MD, 20892-7902, United States 
 
Introduction 
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) is seeking a Study Coordinating Center (SCC) 
for The Lung Health Cohort Study. The purpose of this announcement is to provide a Pre-
solicitation Notice for the release of Solicitation 75N92026R00008. THIS IS A SYNOPSIS. THIS IS 
NOT A SOLICITATION. 
 
Background 
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is the fourth leading cause of death in the United 
States, yet the complexity and chronic nature of the disease have made it difficult to understand 
and treat.  Thus far, pulmonary physicians and respiratory researchers define respiratory health as 
the absence of lung disease.  This simplistic definition has limited the development of a robust 
approach to the prevention of lung disease.  Because of the absence of adult life-course studies 
focused primarily on lung health, the intermediate phenotypes of impaired lung health (which exist 
on a continuum between ideal lung health and lung disease) have not been well-defined.  There is a 
critical need to identify modifiable risk factors and biomarkers for impaired lung health that will 
allow clinicians to recognize impaired lung health and intervene before chronic lung disease 
develops.  There has been a national level infrastructure of the American Lung Association’s (ALA) 
Airways Clinical Research Centers (ACRC) which has formed the first national cohort of adults 
focused on respiratory health.   
 
The Lung Health Cohort (LHC) is a longitudinal study that will enroll up to 4,000 community-
dwelling adults aged 25 -35 years from 17 metropolitan regions across the United States. The study 
was designed to examine a large cohort of healthy young adults to better define and characterize 
the constructs of “ideal” versus “impaired” lung health. The study is currently supported through a 
single NHLBI cooperative agreement (U01), first awarded in 2019 and expected to end in early 
2027, which supports the LHC study coordinating center. The cooperative agreement supports 
study enrollment, data coordination, human subjects regulation, imaging oversight, environmental 
surveillance, and other functions.  
Study procedures for the baseline visit include physical assessment, spirometry, chest computed 

 
 
 
 
Page 2 of 5 
 
tomography (CT) scan, accelerometry, and collection of nasal epithelial lining fluid, nasal epithelial 
cells, blood, and urine.  Additionally, medically related participant questionnaires are being 
recorded such as sociodemographic characteristics, home address histories and exposures, work 
history and exposures, medical histories, lung health, and health behaviors and activity.  While 
baseline visits are ongoing, the full cohort of 4,000 participants is expected to have been enrolled 
and complete a baseline visit by early 2027 under the current cooperative agreement.  
 
 
Objectives 
The objective of this acquisition is to procure the services of a study coordinating center to support 
the continuation of LHC. The contractor shall complete a second in-person visit of the full LHC 
cohort, to be completed approximately five years after the baseline visit, as well as other data to be 
collected remotely, all to be conducted through the ACRC network. Data and biospecimens shall be 
assessed for quality, stored, analyzed, and distributed as appropriate. Finally, the study shall be 
managed in a manner consistent with NIH and NHLBI policies with oversight from a single 
Institutional Review Board (IRB) and an NHLBI-managed Observational Study Monitoring Board 
(OSMB).  The objective of this contract is to exploit the unique characteristics of the LHC to clarify 
how potential factors might alter ideal lung health and increase risk for future diseases such as 
chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. 
 
Project Requirements 
 
Services to be performed include: 
 
Task Area One – Program Management: The contractor shall facilitate the management of study 
personnel, data, and biospecimens to enable achievement of study goals. 
 
1. Organize residential, school and occupational address histories, which will be used to 
enable geocoding. Geocodes will be used to link relevant exposure data to each 
participant, including such exposures as elemental carbon, organic carbon, nitrogen 
dioxide, atmospheric particulate matter, ozone, proximity to greenspace, census-tract 
level indicators of neighborhood socioeconomic position, and local daily temperature. 
2. Evaluate the quality of CT scans collected during study visits. Analyze data of images 
collected during baseline and follow-up study visits. 
3. Analyze LHC data to address the major scientific goals of the study, generate study 
manuscripts, and publish in peer-reviewed journals. Overall, this work is expected to 
result in at least one peer-reviewed publication per year throughout the contract 
period. Provide statistical analytical support to study investigators within limits of 
resources provided by the Data Coordinating Center (DCC). 
4. Perform statistical analyses and power considerations. 
5. Communicate with a designated and approved single IRB to obtain approval for the 
main study protocol and ancillary studies, as well as to report adverse events and other 
deviations as specified by NIH policies. 
6. Schedule, plan, and organize annual meetings and ad hoc meetings as directed of an 

 
 
 
 
Page 3 of 5 
 
Observational Study Monitoring Board (OSMB), consisting of between 4 and 7 
members. Provide compensation to OSMB members. Provide expedited reporting to 
the OSMB of serious unexpected adverse events and unanticipated problems as defined 
and required by NHLBI policies. Provide annual reports to the OSMB of study progress, 
including enrollments and visit completions, adverse events, protocol deviations, data 
quality and timeliness, presentations, publications, and major study findings. (The 
NHLBI Adverse Event (AE) and Unanticipated Problem (UP) Reporting Policy describes 
the procedures for identifying, monitoring, and reporting adverse events and 
unanticipated problems (http://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/funding/policies/adverse.htm). 
7. Oversee general study management using a Data Coordinating Center, and Imaging 
Core, an Environmental Core, and other study centers and cores, as approved by NHLBI. 
8. Establish and manage committees as needed for study governance. These may be 
organized through the ACRC network. 
9. Travel to and register for domestic and international scientific meetings to discuss and 
present study data.  
10. Travel to conduct study site visits and training, as needed. 
11. Oversee a data repository with quality control of study data. The data repository shall 
implement data science methods, standards, and defined metadata that are consistent 
with NHLBI recommendations. 
12. Provide quality control checks of data submitted from the clinical centers, and work 
with the clinical centers to correct errors. Collect and store in the data repository newly 
collected data, including data from study Visits, long-tern follow up contacts, 
environmental monitoring, and biospecimen analyses. Incorporate ancillary study data 
into the contract study data according to NIH and NHLBI policies. Provide appropriate 
data quality control. 
13. Maintain a biospecimen repository for Lung Health Cohort biospecimens. This 
repository will store biospecimens under conditions established by protocol to 
minimize degradation over time and will employ backup systems to ensure preservation 
of biospecimens in the event of power losses. Distribute biospecimens to investigators 
for approved ancillary studies. 
14. Transport biospecimens to an NHLBI-approved biorepository upon study conclusion. 
15. Comply with NHLBI Data Management and Sharing Policies, including the NHLBI 
Supplement to the NIH Policy for Data Management and Sharing (this can be found at 
https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/grants-and-training/policies-and-guidelines/nhlbi-policy-for-
data-sharing). Compliance will involve regular deposition of all available cleaned study 
data and ancillary study data to an NHLBI-approved scientific data repository such as 
NHLBI’s BioData Catalyst. The schedule of data deposition will be mutually agreed upon 
by the contractor and NHLBI, but is expected to be approximately once per year. Data 
sets shall include documentation of data formats and study procedures. 
16. Provide regular progress reports to NHLBI that include enrollment and retention rates 
of Lung Health Cohort participants, in person and telephonic visit completion rates, 
data completeness, data quality measures, numbers of manuscripts and publications, 
numbers of funded ancillary studies, and number of Early Stage Investigators funded to 
conduct ancillary studies. 
 

 
 
 
 
Page 4 of 5 
 
17. Establish a study website that is 508-compliant within 6 months of contract 
award.Maintain and update the website throughout the contract period. The study 
website will include: 
a. A description of the LHC study 
b. A description of available data, how to request data, and how to propose 
ancillary studies.  
c. A description of available biospecimens and the procedures for requesting and 
obtaining approval for obtaining biospecimens. 
d. Links to any current study policies, as appropriate. 
18. Comply with the NIH Public Access Policy To that end, the Contractor shall do so for any 
manuscript that arises from any direct funding from the contract. For more information, 
see NOTOD-08-033 (http://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-
08033.html) and the Public Access website (https://publicaccess.nih.gov/). 
19. Comply with all other NHLBI and NIH policies. 
 
Task Area Two –  The contractor shall use the ACRC network to complete a five -year follow-up exam 
and remote follow-up data collection of the Lung Health Cohort. 
 
1. Complete an in- clinic follow -up exam of up to 4000 Lung Health Cohort participants. 
Visits will be scheduled approximately five years after each participant’s baseline visit. 
This visit will be conducted according to an NHLBI-approved protocol and will include the 
key data listed below. Some subjects may refuse some aspects of the visit but may still 
be considered to have a complete visit. Study visits shall be conducted through the ACRC 
network and may include (as defined by NHLBI-approved protocol): 
a. Physical assessment (e.g. height, weight, resting heart rate, blood pressure) 
b. Spirometry 
c. Pregnancy testing in participants of child-bearing potential 
d. Chest CT scan (to be transferred to a central Imaging Core) 
e. Questionnaires (including but not limited to: contact information, address history, 
demographics, lung health, substance use, environmental and occupational 
exposures, medication use, medical history, activity, sleep, social elements, 
nutrition) 
f. Nasosorption strip collection 
g. Nasal epithelial curettage 
h. Phlebotomy  
i. Urine collection 
2. Process biospecimens collected at baseline exam (blood, nasal epithelial cells, and urine.) 
Each sample will be labeled with a unique bar code that includes no health information 
but can be linked to the participant ID. 
3. Ship biospecimens to ACRC study biorepository for long -term storage. Biospecimens 
collected under this contract will be the property of the United States Government. 

 
 
 
 
Page 5 of 5 
 
4. Collect data remotely on the full Cohort. Remote data collection will be according to an 
NHLBI-approved protocol and may include (as defined by NHLBI-approved protocol): 
a. Home spirometry  
b. Actigraphy monitoring  
c. Activity log 
d. Vaping log 
5. Collect remote follow-up data on up to 4000 Lung Health Cohort participants every 3 to 
6 months (up to four times a year) during which participants may be asked to (as defined 
by NHLBI-approved protocol): 
a. Update contact information 
b. Complete additional assessments related to topics from the in-person visit 
c. Complete additional assessments related to health events 
d. Schedule a coached at-home spirometry session, to be completed at a later date 
6. Contact study participants via telephone or internet to collect additional information if 
deemed necessary by the approved study protocol or by NHLBI. 
 
 
Anticipated Period of Performance 
The Government intends to negotiate an IDIQ contract for the potential period of six (6) years with 
an approximate award date of March 1, 2027. 
 
This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) and the Government is not committed to award a 
contract pursuant to this announcement. The RFP will be available in SAM.gov no sooner than 15 
calendar days of posting this notice.

Performance Work Statement 
AFLCMC Engineering Directorate (EN-EZ) 
Collateral Conference Room 162 
 
1.0 Background 
The U.S. Government requires a technology upgrade for the conference room located at 
conference room 162 located in Building 28, Area B, WPAFB, OH The purpose is to integrate 
a modern Uniﬁed Communications (UC) capability using Microsoft Teams into a Collateral 
Secret SIPRNET environment. The room contains existing VTC equipment that is outdated 
and scheduled for decommissioning but will remain in place temporarily. The new solution 
must be integrated with certain remaining components while replacing those that are 
incompatible. 
2.0 Scope 
The contractor shall provide and install a complete, turn-key solution to enable MS Teams 
functionality within the designated conference room. The work includes providing and 
installing a new camera, microphone system, and control system processor, and 
integrating these components with the existing displays and control interface. The ﬁnal 
system must be capable of dual operation, allowing users to select either the new MS 
Teams capability or the legacy VTC system until it is decommissioned. The solution must 
be engineered to function independently after the legacy system is removed without 
requiring rework. 
3.0 Speciﬁc Tasks 
The contractor shall: 
• 3.1 Install New Camera System: Provide and install one (1) 4K-capable web camera. 
The camera shall be mounted on the front wall, centered between the two existing 
wall displays. 
• 3.2 Install New Microphone System: Provide and install a microphone solution 
optimized for MS Teams. The preferred solution is a single tabletop device capable 
of capturing audio from all participants in the room. The device must feature a 
readily accessible physical mute/unmute control. Ceiling-mounted microphone 
solutions are not desired. 
• 3.3 Integrate Audio: Conﬁgure the audio output from the new MS Teams system to 
be routed through the two (2) existing 75-inch wall-mounted displays. 

• 3.4 Replace Control System Processor: Replace the outdated, end-of-life Crestron 
rack-mounted controller with a modern processor unit that is capable of supporting 
both the new MS Teams integration and the legacy VTC system. 
• 3.5 Reprogram Control Interface: Reprogram the existing Crestron touch panel to 
provide a single, intuitive user interface. The control panel must allow users to easily 
select and operate one of the following modes: 
• Microsoft Teams Session 
• Legacy GVS VTC System 
• PC-based Presentation (local display) 
• 3.6 System Integration and Dual-Use Functionality: Integrate the new MS Teams 
equipment with the legacy VTC system to allow for seamless switching between the 
two. The technical solution must be designed so that the future removal of the 
legacy VTC hardware does not disable or negatively impact the functionality of the 
newly installed MS Teams solution. 
4.0 Security and Compliance Requirements 
All equipment, software, and conﬁgurations provided under this contract must comply with 
all applicable security requirements for operation on SECRET networks. This includes, but 
is not limited to: 
• 4.1 DISA STIGs: The system and its components must be conﬁgured in compliance 
with all relevant Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical 
Implementation Guides (STIGs). 
• 4.2 IA Accreditation: All hardware and software components must be listed on the 
DoD Information Network (DoDIN) Approved Products List (APL) and meet the 
requirements for use in a secure environment. The solution must be capable of 
achieving Information Assurance (IA) accreditation. 
  
See BOM for more details.
