GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS ISSUED  SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION.

SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION ABOUT PRICING, DELIVERY, THE MARKET, AND CAPABILITIES IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI FOR PLANNING PURPOSES IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e).

DISCLAIMER

This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation.  All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly.  IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

SOURCES SOUGHT/RFI DESCRIPTION

This is NOT a solicitation announcement.  This is a Sources Sought Notice / RFI only.  The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice / RFI is to gain information about potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS 541519 (size standard of 150 Employees). Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions.  After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI, further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcements may be published.  

STATEMENT OF WORK

Introduction:

The VA Long Beach Healthcare System has a requirement to purchase six (6) Computer on Wheel (COW) carts equivalent to Howard Medicare HI-Care E Cart Part# 1622668 for Food & Nutrition services. This requirement is in support of a brand name or equal requirement. 

Deliverables

Requirements

VAAR 852.212-71 Gray Market and Counterfeit Items applies on this acquisition. No remanufacturers or gray market items will be acceptable. Vendor shall be an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), authorized dealer, authorized distributor or authorized reseller verified by an authorization letter or other documents from the OEM signed. The letter must either state specific product(s) quoted or that the quoter is an authorized distributor for all the manufacturer’s products. This letter must be on the manufacturer’s letterhead and contains the signature of an authorized official for the manufacturer.

NOTE: Potential offers must be aware that the items being acquired are procured as Brand Name or Equal. For those items that are “or equal”, a description of the salient characteristics is outlined below. It is offeror’s responsibility to demonstrate its offer meeting the salient physical and functional characteristics included in this solicitation. If the offer does NOT demonstrate, the offer will be considered non-responsive. The interested parties bear full responsibility to ensure their submission demonstrates to the government that they can satisfy the requirement by providing the brand name or equal to the supplies being requested.

Salient characteristics:

Must come with power manager, a web-based tool to able to monitor and manage cart from remote access

Must come with power display, a web-based tool to run on the local computer device on each cart providing access to power supply data as well as communication to power manager

Must come with Med Manager, which is web-based tool for remote management of cart settings and med drawer access permissions

Must come with Med Display, which is a windows application that runs on local computing devices on each cart providing direct access to local med drawer cabinets, cart settings, audit records, and drawer calibration

Must have Central control panel for drawer access, power system controls, battery fuel gauge with visual and audible alerts, height adjustments, and light controls 

Must come with a monitor, keyboard, and mouse for each cart.

Monitor mount must be able to tilt and swivel motion, supporting vertical and horizontal monitor orientation

Must come with two locking casters on front

Must feature motorized, height-adjustable mechanisms for both the monitor and the worksurface

Must be rechargeable

Must have ergonomic adjustable push handles on front of cart

Must have slide-out keyboard tray

Must provide a mouse surface and mouse pouch that can be positioned on either the left or right side of the keyboard to accommodate user preference

Must come with a minimum of 8ft power cord with hospital-grade AC plug

Must have a mount for PIV (personal identification verification)

Monitor must come with privacy filter

Must come with a minimum 3-year standard warranty at no additional cost to the Government

Must shipped fully assemble or offer assembly upon delivery at no additional cost to the Government

Delivery

Place of performance:

VA Long Beach Healthcare System

5901 East 7th Street

Building 149

Long Bech, CA 90822

Delivery term is freight on board (FOB) destination. All shipping costs must be included in unit cost

The contractor is required to define the need for a staging area to accommodate delivery if needed

The delivery shall take place during normal business hours: 0800 – 1500 (8am to 3pm pacific local time) Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays

Delivery trucks will not be permitted to remain at the loading dock. Trucks shall be uploaded, moved from the dock, and then brought back to dock if required to haul out any waste, tools, or excess materials.

Labeling of deliverable shall include the VA contract number and purchase order number for identification and reference upon receipt of delivery

The list of DRAFT characteristics is intended to be descriptive, not restrictive, of the supplies/services that are required. 

If your company is interested and capable of providing the required supplies/services, please provide the information indicated below. Response to this notice should include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the following questions:  

(1) Submit your capabilities statement illustrating how your organization can/cannot meet the list of SOW requirements.  For instances where your company cannot meet the SOW requirement(s), please explain.  For instances where your company can meet the SOW requirement(s), please show how your company meets/exceeds each requirement.  

(2) Please review the list of SOW requirements and provide any additional feedback or suggestions.  If none, please reply as N/A.

(3) Please indicate the size status and representations of your business, such as but not limited to: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), HUBZone, Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB), Large Business, etc.

(4) Is your company considered small under the NAICS code identified in this RFI?

(5) Are you the manufacturer, authorized distributor, and/or can your company provide a solution to the required supplies/services described in the list of SOW?

(6) If you are a large business, do you have any designated/authorized distributors? If so, please provide their company name, telephone, point of contact and size status (if available).

(7) If you’re a small business and you are an authorized distributor/reseller for the items identified above, do you alter; assemble; modify; the items requested in any way? If you do, state how and what is altered; assembled; modified.

(8) Limitations on Subcontracting: How does your business ensure compliance with the limitations on subcontracting as outlined in 13 CFR § 125.6? 

(9) Are the items you are identifying/providing considered Commercial of the Shelf (COTS) items as defined in FAR Part 2.101 under commercial items?

(10) Non-Manufacturer Rule: If applicable, can you confirm your business complies with the Non-Manufacturer rule? Specifically, does your company: Provide a product from a small business manufacturer or processor? Not exceed 500 employees? Primarily engage in the retail or wholesale trade and normally sell the type of item being supplied? Take ownership or possession of the item(s) with its personnel, equipment or facilities in a manner consistent with industry practice? 

(11) Please indicate whether your product conforms to the requirements of the Buy American Act?

(12) What is your lead time to deliver a single unit with all components?  Is there scale in lead time with greater quantities? Please elaborate.

(13) What is estimated life span of your solution?  What support/services does that entail?

(14) Does your proposed equipment have FDA clearance?  Please specify what FDA clearance(s) have been obtained.

(15) Does your organization offer a leasing solution?  Please elaborate.

(16) Does your company have a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) GSA/NAC/SAC/BPA/NASA SEWP or any other Federal Government contract? If so, please provide the contract number(s).

(17) If you are an FSS GSA/NAC/SAC/BPA/NASA SEWP or any other Federal Government contract holder, are all the items/solutions you are providing information about available on your schedule/contract? Please state if all or some items are available on the contract.

(18) General pricing of your products/solution is encouraged. Pricing will be used for the purpose of market research only. It will not be used to evaluate for any type of award.

(19) Please provide your SAM.gov Unique Entity ID/Cage Code number.

Responses to this notice shall be submitted via email to Hestia.Sim@va.gov. Telephone responses will not be accepted.  Responses must be received no later than Thursday, April 23, 2026, by 10AM Pacific Local Time. 

All responses to this Sources Sought/RFI will be used for planning purposes only.  Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI are not considered a request to be added to a prospective bidders list or to receive a copy of the solicitation.  If further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcement is issued as a result of the information provided from this RFI, all interested parties must respond to the specific posting separately IAW the specifications of that announcement.

1. Identification of the agency and the contracting activity.
This justification was prepared in accordance with FAR 16.505 by the Federal Communications
Commission (FCC), Headquarters (HQ), Office of the Managing Director (OMO), Enterprise
Acquisition Center (EAC) located at 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554. The managing
program is the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (PSHSB).
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
The FCC requires acquisition of WireScreen Full Intelligence Platform, a brand name solution, to
enable advanced data analytics for identifying ownership, control, and influence of
communications companies, equipment, and services by foreign adversarial nations. This is a
new requirement under a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) task order. The acquisition will include a base
year and four option years to ensure continuity of service.
To effectively manage risks to the U.S. communications sector and all dependent critical 
infrastructure sectors and resources, the FCC requires an integrated solution enabling FCC staff 
to analyze data from disparate sources and identify entities, equipment, and services that are 
potentially owned, controlled, or influenced by foreign adversarial countries. 
The Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2021 directed the FCC to publish and 
update on its website a list of any communications equipment or service that poses an 
unacceptable risk to national security based on determinations made by executive branch 
interagency bodies, including the Federal Acquisition Security Council (FASC), the Department of 
Commerce pursuant to Executive Order No. 13873, or other national security agencies. 
Updating this list-particularly identifying subsidiaries and affiliates-requires access and 
analysis of official filings and public data from hundreds of thousands of sources in multiple 
formats. 
3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs (including the
estimated value).
Product: WireScreen Full Intelligence Platform
Description: WireScreen is a research database which provides access to data on China's
defense, technological, and economic landscapes, and combines cultural nuance with the latest
cutting edge software and data engineering to enable critical, actionable intelligence supporting
national security decisions. WireScreen's unique data structure reveals China's business
structures, economies, and supply chains, empowering analysts to effectively surface hidden
relationships, track complex ownership structures, prioritize targets for investigation, and
identify strategic linkages with China's defense sector and State-Owned Entities. WireScreen

offers a secure environment where user queries are not tracked and data is encrypted to ensure 
integrity. 
The information WireScreen provides through its solution is unavailable through others and 
enables the FCC to identify and characterize relationships between China-based companies 
doing business (i.e., producing, selling, and providing equipment and services) in the United 
States, China's government, or other international entities posing an unacceptable risk to 
national security.

U.S. Department of Justice 
Federal Bureau of Investigation 
 
 
 
Instructions to Offerors 
 
The proposal shall be clear, concise, and include sufficient detail for an effective evaluation 
and for substantiation of the validity of stated claims. The proposal should not simply rephrase 
or restate the Government's requirements but, rather, shall provide convincing rationale to 
address how the offeror intends to meet these requirements. Offerors shall assume that the 
Government has no prior knowledge of their facilities or experience and will base its 
evaluation on the information presented in the offeror's proposal. 
 
Submission Format 
The offeror’s proposal submission shall contain a cover letter and a technical volume. The use 
of hyperlinks in proposals is prohibited. Please see the following table for Volume naming 
conventions and page limits. 
 
Volume Title # of

Each volume shall be clearly identified; the pages numbered and contain the offeror’s name. 
Volume II, Price, may be submitted using Section 1 – Commodity or Services Schedule of this 
solicitation.  
 
Cover Letter 
 
Firms shall include a Cover Letter that is no more than two (2) pages total with their proposal 
submission that identifies the following: 
1. The RFP number 
2. Name and Address of the Company 
3. CAGE code and SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) 
4. Point of Contact Names, Phone Numbers, and E-mail Addresses 
5. Summary of the firm’s volumes that are being submitted for evaluation 
6. Acknowledgement of all amendments 
 
EVALUATION FACTORS 
 
VOLUME I, FACTOR 1: TECHNICAL PROPOSAL 
 
The Technical Proposal consists of three evaluation sub-factors: Sub-Factor 1 – Technical 
Approach, Sub-Factor 2 – Past Performance, and Sub-Factor 3 – Schedule. Each sub-factor is 
described in detail below. Collectively and individually, these elements must demonstrate the 


Offeror’s understanding of the requirements outlined in this RFP and the Offeror’s approach to 
executing this contract in accordance with the Statement of Work (SOW). The Technical Approach 
should not restate or paraphrase the SOW; instead, the Offeror must clearly articulate its 
understanding of the service requirements and describe how it intends to meet them. 
 
SUB-FACTOR 1: Technical Approach 
The Offeror shall present a comprehensive Technical Approach that includes, at a minimum, the 
following elements: 
• Team Organization 
• Demonstrate that all required key personnel identified in the SOW will be provided. 
• Acknowledgement the government has the right to deny any other proposed 
Key Personal after start of the project if they do not fit the original criteria 
listed in the SOW 
• Provide any professional certifications for the proposed Analysis Technician. 
 
SUB-FACTOR 2: Past Performance 
The Offeror shall demonstrate relevant past performance, including experience executing Vibration 
Analysis on similar systems of this size and scope.  
 
SUB-FACTOR 3: Schedule 
The Offeror shall provide a schedule that demonstrates its ability to perform Vibration Analysis 
and Evaluation semi-annually, including: 
• Commitment to completing the inspections in accordance with the SOW. 
VOLUME II, FACTOR 2: PRICE 
 
All Cost/Price information shall be addressed only within Section 1 – Commodity or Services 
Schedule of this solicitation. Proposals must set forth full, accurate, and complete information as 
required by this solicitation. The penalty for making false statements is prescribed in 18 U.S.C. 
§ 1001. 
 
 
BASIS FOR AWARD 
The acquisition evaluation will be conducted utilizing the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable 
process. As defined in the FAR, lowest price technically acceptable process represents an award made 
based on the lowest evaluated price of proposals meeting or exceeding the acceptability standards for 
non-price factors and past performance. The following criteria will be evaluated for all factors and sub-
factors: 
 
FACTOR 1: Technical - The term “technical,” as used herein, refers to the non-price elements 
listed below. Quotes will be rated as "Acceptable" or "Unacceptable" regarding their ability to 
meet each element. All elements must be acceptable for a quote to be considered for award.

("LPTA") evaluation method for this requirement. Trade -offs between cost/price and non - 
cost/price Elements are not permitted. The Government intends to award a firm fixed price

FEDERAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION 
 
CJIS DIVISION | RESOURCES MANAGEMENT SECTION 
 
  
 
 
 
 
Vibration Analysis & Ultrasound Testing  
For the  
CJIS Division  
 
Statement of Work 
4/14/2026 
 
 


2 | P a g e  
 
1 Scope 
This is a contract to provide Vibration and Ultrasound Analysis for the Heating, Ventilation, and Air 
Conditioning Systems to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) CJIS Division, Clarksburg, WV. This is a 
non-personal services contract. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over 
contractor employees performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be 
accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn is responsible to the Government. 
 
1.1 Description of Services/Introduction 
The CJIS Facilities Management Unit is requesting to establish a Five (5) Year (1 Base Year with Four (4) – 
1 Year Options contract for the Vibration Analysis and Ultrasound Analysis of the CJIS Complex Heating, 
Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Systems.  
 
1.2 Background 
Each year the CJIS Division obtains Vibration Analysis Servies for site equipment such as pumps, 
centrifugal chillers, reciprocation chillers, air handlers, cooling towers, and exhaust fans.  This has been 
conducted over the past several years.  With each analysis, a report/spreadsheet is prepared that 
included all data and readings collected.  The report details all anomalies detected and recommended 
corrective actions that are prioritized as to the severity of the anomaly.  The spreadsheets need to show 
a continuous data stream for each site visit for trending purposes of each piece of equipment tested.   
An ultrasound analysis program was implemented for the pneumatic (compressed air) systems in 
Buildings 0001A, 0002, 0003, & 0005.  These pneumatic systems provide the motive power to actuate 
the HVAC system automated controls (valves, dampers, etc.) that control the delivery of cooling to 
critical data processing equipment.  The ultrasound analysis program will detect compressed air leaks in 
these pneumatic systems that are too small to be detected audibly.  By detecting and repairing 
pneumatic systems failures early, major failures can be prevented from occurring and possibly impacting 
HVAC system operation.  The ultrasound analysis program will have the additional benefit of reducing 
pneumatic system energy consumption by reducing system air loss due to small, compressed air leaks.  
A Vibration analysis program was implemented for the mechanical systems in Buildings 0001, 0002, 
0003, 0005, & 0009.  These Mechanical systems provide the motive power to actuate the HVAC system 
automated controls (valves, dampers, etc.) that control the delivery of cooling to critical data processing 
equipment.  The vibration analysis program will detect equipment failure that is too small to be 
detected audibly.  By detecting and repairing mechanical systems failures early, major failures can be 
prevented from occurring and possibly impacting HVAC system operation.  The vibration analysis 
program will have the additional benefit of reducing maintenance system energy consumption by 
reducing system down time.   

  
3 | P a g e  
 
The technical data from the results is used to identify trends and changes detected in the equipment.  A 
database on each consecutive inspection is to be built and maintained by the contractor.    
2 Applicable Documents  
Not Applicable  
3 Requirements 
This request is to establish a Five (5) Years Contract (1 Base Year with Four – 1 Year Options) for the 
Vibration and Ultrasound Analysis of the CJIS Complex Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) 
Systems.  The services requested include the following: 
• Vibration Analysis and Evaluation of the CJIS Division’s Campus equipment performed as semi-
annual inspections on buildings 0001, 0002, 0003, 0005, & 0009 on the following:   
 
Building 0001 – Service Center - 4 pumps 
Building 0002 – Central Utility Plant - 59 pumps 
Building 0003 – Data Center - 8 pumps & 2 exhaust fans 
Building 0005 – Main Administrative Building – 6 exhaust fans 
Building 0009 – Biometric Technology Center (BTC) - 6 pumps 
 
• Ultrasound Analysis inspection of the CJIS Division’s Campus Pneumatic (compressed air) 
Systems, conducted semi-annually on buildings 0001A, 0002, 0003, & 0005 on the following:   
 
Building 0001A – Motor Pool Maintenance – Approximately 6250 sq ft building with 12 pieces of 
equipment, 1 Air Compressor, 9 Hose Reels, and pneumatic piping throughout. 
 
Building 0002 – Central Utility Plant – Approximately 64,000 sq ft building with 4 Air 
Compressors, 114 Actuators, 66 Valves, 2 Panels, and pneumatic piping throughout. 
 
Building 0003 – Data Center – Approximately 2500 sq ft mechanical room with 2 Air 
Compressors feeding another mechanical room directly above approximately 4000 sq ft with 23 
Valves & pneumatic piping throughout and feeding another mechanical room approximately 64

The additional ceiling will allow NRC to increase the ceiling on two existing task orders and issue a new task 
order so that the Contractor can perform the critical requirements for continued system support, regulatory fee 
billing operations, and required modernization of FAIMIS-related environments. These requirements are as 
follows: 
 
1) A new follow-on Fee Billing Operations and Maintenance (O&M) task order upon the completion of the 
initial implementation of the Fee Billing application on August 31, 2026. 
2) A new CLIN to support Go.gov implementation within the existing FAIMIS O&M Task Order. 
3) Upgrade of the FAIMIS-STAQS System Integration and Test (SIT) Environment under the SIT task order
. 
 
5. Authority:  
 
☒ FAR 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. 
6. Supporting Rationale: 
 
The following rationale supports the use of the authority cited in Section 5 of this document. See brand name 
description1 if applicable. 
 
☒  FAR 6.103 Rationale 
 
 
This modification being issued under the authority of FAR 6.103-1 “Only One Responsible Source and 
No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements,” Continued operations, 
maintenance, and modernization support are required for the NRC’s highly customized FAIMIS 
Momentum® ERP system. CGI Federal Inc. (CGI) is the only responsible source capable of providing 
this support without introducing significant risk to the agency’s financial management operations. 
 
The NRC’s FAIMIS environment includes extensive proprietary customizations—most notably the 
license fee billing capabilities that support complex, mission-critical billing functions. CGI is the original 
developer and implementer of these customizations and has continuously supported FAIMIS and the 
NRC’s eBilling solution since 2012. 
 
Due to the high utilization of the current IDIQ contract ceiling, the NRC is conducting market research 
with the intent to solicit and award a new contract for future FAIMIS support. However, the existing 
task orders and newly identified requirements are tightly integrated with the NRC’s customized 
FAIMIS environment and cannot be transitioned to another vendor without significant time and a major 
system overhaul. Any transition would likely require replacing the NRC’s financial management 
system and recreating all NRC‑specific customizations and interfaces, resulting in substantial 
duplication of cost, unacceptable delays, and considerable operational risk. 
 
Because the agency cannot complete a new procurement before the follow‑on work must begin, a 
ceiling increase is necessary to maintain continuity of operations and ensure that critical new 
requirements can be supported without disruption. The work requiring the ceiling increase consists of 
 
.

customized enhancements, continued O&M, modernization activities, and extensions of existing 
FAIMIS modules, all of which build directly on CGI’s prior tasks. These efforts constitute a follow-on to 
services already performed under the existing contract and cannot be performed by any other source 
without substantial disruption. The proprietary nature of the Momentum® ERP platform further 
requires that such updates be performed by CGI, the system developer, and the only entity with 
access to the proprietary components, architecture, and NRC-specific customizations. 
The NRC has made a significant long-term investment in developing, customizing, and maintaining its 
FAIMIS environment. Based on system dependencies, proprietary architecture, and the risk and cost 
associated with transitioning to a new vendor, CGI remains the only responsible source capable of 
meeting the agency’s immediate operational and modernization needs. Accordingly, proceeding with 
this action under FAR 6.103-1 is in the best interest of the Government, ensuring economy, efficiency, 
and uninterrupted mission-critical financial management operations. 
 
 
7. Market Research (MUST BE COMPLETED):  
 
Market research was not conducted for the ceiling increase but the NRC is in the early stages of 
market research to develop an acquisition strategy to replace the current FAIMIS IDIQ contract. 
However, the agency does not have sufficient time to solicit requirements, conduct transition 
activities, and onboard a new contractor before the immediate follow-on FAIMIS requirements must 
be performed. 
 
The NRC has determined that no other source is capable of assuming, transitioning, and 
successfully performing these highly customized and mission-critical FAIMIS services before the 
ceiling is required for the new critical requirements. Technical experts in OCFO determined that due 
to the proprietary nature of the system, other vendors cannot perform these functions without 
substantial duplication of cost, prolonged transition time, and unacceptable operational risk to 
financial management operations. 
 
Accordingly, a sole-source modification is necessary to maintain continuity of operations while the 
NRC completes a competitive acquisition. Proceeding with a ceiling increase modification ensures 
uninterrupted financial system performance and mitigates the significant risks associated with 
attempting to transition to a new vendor before the competitive procurement is finalized. 
 
 
8. A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, 
including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under 
5.202 applies. 
 
In accordance with FAR 6.103-1, this action is being conducted on a sole-source basis. As a result, offers 
were not solicited from multiple sources because the NRC has determined that only one responsible 
source, CGI Federal Inc. (CGI), is capable of performing the required FAIMIS services without 
unacceptable delay, substantial duplication of cost, or significant operational risk. A pre-solicitation notice 
for this ceiling -increase modification will be posted to the Governmentwide Point Entry (GPE) in 
accordance with FAR 5.101(a). 
The NRC is currently developing a full and open competitive acquisition for future FAIMIS support 
services. However, due to the immediate need to maintain continuity of operations during this interim 
period and the proprietary nature of the FAIMIS Momentum® ERP environment, it is not practicable to

solicit competition for this action. Competition will be pursued to the maximum extent practicable under 
the forthcoming competitive procurement. 
9. A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. 
 
The Contracting Officer will determine that the anticipated cost of this modification is fair and reasonable 
prior to award, consistent with the requirements of FAR 15.404. This determination will be based on 
evaluation of the contractor’s proposed pricing, including an assessment of labor categories, labor mix, 
hours, and level of effort for each requirement. 
The Contracting Officer will consult with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) to confirm the 
technical validity and reasonableness of the proposed level of effort to ensure that it accurately reflects 
the work necessary to meet the NRC’s requirements. 
To establish price reasonableness, the Contracting Officer will compare CGI’s proposed pricing with: 
• existing contractual rates under the FAIMIS IDIQ, 
• historical pricing for similar FAIMIS support services, and 
• the complexity and scope of the tasks associated with the ceiling increase. 
Upon completion of this review, the Contracting Officer will document the determination that the pricing 
for this modification is fair and reasonable and represents the best value to the Government. 
 
10. Any other facts to support justification.  
6.104-1(a)9 Justification content. 
(i) When 6.103-1 is cited for follow-on acquisitions as described in 6.103-1(c)(2), an estimate of the cost 
to the Government that would be duplicated and how the estimate was derived. 
(ii) When 6.103-2 is cited, data, estimated cost, or other rationale as to whether and how much the 
Government would be harmed. 
 
If the NRC were to transition the FAIMIS requirements to a new contractor at this time, the Government 
would incur substantial duplication of cost due to the proprietary Momentum ERP architecture and the 
extensive NRC specific customizations developed and maintained by CGI Federal since 2012. A new 
contractor would be required to: 
• conduct a full system discovery  
• recreate or redevelop NRC specific configurations, interfaces, and fee-billing logic; and  
• revalidate all financial system integrations to ensure compliance with Federal financial 
management requirements. 
Based on prior modernization efforts, historical FAIMIS implementation costs, and estimated labor hours 
required to redevelop the NRC’s custom Momentum environment, the NRC estimates that transitioning to 
a new contractor at this stage would result in an estimated $20 million in duplicated costs. This estimate 
reflects expected costs for system analysis, redevelopment, data mapping, interface reconstruction, 
integration testing, and recertification activities. These costs would be incurred before any new contractor 
could begin performing the follow-on work required under this action. 
 
Because these duplicated costs would not contribute to any new capability and would significantly exceed 
the cost of continuing performance under the current contract, a competitive transition at this time would 
not be in the best interest of the Government.

12. A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition 
before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required. 
 
The NRC recognizes the importance of promoting competition for future acquisitions. The primary barrier to 
competition for the current requirement is the highly customized and proprietary nature of the NRC’s FAIMIS 
implementation within the CGI Momentum® ERP environment. These system characteristics limit the ability of 
other vendors to assume support without significant transition time, cost duplication, or operational risk. 
To remove or reduce these barriers for subsequent acquisitions, the NRC is actively preparing to conduct a full 
and open competitive procurement for future FAIMIS support services. As part of this effort, the agency will 
evaluate opportunities to enhance documentation, standardize interfaces, assess alternative solutions, and 
identify potential strategies to increase the number of vendors capable of performing the work. The NRC will also 
develop a comprehensive acquisition strategy and timeline to ensure adequate time for competition. 
This limited-source modification is necessary only to maintain continuity of operations while the agency 
completes the planning and development activities required for the upcoming competitive procurement. The NRC 
is committed to restoring full competition as soon as practicable.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)
/ MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE

TFSC AI Modernization Initiative

Air Force Personnel Center (AFPC)

Draft Planning Document for Industry Engagement and Acquisition Planning

Release and distribution of this package should be coordinated with the cognizant contracting office prior to external dissemination.

1. Notice to Industry

This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes.

This notice is not a solicitation, not a Request for Proposal (RFP), not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), and not a commitment by the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for information received in response to this notice.

The Government seeks information from industry to better understand commercially available capabilities, implementation considerations, security and compliance approaches, integration patterns, sustainment models, and rough-order-of-magnitude planning factors relevant to the modernization of customer service operations supporting the Total Force Service Center (TFSC).

Responses to this RFI are for informational and planning purposes only. A response to this notice will not be considered an offer and will not be evaluated for contract award. The Government will not pay respondents for any information submitted or for any costs incurred in preparing a response. Any information submitted may be used by the Government in developing or refining requirements, acquisition strategy, and any future pre-solicitation or solicitation documentation.

Participation in this RFI is voluntary. The Government reserves the right to use or not use any information provided and is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of responses, provide feedback to respondents, or release the results of this market research effort.

2. Background

The Air Force Personnel Center (AFPC), located at Joint Base San Antonio–Randolph, Texas, provides personnel support and human resource services affecting a large Total Force population worldwide. One of AFPC’s critical service organizations is the Total Force Service Center (TFSC), which provides customer support across a range of personnel, benefits, and human resource-related inquiries for military members, civilians, retirees, veterans, and eligible family members.

AFPC is exploring options to modernize TFSC customer service capabilities through the use of advanced automation and artificial intelligence-enabled solutions. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, intelligent virtual agents, conversational AI, voice and chat automation, knowledge-based assistance, workflow automation, agent-assist capabilities, analytics, secure integration with enterprise systems, and scalable contact center operations suitable for government environments.

The Government is conducting market research to better understand existing industry capabilities, deployment models, security posture, implementation approaches, and associated risks or dependencies relevant to a potential future requirement.

3. Purpose

The purpose of this initiative is to refine and validate operational and technical requirements while assessing commercially available and emerging solution capabilities. It also aims to facilitate an understanding of hosting, integration, security, and compliance considerations. Furthermore, the objective is to identify implementation dependencies, risks, and best practices to inform the acquisition strategy and potential contract structure, and to develop a more accurate understanding of pricing and scaling considerations.

4. Scope of Interest

• Conversational AI for voice and digital channels.

• Natural language understanding and intent recognition.

• Intelligent virtual agents and chatbots.

• Voice automation and IVR modernization.

• Human-agent escalation and assisted service.

• Ticketing and workflow automation.

• Knowledge retrieval and response generation.

• Analytics, reporting, and performance monitoring.

• Integration with case management, CRM, telephony, and enterprise systems.

• Secure deployment in government or DAF-relevant environments.

• Scalability to support enterprise customer service operations.

5. Requested Information from Industry

Interested vendors are requested to provide written responses to the questionnaire in Attachment A and, where applicable, comments on the draft requirements contained in Attachment B.

Respondents are encouraged to describe currently available capabilities, clearly identify any functionality that remains on a future product roadmap, and distinguish between native product capabilities and partner-delivered or integrator-delivered services. Respondents should also identify assumptions, dependencies, implementation prerequisites, and any material limitations that may affect cost, schedule, security posture, or operational feasibility.

Where appropriate, respondents are encouraged to recommend clarifications, alternative approaches, or tradeoffs the Government should consider before finalizing operational or technical requirements.

6. Response Instructions

Interested vendors should submit a written response containing, at a minimum, the items listed below. Responses should be clear, concise, and tailored to the subject matter of this RFI. Proprietary or competition-sensitive information should be clearly marked.

• Company name.

• Primary point of contact.

• Email address and telephone number.

• CAGE code and DUNS number.

• Completed questionnaire responses.

• Comments on the draft requirements list / compliance matrix.

• Optional supporting materials, such as capability briefs, product sheets, architecture overviews, or relevant case studies.

Suggested formatting and administrative information:

.

Responses should be submitted electronically via email to the points of contact listed below no later than the response due date.

Primary POC: Shiri Avnet, shiri.avnet.1@us.af.mil

Alternate POC: Corey Collins, corey.collins.12@us.af.mil

Please format your response in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF and limit it to 20 pages.

The subject line of the email should read: "Response to RFI-FA701426-TFSC - [Your Company Name]".

7. Important Disclaimer

This RFI is issued for market research only. The Government is not requesting proposals, quotations, or bids at this time. No contract will be awarded as a result of this notice. The Government may use information received in response to this notice to support planning, requirement development, acquisition strategy development, and any future acquisition documentation.

If a future solicitation is issued, it will be announced through the appropriate contracting channels. External distribution of this market research package should be coordinated with the cognizant contracting office to ensure fair and consistent dissemination practices.

8. Attachments

This package includes the following attachments:

• Attachment A – Market Research Questionnaire

• Attachment B – Draft Vendor Requirements / Compliance Matrix

ATTACHMENT A

Market Research Questionnaire

I. General Vendor Information

SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION UNDER FEDERAL SUPPLY SCHEDULE
SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING 
ACTIVITY
Department of State 
Contracting Activity Acquisition Management
Requiring Activity Bureau of Economic, Energy, and Business Affairs (EEB)
SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING 
APPROVED
Approval is requested to solicit and award an order to KPMG LLP, 8350 Broad St, Suite 900, 
McClean, VA 22102, UEI MAA3SBDQVM1 under General Services Administration (GSA) 
Multiple Award Schedule (MAS): GS-00F-275CA for the supplies and/or services described in 
Section 3 on behalf of the Requiring Activity. 
The Government seeks to procure services that establish and operationalize a secure, compliant, 
and transparent financial monitoring mechanism that the selected contractor can deploy for the 
review, control, tracing, and validation of revenues associated with Venezuelan natural resource 
transactions and related fund disbursements, such as those from designated United States 
Department of the Treasury accounts (“U.S.-controlled accounts”) in accordance with 
Executive Order 14373. The resulting contract should furnish advisory and operational support 
that enables the DoS to exercise informed oversight, protect against fraud and corruption, and 
help ensure that funds benefit the Venezuelan people in accordance with U.S. foreign policy 
priorities.
A Time & Materials (T&M) award is anticipated.
SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE 
AGENCY’S NEEDS
The Government anticipates a complex operating environment at the intersection of diplomacy, 
financial management, sanctions compliance, commodity trading, and public-sector expenditure 
oversight. The contemplated mechanism must address risks associated with vetting inbound 
funds, oil sale transaction integrity, disbursement validation, foreign exchange (mis)use, tracing 
of outflows through the Central Bank of Venezuela (BCV) and other financial channels, and 
verification that downstream recipients use funds for authorized purposes.
SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED

Page 2 of 6
The Government therefore seeks the services of the selected contractor capable of designing, 
implementing, and sustaining a high- integrity financial oversight framework that can scale as 
needed and as transaction volumes increase and that can provide disbursement transparency and 
reliable data for policymakers, as well as evidence and documentation for executive and 
legislative stakeholders. 
 
The Contractor will, in consultation with the Government, deliver an integrated capability for the 
Venezuelan Revenue Transparency Mechanism that can strengthen governance, compliance, and 
program-level risk management; support the vetting of inflows, counterparties, budget requests, 
and downstream recipients; enable auditable tracing of disbursements and verification that 
downstream recipients use funds for authorized purposes; provide data-driven financial, forensic, 
and market analysis to detect revenue leakage or misuse; and establish repeatable processes, 
documentation standards, and reporting that support oversight and long- term financial 
sustainability. The contractor will provide all necessary personnel, materials, and services to 
perform the tasks outlined below, as requested by the Government. 
 Compliance and Risk Management 
 Inflow and Counterparty Vetting 
 Disbursement and Recipient Validation 
 Traceability, Auditing, and Verification 
 Commodity, Pricing, and Market Integrity 
 Data, Automation, and Reporting 
 Technical Advisory and Surge Support 
The estimated value for the entire period of performance including the one- year base and four 
one-year option years is up to $84,384,634.38. The pricing of KPMG is based on their negotiation 
and established labor rates under the GSA MAS, with a 4% discount offered to the DoS, based 
on the total value of the contract. 
SECTION 4: AUTHORITY AND SUPPORTING RATIONALE
This acquisition is conducted pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul 8.401(b) and 
General Services Acquisition Regulation 538.7104-3 (b) (ii): 
“Only one source is capable of providing the products, services, or solution required at the 
level of quality required because the products, services, or solutions are unique or highly 
specialized.” 
Managing Venezuelan natural resource revenue to promote urgent economic stability in 
Venezuela is a top U.S. foreign policy priority, with a critical need to establish a secure and 
transparent financial framework for the sale and distribution of revenue resulting from those
SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED

Page 3 of 6
transactions. Financial transactions are already underway to ensure liquidity in the Venezuelan 
economy and support critical government expenditures, making it especially urgent to hire a 
qualified and independent auditor immediately to help monitor transactions involving Foreign 
Government Deposit Fund accounts. There is only one auditing firm available under the MAS 
that (1) can meet the Government’s specialized requirements including experience with similar 
financial monitoring mechanisms, (2) acceptability to the Central Bank of Venezuela, and (3) 
ability to begin establishing the mechanism required almost immediately.
SECTION 5: DETERMINATION BY THE ORDERING ACTIVITY CONTRACTING 
OFFICER THAT THE CONTRACT ACTION REPRESENTS THE BEST VALUE 
CONSISTENT WITH FAR 8.305 
The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated price(s) will be fair and reasonable 
based on KPMG’s established price list through its GSA MAS and the logical connection 
between KPMG’s proposed labor hours and the efforts proposed, and that this represents the 
best value to the Department. DoS has compared KPMG’s cost proposal against the pricelist 
available through GSA and the reviewers confirmed KPMG has discounted their rates as agreed 
to through its existing GSA contract. Further, the Government verified that certain hourly rates 
outside of the MAS price list do reflect the rates typically paid in the commercial marketplace 
for the specific services and skill levels for which those rates are proposed. This is a time and 
materials contract, under which the scale of the contractor’s efforts will be determined by 
subsequent Government direction; therefore, our reasonableness evaluation focuses on the 
hourly rates and markups on ODCs the contractor is proposing. Further, the contractual costs 
will ultimately be borne by the Government of Venezuela as funding for the contract will be 
paid with proceeds from the sale of commodities to buyers or purchase of diluents from 
suppliers to Venezuela. 
By signing the justification, the Contracting Officer makes a determination that the cost of 
$84,384,634.38 to the Government is expected to be fair and reasonable.
SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED AMONG 
SCHEDULE HOLDERS AND THE RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON 
MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED 
Limited market research was conducted with firms to determine their capabilities and 
familiarity with the requirements of, and acceptability to, the Central Bank of Venezuela. The 
Government identified and contacted several firms believed to have relevant experience in 
international financial advisory and audit-related services. During this research, the 
Government assessed: 
1. Each firm’s prior experience providing services to, or in coordination with, central banks 
or comparable sovereign financial institutions. 
SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED

Page 4 of 6
2. The firm’s understanding of the regulatory, compliance, and operational environment 
applicable to the Central Bank of Venezuela and familiarity with key Venezuelan 
institutions and personnel 
3. The firm’s ability to initiate and perform work in a timely manner given the specific 
geopolitical, financial, and sanctions-related context. 
The results of this market research indicated that only one firm demonstrated (1) established 
acceptability to the Central Bank of Venezuela, (2) a proven ability to conduct business 
effectively with that institution under current conditions, and (3) the firm’s ability to begin 
establishing the required mechanism almost immediately and to initiate and perform work in a 
timely manner given the specific geopolitical, financial, and sanctions-related context. Based on 
this analysis, KPMG was selected as the potential vendor for the resultant contract. 
The principal barriers that led to restricted consideration in this acquisition are the requirement 
that the vendor be acceptable to, and operationally capable of doing business with, the Central 
Bank of Venezuela in a highly specialized and constrained environment, along with the 
requirement that it be able to begin work immediately. 
Before any subsequent acquisition for similar supplies or services is made, the agency may take 
the following actions to remove or reduce these barriers, to the extent practicable, provided that 
circumstances do not support continued sole-sourcing on the logical follow-on basis for 
restricting competition: 
1. Earlier Market Engagement: Conduct earlier and more extensive market research, 
including Requests for Information (RFIs) or Sources Sought notices, to identify 
additional firms that may be developing relevant capabilities and relationships with 
central banks or comparable entities. 
2. Periodic Market Surveillance: Periodically review the market (e.g., annually or prior to 
future requirements) to determine whether additional firms have gained relevant 
experience, obtained necessary approvals, or otherwise become acceptable to the Central 
Bank of Venezuela or similar clients. 
The Department will continue to examine capabilities of vendors in the future, as additional or 
new requirements, similar in nature, are identified. 
SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI): Session Border Controller (SBC) Network Solution


DESCRIPTION: This Request for Information (RFI) is for informational and market research purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not constitute a solicitation. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the U.S. Government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for the preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents is strictly voluntary.

The Directorate of Contracting, Test Range and Specialized Contracting Division at the Air Force Test Center (AFTC), Edwards Air Force Base, CA, 93524, is conducting market research. The purpose is to identify available and mature information system network or on-premise network solutions that include comprehensive life-cycle support. The AFTC would acquire the solution to issue as Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE) to small business contractors supporting the various service and research and development efforts for the AFTC.

BACKGROUND: The AFTC is seeking information on available information system network or on-premises solutions that include comprehensive life-cycle support. Such a solution, acquired by AFTC, would ensure that all Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)—whether provided by the government or generated by AFTC contractors and their subcontractors—resides on a government-owned platform. The express purpose is to maintain AFTC control over all contractor-related CUI.

This RFI explores a new paradigm where the responsibility for protecting Department of Defense (DoD) CUI remains with the DoD, rather than being distributed across multiple small business networks. Consequently, small business contractors using this AFTC-owned and furnished solution would not be subject to CMMC Level 2 assessment, as the CUI would reside on a government network, not a contractor network. This model is similar to existing networks, such as the one used by PEO Carriers, which centralizes all shipbuilding CUI on the PEO’s network instead of distributing it across contractor and subcontractor systems. Other similar networks are currently used to protect sensitive information in various fields.

The ideal solution would be comparable to the federal NIPRnet but offer greater flexibility to accommodate the diverse needs of small business contractors supporting the AFTC. The solution must provide life-cycle support compliant with NIST SP 800-53 and all other government requirements, encompassing hardware, firmware, software, provisioning, training, help-desk support, monitoring, and governance. Furthermore, the solution must meet all requirements for protecting ITAR and EAR data and be capable of qualifying for a DoD Authority to Operate (ATO).





SOLUTION REQUIREMENTS: Potential contractors with a comprehensive solution to the challenge described are requested to submit an entry in the attached spreadsheet, detailing how their solution meets the requirements below. These characteristics are intentionally open-ended to encourage unique and innovative proposals:

Scalable from a pilot program to tens of thousands of contractors.

Acquirable by the government in its entirety.

The network must contain contractor-generated and government-provided CUI while enabling small business contractors and their subcontractors to perform work on a wide range of contract deliverables for the AFTC, including manufacturing, software development/testing, R&D, and other services.

The solution must comply with NIST SP 800-53 and other government network requirements to ensure it is acceptable for acquisition and can achieve an ATO from the AFTC.

The solution must be a stand-alone, comprehensive solution that includes life-cycle services/support, training, governance, a helpdesk, monitoring, and all other related functions.

The solution must provide life-cycle support in the form of personnel and hardware/firmware/software. It should also include the knowledge and expertise to adapt the network to the needs of AFTC contractors and to remain compliant with AF IT acquisition and life-cycle requirements.

The stand-alone solution must comprehensively include all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to sustain the network or on-premises solution.

If a proposed solution has challenges in meeting the full requirements detailed in this RFI, respondents should provide suggested methods for overcoming those challenges.

INSTRUCTIONS:

INDUSTRY DAY (PENDING RESPONDENT INTEREST): Based on interest generated by this RFI, the AFTC may hold an industry pitch day. This event would serve to present the AFTC's mission and objectives for the anticipated services and to receive comments from industry. The government will determine whether to schedule an industry day after reviewing RFI responses.
WHERE: Virtual
WHEN: To Be Determined (TBD)

No contract will be awarded from this notice, and it is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. All submissions are voluntary, and the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred in responding to this market survey. The Government is not obligated to acknowledge receipt of any information or to provide feedback to respondents. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged.

Interested parties are requested to submit a capability statement demonstrating their experience in meeting all or part of the Solution Requirements. These statements should not be proposals, but rather a summary of the entity’s existing technical and management capabilities to perform the work as outlined. Respondents should clearly indicate which requirements their solution can meet. All submitted information must be in writing and contain sufficient detail to allow the government's technical representative to evaluate the state of the industry. All information is for market research purposes only and is provided on a voluntary basis.

Scope and Objective: The critical objective is to determine if secure network or on-premises information system solutions are available for procurement by the AFTC. These solutions would be for use by small business contractors and their subcontractors who provide a wide array of services and research and development efforts to the AFTC.

Purpose: This RFI supports market research being conducted by AFTC to identify the current state of the industry for network or on-premises solutions designed to protect DoD Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) that is provided to or generated by small business contractors and their subcontractors.

Requirements: See SOLUTION REQUIREMENTS.

a. Company name, UEI Number and CAGE Code, address, points of contact with phone number and email address.
b. Responses should be provided by completing Column B of the attached spreadsheet to illustrate the state of the industry for this type of solution. The information package must be clear, concise, and complete. The Air Force is under no obligation to provide feedback or contact any company for clarification.

Inquiries: Requests for further information will not be honored.

DARPA-SN-26-33
1
Request for Information
DARPA-SN-26-33
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
Tactical Technology Office
Responses due 15 May2026, by 4:00 PM Eastern Time (ET).  
This Request for Information (RFI) from the Defense Advanced Research Projects 
Agency (DARPA)’s Tactical Technology Office (TTO) seeks information regarding 
capabilities for the following two categories.  
1) Unmanned aerial vehicle (herein referred to as “drones”) in the Group 1-3 space 
with capabilities for fully autonomous launch, recovery, storage, organization, 
recharging/refueling, organization, internal logistics management, and pre/post-
flight checkout.  Proposed drone designs must form a mission-focused, 
collaborative constellation.  Responses must be cognizant of long endurance 
drone constellations with high operational availability and constellation 
management.  
When responding to this category, use Attachment 1 and follow instructions 
provided in the Requested Information section below. 
2) Storage containers (herein referred to as “containers”) that provide fully 
autonomous drone storage, logistics management, launch, recovery, and 
recharge/refuel, while conforming to the intention of a standardized military 
container (e.g. Conex, 463L pallets, Tricon, ISU container, etc.).  Innovative ideas 
and non-standard containers (e.g. suitcase-based distributed systems, box-based 
systems) will also be considered within the context of the presented approach, but 
solutions should be compatible with current military transport capabilities. It is 
envisioned that these containers shall be self-sufficient with consideration of 
energy storage, communication equipment, and compute capability. 
When responding to this category use Attachment 2 and follow instructions 
provided in the Requested Information section below. 
Participants may respond to either one or both categories described above using separate 
Attachments (provided).
RFI Responses may be used as a market analysis tool informing DARPA about potential 
vendors for a new program seeking to advance fully autonomous and containerized, 
deployment, sustainment, and operational support of unmanned autonomous platforms in 
the Group 1-3 space.  
BACKGROUND:
Existing commercial, airborne Group 1-3 platforms are limited in endurance, payload 
capacity, and onboard electrical auxiliary power.  When operated as constellations, they 

DARPA-SN-26-33
2
typically require substantial infrastructure and basing area for deployment and recovery. 
These constellations typically require human involvement to recover, recharge/refuel, and 
launch again, lacking full autonomy necessary to achieve sustained operations spanning 
days or longer. The landscape of current platform technologies has broad limitations that 
require evolution to achieve high-endurance constellations consisting of drones with 
meaningful payload Size Weight, Power, and Cost (SWaP-C) staged from fully 
autonomous containers capable of complete mission-cycle management inclusive of 
launch, sustainment/swap-out, and recovery.  
Example limitations include, but are not limited to:
- Drones
oElectric-based platforms have limited battery discharge depth and recharge 
cycle limits that restrict flight time and sortie numbers before substantial 
performance degradation manifests or battery-changes are required. 
oHybrid-electric solutions add weight and the complexity of onboard fuel-
storage, combustion, electric-machines, and high-voltage power transfer.
oBuoyant solutions often lack fine six degrees of freedom (6DOF) control 
and typically have lower onboard auxiliary electrical power available 
without the use of heavy batteries or large solar panels.  
oFixed wing platforms typically prohibit compact, autonomous 
launch/recovery solutions without requiring human intervention at some 
step and lack the ability to hold fixed spatial positions (not required but is 
a limitation of fixed wing).
- Containers
oExisting containers often rely upon a Differential Global Positioning 
System (DGPS) and cannot position themselves in GPS-denied 
environments.
oDeployable containers often lack internal volume allocations for 
communication equipment and fuel-storage necessary to sustain a 
constellation for multi-day continuous missions.
oWhile some constellation delivery solutions can unleash hundreds of 
drones in under a minute, these platforms often lack the ability to integrate 
external payloads, with their additional SWaP, that enable meaningful 
effects/surveillance. 
oSome container solutions provide internal volume sufficient for drones 
with meaningful payload-size but may lack the deployment and recovery 
tempo required to rapidly establish a persistent drone constellation of 
adequate density for the desired effect. 
oModern containers optimize designs around battery-powered drones 
(typically low range, low endurance) without payloads and are incapable 

DARPA-SN-26-33
3
of supporting alternative fuel-sourced platforms providing extended flight 
times necessary to achieve mission relevance. 
While sufficient for preplanned lightshows and commercial activities, further 
advancements are required to exploit constellation technologies in a high platform 
density and rapid deployment scenario. Full autonomy in launch, mission, recovery, 
post/pre-flight and re-launch in a continuous operational cycle for extended hours/days is 
desired. 
DARPA has identified an exigent need for highly deployable, versatile-SWaP Group 1-3 
platforms, operating in autonomous constellations that are stored within, deployed from, 
recovered in, and managed by a fully autonomous container, to support a variety of 
payloads and missions in GPS-denied environments.  Advancements in low-SWaP 
technologies enable constellations comprising a variety of novel payloads, each requiring 
dedicated power and weight, but capable of operating in synchrony across the 
constellation.  Constellation populations may comprise up to 500 platforms (number may 
vary as a function of payload type). Each platform will be equipped with a subsystem or 
independent payload system with the potential to achieve high operational availability for 
the combined system over multiple-day periods.
DARPA is looking for responses for U.S. manufactured and assembled drones in the 
Group 1-3 space and containers spanning current and future technologies to chart the 
mosaic of possibility in advancing autonomous constellation dynamics for the military.  
Novel configurations that enable multi-day continuous operations with their corollary 
constellation management software (ideally with path optimization and collision 
deconfliction) and innovative configurations of autonomous container-based deployment 
solutions are of particular interest to DARPA.  
Forthcoming technology development programs may leverage these RFI results to inform 
a new program. 
A mission-adjacent use-case involves a transportable container deployed to an austere, 
GPS-denied environment in suboptimal terrain or onboard a host platform that, upon 
remote operator inputs, activates and autonomously deploys a series of platforms 
launching from a single area (possibly serially). The platforms traverse some radius 
away, loiter on-station with an active payload (not all necessarily in the same location nor 
same payloads), and execute a mission before returning back to the launch area, 
autonomously recovering, recharging/refueling, and launching again to repeat the mission 
(without human intervention).  The platform quantity is determined by the particular 
effect, target, and mission. Thus, “constellation” may comprise any number above 2. 

DARPA-SN-26-33
4
Container size is limited by transportability, endurance, storage, and operability 
objectives. 
DESCRIPTION:
This RFI is looking for information on novel, U.S. manufactured and assembled, aerial 
platforms and containers, and performers that fundamentally enable:
- Autonomy Level 4 (no human participation required except for mission 
definition) for the system’s operation: 
oE.g., the operator issues a command, then the drones/constellation 
maintain level 4 autonomy 
- Long-constellation endurance (on the order of multiple days)
- Drones with continuous electrical power available to payloads, low-cost 
Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) construction, and sized for containerized 
storage
- Constellation management software (path optimization, collision avoidance 
planning, constellation reshaping/reorientation, formation flying)
- Autonomous container operation (inclusive but not limited to storage, launch, 
recovery, recharge/refuel, constellation communications, compute capability, 
multi-day fuel/energy storage, and constellation management software)
Responders are requested to provide tabular information on either existing or notional 
platforms that may satisfy this RFI in the attachments provided. 
REQUESTED INFORMATION: 
DARPA is interested in responses that provide information and insights related to core 
capability metrics. Response instructions are below.  
If responding ONLY to the “Drone” portion of the RFI, see RFI Attachment #1 and 
complete the Cover Page, Required Data Table, enter any optional Graphics, and use the 
Technical Description sections as required, entering any References on the last page.  Use 
Attachment #1 to capture all information for your response, keeping all responses to 5 
pages maximum (including references).  Do not modify Attachment #1’s layout or add 
pages to Attachment #1. Keep all responses to the maximum 5-page limit of Attachment 
#1. 
If responding ONLY to the “Container” portion of the RFI, see RFI Attachment #2 and 
complete the Cover Page, Required Data Table, enter any optional Graphics, and use the 
Technical Description sections as required, entering any References on the last page.  Use 
Attachment #2 to capture all information for your response, keeping all responses to 5 
pages maximum (including references).  Do not modify Attachment #2’s layout or add 

DARPA-SN-26-33
5
pages to Attachment #2. Keep all responses to the maximum 5-page limit of Attachment 
#2. 
If responding to both the “Drone” and “Container” portions of the RFI, complete both 
Attachment #1 and Attachment #2, per the respective attachment instructions, and submit 
both documents together.  
Responders are encouraged to provide information about an existing, exemplary system 
that fits this space, if available.  If none currently exists, responders are recommended to 
size appropriate systems based on their experience and abilities to populate information 
within the requested table below. The opportunity to list up to 2 bounding examples is 
provided within the tabular body of both Attachment #1 and Attachment #2 (up to 2 
examples for each attachment). Examples may be existing, proposed, or conceptual. 
SUBMISSION:
This announcement contains all information required to submit a response. No additional 
forms, kits, or other materials are needed.
Submissions in response to the RFI should be concise. Responders should submit a single 
integrated response addressing the areas described above. DARPA will only review 
submissions received as a Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx) file or unprotected Adobe 
Acrobat (.pdf) file. Each response is limited to the 5-page limit of each Attachment #1 
and Attachment #2 (total of up to 10 pages if both Attachments are submitted) using 12-
point font and 1-inch margins on 8.5-inch by 11-inch paper. Effective responses that can 
be provided in fewer than 5 pages are encouraged. 
574762
Attachment #1 and Attachment #2 include a template all responders are required to 
complete for their submission.  
SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS AND CONTACT INFORMATION
All unclassified responses to this RFI must be emailed to DARPA-SN-26-
33@darpa.mil. Responses will be accepted until 4 p.m. ET on 15 May, 2026. Early 
responses are encouraged. 
DO NOT SUBMIT CLASSIFIED INFORMATION TO THIS ADDRESS.
Please see Attachment 3 – Security to this notice for instructions on submitting classified 
information. 
All technical and administrative correspondence and questions regarding this RFI must 
be sent to the same email address. Emails pertaining to this RFI that are sent directly to 
individual DARPA program managers will not receive a response. No telephone inquiries 
will be accepted.

DARPA-SN-26-33
6
NOTE: DARPA may conduct discussions with individual respondents as necessary to 
gain a full understanding of the information submitted. 
DISCLAIMERS AND IMPORTANT NOTES:
This is an RFI issued solely for information and new program planning purposes; 
it does not constitute a formal solicitation for proposals or proposal abstracts. In 
accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot 
be accepted by the Government as such.  
DARPA will not provide reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to this 
RFI.  
If proprietary information is submitted, it must be appropriately and specifically 
marked. It is the submitter’s responsibility to clearly define to the Government 
what is considered proprietary data. Any proprietary information should clearly 
be labeled as “Proprietary.”  DARPA will not publicly disclose proprietary 
information obtained as a result of the RFI. To the full extent that it is protected 
pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act and other laws and regulations, 
information identified by a respondent as "Proprietary" will be appropriately 
controlled. Responses to this RFI will not be returned.
Respondents are advised that DARPA is under no obligation to acknowledge 
receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with 
respect to any information submitted under this RFI. Responses to this RFI do not 
bind DARPA to any further actions. 
DARPA will disclose submission contents only for the purpose of review. 
Submissions may be reviewed by the Government (DARPA and other 
Government partners), Federally Funded Research and Development Centers 
(FFRDCs), and Scientific, Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) support 
contractors bound by appropriate non-disclosure agreements.

Questions & Responses 
 
RFI 1.Please confirm an acceptable alternative for the lead commissioning agent qualifications 
(experience, education, commissioning background). ANSWER:  
A. 25+ years HV AC/BAS background: YES. 
B. Hands-on maintenance/repair experience: DOCUMENT AT LEAST 5 YEARS OF 
EXPERIENCE.

EXPERIENCE. 
D. Significant commissioning experience: "SIGNIFICANT" SHALL MEAN AT LEAST 5 
YEARS EXPERIENCE. 
RFI 2. Will a controls technician be available onsite, and does the O&M staff have a login for 
Metasys configuration and trending? ANSWER: 
There is no controls technician available at the project site. Staff has a log-in that allows 
configuration of alarms and trend logs. 
RFI 3. Clarify the RFP requirement for 2-point calibration and whether slope/intercept is 
applicable for thermistors.  ANSWER: 
Thermistors use non-linear lookup tables, so slope/intercept calibration is not meaningful; verify 
readings fall within acceptable error band and adjust offset if needed. Rtds or linear transmitters 
may use slope/intercept where applicable (e.g., heating water or outside air). 
RFI 4. Clarify whether the contractor is required to perform maintenance tasks in addition to 
retro-commissioning checklists. ANSWER: 
Item 8.2 refers to necessary site visits for contract completion. It is NOT intended to require 
general maintenance. Retro-commissioning checklists are expected; performing maintenance 
tasks is NOT.

SERDP and ESTCP Support
1     OBJECTIVE
The Strategic Environmental Research and Development Program (SERDP) and the 
Environmental Security Technology Certification Program (ESTCP) require program support to 
execute their missions of developing and demonstrating technologies that meet the Department of 
Defense (DoD) environmental and energy requirements. SERDP and ESTCP are separate 
programs that are managed through a joint program office. Support is needed at the program level 
and in each of the technical areas in which these programs invest. 
2     BACKGROUND
SERDP is a multi-agency research and development program that was established by Congress in 
1991. As described in Title 10, U.S.C. Sections 2901-2904, the major focus of SERDP is to 
"address environmental matters of concern to the Department of Defense and the Department of 
Energy through support for basic and applied research and development of technologies that can 
enhance the capabilities of the departments to meet their environmental obligations." SERDP 
supports environmental research and development activities in government, industry, and 
academic laboratories in the areas of Environmental Restoration, Munitions Response, Resource 
Conservation and Resilience, and Weapons Systems and Platforms.
ESTCP is a DoD demonstration and validation program for environmental, energy, and installation 
resilience technologies. The DoD established ESTCP in fiscal year 1995. ESTCP demonstrates 
and validates innovative technologies that target DoD's most urgent environmental, energy, and 
installation resilience needs and are projected to pay back the investment through cost savings, 
increased efficiency, and improved mission outcomes. The program provides funding to 
government, industry, and academic institutions to conduct demonstrations in the following six 
areas: Environmental Restoration, Installation Energy and Water, Munitions Response, Natural 
Hazards Adaptation, Resource Conservation and Resilience, and Weapons Systems and 
Platforms.
Details about the SERDP and ESTCP program structure, current projects, examples of solicitation 
documents, project requirements, and examples of program outreach can be found on the joint 
SERDP and ESTCP web site, https://serdp-estcp.mil/.

2026. The ceiling increase is necessary to avoid a gap in services critical to the Department of
