design services and not to be included in AE Consultants? 
 
VA’s Response: Yes, this commissioning contract is being solicited separately from AE 
design services. Commissioning services are not included in the AE scope of work. 
 
5. The description of project says that there is a 3D Mammography space as part of the 
project, is the equipment design selection to be by AE services/medical equipment 
planner or by VA department staff?

will select 3D Mammography equipment that will be used as a “basis of design”.

existing MRI equipment located adjacent to space?

1) Preventing 1st Floor existing MRI Magnetic Field from entering/ interfering with the 
new Mammography Suite and equipment. 
2) Preventing Basement Level  3D Mammography radiation (low-dose X-Ray) from 
interfering with MRI equipment above.

certification requirement?

certifications to address the shielding issues identified in RFI 5 above.

4. Authority for Contracting Without Competition Over $350,000
 
Up to and including $350,000
For this requirement up to $350,000, using simplified acquisition procedures under FAR part 13, the basis for contracting without 
providing for full and open competition is:  
Only one responsible source is reasonably available to meet Library requirements. 41 U.S.C. § 6101(b); FAR 13.106-1.

5. Rationale for Contracting Without Competition 
We are authorized to limit competition on the basis of the citation in section 4 because:  
 
The Library of Congress’s BIBFRAME Linked Data System (BFLDS) previously operated in tandem with Voyager and, as of 
June 2025, now interfaces with FOLIO as the Library’s system of record. BFLDS consists of the BIBFRAME database 
(BFDB), Linked Data Service (LDS ID), and the Marva editor, with LDS ID and BFDB built on the MarkLogic platform, 
which incorporates triplestore functionality. BFLDS and FOLIO were developed using distinct and not fully compatible 
architectures, requiring specialized middleware to enable efficient interoperability. 
Under contract LCLGD25C0002, IndexData conducted a comprehensive analysis, working directly with the original 
FOLIO developers, of how BFLDS and FOLIO can be integrated. This effort produced detailed, implementation-ready 
recommendations for middleware design, workflow optimization, and data exchange. 
 
IndexData is uniquely qualified to perform this work due to its direct role in both the design and development of FOLIO 
and the development of core components of BFLDS. As a result, IndexData possesses institutional and technical 
knowledge of system architecture, design decisions, and integration constraints that is not documented to a level 
sufficient for transfer to another contractor without additional time and cost. 
 
Awarding this requirement to another contractor would require the new contractor to independently reconstruct 
IndexData’s prior analysis, reverse-engineer design decisions across both systems, and develop equivalent expertise. 
This would result in significant duplication of effort, increased cost to the Government, and schedule delays. 
 
Accordingly, IndexData is the only responsible source capable of meeting the Library’s requirement within the required 
timeframe, without duplication of costs. 
6. Actions to Overcome Barriers to Competition Before Subsequent Contract Is Required  
To increase competition, we will: continue to survey the environment for possible expertise. 
 
7. Program Office Certification  
I certify that the description of the Government’s minimum needs, schedule requirements, and technical information that provide 
the basis for this justification are accurate and complete.

Use/relationship:   
 
The Status Report documents the status of contractor effort towards achieving contract 
objectives. It identifies accomplishments to date and difficulties encountered, and 
compare the status achieved to planned goals and the resources expended. It is used by 
the Government to monitor and evaluate contractor performance. 
 
This Data Item Description (DID) contains format and content preparation instructions 
for the data product generated by the specific and discrete task requirement as delineated 
in the contract. 
 
It is not intended that all requirements herein should be applied to every program. 
Portions of the DID are subject to tailoring by deletion depending on the specific 
status reporting requirements of the project.

REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) # 83310126Q0028 –  
 
Dear Vendors, 
 
This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format 
in Subpart 12.6 “Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items,” as 
supplemented with additional information included in this notice. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT 
CONSTITUTES THE ONLY SOLICITATION; A SEPARATE WRITTEN SOLICITATION WILL NOT BE ISSUED. 
 
This Request for Proposal (RFP/RFQ), with solicitation number 83310126Q0028, is in accordance with 
FAR Parts 12 and 13 and is in accordance with provisions and clauses effective in Federal Acquisition 
Circular (FAC) 2025-06 dated 10/01/2025. This solicitation is under NAICS code  541690 Other Scientific 
and Technical Consulting Services.   
 
Please send questions regarding the solicitation via email to Mark Jefferson at mark.jefferson@exim.gov 
and Mark Jefferson at Mark.Jefferson@exim.gov].

April -  4 PM EST).  Offers are to be submitted via e-mail to the Contracting Officer shown below, at the 
following -e-mail address,  mark.jefferson@exim.gov.  
 
Thank you in advance. We look forward to reviewing your quotes. 
 
Sincerely, 
Mark Jefferson 
Contracting Officer Office of Contract Services (OCS)

1. SUPPLIES OR SERVICES AND PRICE/COSTS - Schedule of Prices

The Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) has a need for an archive platform, to replace the 
existing Texworks platform (from Quilty Analytics LLC), as shown in the attached SOW.

3.1 Period of Performance: 
 
The Performance Period (PoP) of the contract to be awarded under this Solicitation is a five-year  
period commencing upon the date of the contract award. The PoP is comprised of the base year  
and four, one-year option periods.

4.2 Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR): 
Definitions:  
“Contracting Officer’s Representative” – The Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) is designated by 
the Contracting Officer, in writing, and is contract order specific. The COR is the technical representative 
for all technical requirements of the specific contract.  
“Contracting Officer” – The Contracting Officer (CO) is the exclusive agent of the Government with the 
authority to enter into and administer contracts. Thus, the CO has the responsibility to see that all 
requirements of the law and regulation are followed. However, as the CO’s representative, the COR is 
delegated the authority to monitor the technical effort being performed under the contract.  
The CO is the only individual with authority to enter into, administer, or terminate contracts. The CO 
ensures performance of all necessary actions for effecting contracting, ensuring compliance with the 
terms of the contract and safeguarding the interests of the United States in its contractual relationships.  
The COR is not authorized nor has authority to: 
• Award, agree to, or sign any contract, delivery order or task order. All contractual agreements, 
commitments, or modifications shall be made only by the CO. 
• Make any commitments or otherwise obligate the Government, or to make any changes to the 
contract. 
• Grant deviations from or waive any of the terms and conditions of the contract. 
• Impose or place a demand upon the contractor to perform any task or permit any substitution 
not specifically provided for in the contract.  
• Increase the dollar limit of the contract or authorize work beyond the dollar limit of the contract 
or authorize the expenditure of funds. 
• Give direction to the contractor or to the employees of the contractor except as provided for in 
the contract. 
• Change the period of performance. 
• Authorize the purchase of equipment, except as required under the contract. 

 
Solicitation No.: 83310126Q0018                                                                                                                                                                                   Page 4 of 5 
 
• Authorize the furnishing of Government property, except as required under the contract. 
• Authorize subcontracting or the use of consultants. 
• Approve shifts of funding between line items of the budget. 
• Approve travel and relocation expense over and above that provided for in the contract. 
• Authorize the use of overtime. 
When, in the opinion of the contractor, the COR requests effort outside the existing scope of work (or 
task order), the contractor shall promptly notify the contracting officer in writing. No action shall be 
taken by the contractor under such direction until the contracting officer has issued a modification to 
the contract or to the task order; or until the issue has been otherwise resolved by the CO. 
 
5.  CLAUSES 
Note- this procurement is being issued in accordance with FAR subpart 12. However, the Contracting 
Officer may replicate some of these schedule clauses or provisions in order to highlight their importance 
for this requirement. Applicable clauses are shown herein.  
FAR 52.239-1 -- Privacy or Security Safeguards (Aug. 1996) 
(a) The Contractor shall not publish or disclose in any manner, without the Contracting Officer’s written 
consent, the details of any safeguards either designed or developed by the Contractor under this 
contract or otherwise provided by the Government. 
(b) To the extent required to carry out a program of inspection to safeguard against threats and hazards 
to the security, integrity, and confidentiality of Government data, the Contractor shall afford the 
Government access to the Contractor’s facilities, installations, technical capabilities, operations, 
documentation, records, and databases. 
(c) If new or unanticipated threats or hazards are discovered by either the Government or the 
Contractor, or if existing safeguards have ceased to function, the discoverer shall immediately bring the 
situation to the attention of the other party. 
7.  LIST OF ATTACHMENTS  
The following Attachments are applicable to this solicitation (Samples shown below)  
• Statement of Work / Requirement Description  
• SF 1449  
 
8.  INSTRUCTIONS, CONDITIONS, AND NOTICES TO OFFERORS 
 
Note: All firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database 
@www.sam.gov to be considered for award. All Offers must be submitted in electronic format and 
emailed to Mark Jefferson at mark.jefferson@exim.gov and Naol.Fufa.ctr@exim.gov Contracting 
Specialist, at no later than the solicitation due date and time.  
 

 
Solicitation No.: 83310126Q0018                                                                                                                                                                                   Page 5 of 5 
 
Please send questions regarding the solicitation via e-mail to the POC’s shown above. If using email, it is 
the contractor’s responsibility to follow up with the listed POC to ensure their offer was received on 
time. Award may be based on initial responses. As such, offerors are highly encouraged to include their 
most advantageous pricing in their initial response. 
 
NO CORRECTIONS AND/OR CHANGES ARE ALLOWED AFTER DUE DATE AND TIME OF SUBMISSION OF 
OFFERS. 
 
8.1 Content and Format for Submission of Offer:  
Submit one (1) original complete response to this solicitation consisting of two (2) sections.  
Volume I: - Technical proposal.  
 
A brief narrative description of how the offeror’s proposed solution meets the technical requirements 
shown in the attached SOW, including migration from the existing platform to the new one. Prospective 
offerors are permitted to use standard data sheets, line cards, and brochures (in lieu) where suitable.  
 
Volume II: Pricing Information 
  
Pricing will be evaluated based on the total price reasonableness of the offer. The contractor shall 
submit a price proposal with the following minimum information:  
 
1. A completed version of SF1449 with all line items completed. Offers submitted without this will 
be determined non-responsive.  
2. Your own quote, with all pricing including a grand total, may also be included.  
3. % Discount from the offerors standard commercial market rates shall be indicated. 
 
9. EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD/BASIS OF AWARD      
 
9.1 Basis of Award 
 
Award shall be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to this solicitation, provides 
the overall best value to the Government, technical and price considered.  
(a) However, for an offeror to be considered for award, it must:  
1. Meet all technical requirements of this solicitation.  
2. Price must be consistent with and based upon the data provided in the Offeror’s Technical 
submittal.  
 
(a) Option Periods. 
The Government will evaluate Offerors for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to 
the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an Offeror is 
unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate 
the Government to exercise the option(s).

ADDENDUM to RFO 52.212-2 EVALUATION—COMMERCIAL ITEMS:

The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the offeror responsible whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government considering price and other factors.

The following factors shall be used to evaluate quotations: 

Factor I.  Technical capability or quality offered to meet the Government requirement

Factor II.  Price

Factor III. Past Performance

Evaluation Approach. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Government will use comparative analysis. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: 

Factor I. Technical capability or quality offered to meet the Government requirement: The quotation will be evaluated to the extent to which it can meet and/or exceed the Government’s requirements as outlined in the solicitation and based on the information requested in the instructions to quoters section of the solicitation. 

 

Factor II. Price: The Government will evaluate the price by adding the total of all line-item prices, including all options. The Government may use various price analysis techniques and procedures to make a price reasonableness determination. Offers that do not meet or exceed the technical capability or quality of the service offered to the Government requirement, as stated in Factor 1 shall not be selected regardless of price.

Factor III. Past Performance: The Offeror shall be evaluated on relevant/recent performance of past contracts and how well the offerors identified performance relates to the work being procured under the Performance Work Statement for this procurement. The following will be used to assess past performance.

Relevant past performance is defined as present/past performance effort involved similar scope and magnitude of effort and complexities this solicitation requires. Annual amount is used to determine similar scope and magnitude.

Recent past performance is defined as performance completed within the last three years or currently in progress.

The second aspect of the past performance evaluation is to determine how well the contractor performed on the contracts. The past performance evaluation performed in support of this evaluation does not establish, create, or change the existing record and history of the offeror's past performance on past contracts; rather, the past performance evaluation process gathers information from customers on how well the offeror performed those past contracts. The Evaluation Team will review this past performance information and determine the quality and usefulness as it applies to a performance confidence evaluation.

In the case of an offeror without a record of relevant past performance or for whom information on past performance is not available, the offeror may not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably on past performance. The Government may use other methods to evaluate past performance, including but not limited to review of CPARS.

If offeror does not provide all volumes as outlined in RFO 52.212-1 Instructions, the offer may be considered nonresponsive.

P.O. Box 5000 
Upton, NY 11973-5000 
 
managed by Brookhaven Science Associates 
for the U.S. Department of Energy  
 
 
STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Workday Human Capital Management System 
Subscription Renewal 
March 31, 2026 
 
 
    
 
   
    
    
    
    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
2 
 
1. INTRODUCTION 
 
Brookhaven Science Associates (BSA) is the management and operating contractor for the U.S. 
Department of Energy (DOE) at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL). BNL is a 
multidisciplinary research institution supporting advanced scientific discovery and operational 
excellence. 
 
As part of its digital modernization strategy, BSA transitioned from a legacy, internally 
developed Human Capital Management System (HCMS) to Workday Human Capital 
Management (Workday HCM), a cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform. Workday 
HCM has served as BSA’s enterprise system of record since its production deployment on 
September 23, 2023. 
 
This SOW defines the scope, requirements, and expectations for the renewal and potential 
expansion of Workday HCM services to ensure continuity of operations, system optimization, 
and scalability to meet evolving organizational needs. 
 
2. SCOPE 
2.1 Current Functional Modules in Use 
Workday HCM currently supports approximately 3,000 employees and includes the following functional 
areas: 
• Absence Management 
• Advanced Compensation 
• Benefits Administration 
• Compensation Management 
• Core Human Capital Management 
• Learning Management 
• Onboarding 
• Payroll (U.S.) 
• Recruiting 
• Talent Management 
• Time Tracking 
These modules support the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, development, 
compensation, time reporting, and separation. 
2.2 Subscription Renewal Requirements 
The Contractor shall provide: 

 
3 
 
• Continued subscription access to all currently licensed Workday HCM modules 
• System availability in accordance with Workday’s Service Level Agreements (SLAs) 
• Ongoing system updates, patches, and enhancements 
• Data hosting, backup, and disaster recovery services 
• Security controls compliant with federal and DOE requirements 
2.3 Optional Module Expansion 
BSA reserves the right to expand functionality through additional Workday modules, including but not 
limited to: 
• Workday Extend (application development platform) 
• Workday Help (case management and employee support) 
• Workday Journeys (employee experience workflows) 
• Workforce Planning (strategic workforce modeling and forecasting) 
• Workday Success Plans (WSP) Accelerate Plus (Enhanced technical support) 
Implementation of additional modules may be executed under this SOW. 
2.4 Tenant and Environment Requirements 
BSA requires multiple Workday tenants to support development, testing, and production operations. 
Current and future needs include: 
• Existing Production Tenant (e.g., BNL5) 
• Additional Implementation Tenants (minimum of two) 
• Sandbox and testing environments as required 
The Contractor shall ensure proper provisioning, maintenance, and synchronization of these 
environments. 
3. DELIVERABLES 
The Contractor shall deliver continuous access to the Workday HCM platform along with all associated 
services required to maintain system functionality and performance. This includes ensuring system 
availability in accordance with SLAs, providing regular system updates and release management, and 
maintaining documentation related to system changes and enhancements. 
The Contractor shall also provide support services for incident resolution and service requests, ensuring 
that issues are addressed in a timely and effective manner to minimize disruption to BSA operations. 
4. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS (SLAs) 
The Workday HCM system must meet defined performance and availability standards to support 
mission-critical operations at BNL. The Contractor shall ensure system uptime of no less than 99.7 
percent, excluding scheduled maintenance windows. 

 
4 
 
In addition, the Contractor shall provide timely responses to incidents based on severity levels, maintain 
acceptable system response times consistent with industry SaaS benchmarks, and ensure that data 
backup and recovery processes meet established standards for reliability and continuity of operations. 
5. SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE 
The Contractor shall implement and maintain security controls consistent with federal and DOE 
requirements. All data must be encrypted both at rest and in transit, and access to the system must be 
governed through role-based access controls. 
The system must support audit logging and monitoring to ensure accountability and traceability of 
system activities. 
BSA retains full ownership of all data within the Workday system. The Contractor shall not access, use, 
or disclose BSA data except as required to perform services under this scope. 
6. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
The Contractor is responsible for delivering and supporting the Workday SaaS platform, including 
coordination of infrastructure, system availability, security, and ongoing updates in alignment with 
Workday’s standards and services. The Contractor shall also provide customer support services, 
including defined escalation procedures for critical issues. 
BSA is responsible for system configuration, business process management, user access administration, 
and oversight of integrations with other enterprise systems.  
7. GOVERNANCE AND SUPPORT 
The Contractor shall provide a structured support model that includes defined service tiers, escalation 
paths, and communication protocols. Regular communication regarding system updates, releases, and 
potential impacts shall be provided to BSA. 
The Contractor shall work collaboratively with BSA to ensure alignment on system changes, issue 
resolution, and continuous improvement efforts.

Statement of Work 
KERMIT Mounting Plate  
Period of Performance: Task Order Issuance – June 30, 2027 
 
Contract Overview  
The International Space Station (ISS) Program has a requirement for a new mounting plate for 
the KEyence Research MIcroscope Testbed (KERMIT).  The KERMIT is a commercial off-the-
shelf microscope that provides researchers with fundamental microscope capabilities, including 
state-of-the-art imaging and analysis modules.  KERMIT provides the ability to perform 
advanced microscopy during spaceflight and remotely from the ground.  KERMIT is designed to 
streamline image collection and analysis through a single platform. The images collected from 
KERMIT are transferred to operators on the ground without having to wait for a return vehicle.  
KERMIT is currently installed into the Materials Science Research Rack (MSRR) on the ISS.  
The MSRR will soon be removed, and the KERMIT will be installed into a Basic EXPRESS 
Rack. 
 
The scope shall encompass all activities required to design, fabricate, certify for flight, and 
install a new mounting plate for the KERMIT Head Unit and Control Box.  
 
DOCUMENTS 
 
Applicable Documents 
 
Document # Title 
SSP 57000 Pressurized Payload Interface Requirements Document (IRD) for 
International Space Station (ISS) 
SSP 57057 ISS Science, Technology, and Exploration Integration Flow 
SSP 51721 ISS Safety Requirements Document 
SSP 30599 ISS Safety Review Process 
SSP 52054 CoFR Implementation Plan 
OZ-23-048 PD Expectations Letter 
 
Reference Documents 
 
Document # Title 
KERMITMOUNT KERMIT Mounting Plate Assembly 
IC-4108 KERMIT Microscope Relocation Topology Assessment 
 
  

 
REQUIREMENTS  
 
The Contractor shall provide the necessary resources (except for those identified as Government 
Furnished Equipment/Property on this TO) to perform the following tasks/requirements to 
design, manufacture, certify for flight, and install the KERMIT Mounting Plate:  
 
1.  The Contractor shall be responsible for the design of the KERMIT Mounting Plate to fit 
in a Basic EXPRESS Rack (BER).  
2. The KERMIT Mounting Plate shall be made to isolate the KERMIT Head Unit and 
Control Box from outside vibrations. 
3. The Contractor shall be responsible for the design, development, and fabrication of the 
KERMIT Mounting Plate.   
4. The Contractor shall produce fabrication and installation drawings of the KERMIT 
Mounting Plate. 
5.  The Contractor shall maintain a project schedule and report updates monthly at a 
minimum or as changes occur. 
6. Console Reports – The Contractor shall submit a report of on-orbit operations within 
48hrs of operations. 
7. The Contractor shall define their proposed resources, including facility needs for ground 
testing and flight operations support in their proposal. 
8. The Contractor shall provide engineering support, near real-time on-call support during 
KERMIT Mounting Plate installation, provide engineering analysis, and resolve 
anomalies and/or failures of KERMIT Mounting Plate.  Anomaly resolution will require 
interactions with the Mission Evaluation Room (MER) and Payload Operations and 
Integration Center (POIC). 
9. The Contractor shall define and deliver their proposed solution to addressing any on-orbit 
hazard controls for KERMIT Mounting Plate and plans to mitigate any hazards.  This 
includes the completion of Safety Phase 0-3.   
10. Contractor shall develop and deliver a Flight Certification that states all requirements 
(safety and interface) have been met and the payload/sample is safe and ready to launch 
and operate on the ISS for each flight.   
a. Documentation that supports this Flight Certification shall be in the Contractor’s 
best practices format and content and will be retained for the duration of the task 
order 
b. The Flight Certification Statement shall meet the requirements defined in the OZ

Immunization Coverage Reporting & GPRA Optimization 
1 
 
Sources Sought Notice 
Title:  Immunization Coverage Reporting & GPRA Optimization  
Agency:  Indian Health Service  
Issue Date:  April 13, 2026 
Due Date:  April 23, 2026, no later than 5:00pm EST 
Contacts:  Responses must be submitted via email to cynthia.cason@ihs.gov and include “GPRA 
Optimization – Your Company Name” in the Subject of the email. 
 
This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for market re search and planning purpos es only and shall not be 
construed as a solicitation or an obligation or comm itment to issue a solicitation by the Indian Health 
Service (IHS). This SSN is seeking information from the specific types of ent ities listed below to assess 
their capabilities in fulfilling the requirements set forth in this SSN. The information from this SSN will be 
used to determine the appropriate set-aside, if any, in accordance with the applicable regulations listed. The 
Government encourages the identified to respond to this Notice and be assessed of their capabilities in the 
following priority: 
 
1. Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEE) 
2. Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE) in accordance with HHSAR 326.603-1 
3. Small business concerns in accordance with FAR 19.502-2 (b)(1) & (2) 
 
Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in dete rmining the appropriate 
acquisition method, including whether any ISBEE/IEE or small business set-aside is possible based on the 
Contracting Officer’s reasonable expectation of obtainin g offers from two or more relevant concerns that 
will be competitive in terms of market price, product quality, and delivery capability. An organization that 
is not considered an ISBEE/IEE firm OR small business under the applicable NAICS code should 
NOT submit a response to this notice. The applicable primary NAICS code for this requirement is 541611 
– Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services. The anticipated period 
of performance for this effort will be approxi mately one year from the date of award. Generic capability 
statements are not sufficient and may not be cons idered when assessing enti ty capabilities. Please 
reference the Submission Information further below. 
 
Background and Objectives 
(see details regarding the scope of work further below) 
The purpose of this project is to improve immuni zation coverage rates by enhancing understanding, 
consistency, and utilization of immunization reporting systems across the enterprise. The systems outlined 
below are used at multiple levels within the Indi an Health Service (IHS) federal facilities, including 
Headquarters (HQ), Area Offices, and Service Units (lo cal hospitals, clinics, and health centers serving 
American Indian and Alaska Native populations). Primary users include providers (physicians, nurses, and 
pharmacists), immunization program staff, qua lity improvement personnel, Area Immunization 
Coordinators, and national leadership.  
 
Key systems and regulations included in the scope of this effort are: 
 Government Performance and Results Act (GPR A): Federally mandated performance measures, 
including those measuring immunization coverage  
 Clinical Reporting System (CRS): Extracts clinical quality data from RPMS for GPRA and related 
reporting  
 Population Management Tool (iCARE): Helps pr oviders efficiently manage the care of their 
patients 

  
Sources Sought Notice 
Immunization Coverage Reporting & GPRA Optimization 
2 
 
 Resource and Patient Management System (RPMS) : Electronic health record capturing patient-
level data  
 National Immunization Reporting System (NIRS) / National Vaccine Coverage (NVC) Dashboard: 
Enterprise tools for aggregating and visualizing coverage data 
 
These systems are all interconnected, as data generates from RPMS and measures immunization coverage, 
vaccine uptake, missed opportunities, and GPRA-relate d clinical quality indicators. Currently, system use 
is inconsistent across the enterprise due to unclear guida nce, variation in interpretation, and differences in 
data definitions and outputs. This leads to confusion, reduced confidence in data, and missed opportunities 
to improve vaccination coverage. Additionally, federal reporting re quirements (e.g., GPRA) require 
accurate and consistent data use. 
 
This project will develop a standardized, actionable framework, end-user guidance, and training to support 
service units and stakeholders in effectively using immunization data systems. These outputs are intended 
for broad use across service units nationwide, suppor ting providers, program staff, and leadership. 
Improved clarity and standardization will strengthen data integrity, improve identification of coverage gaps, 
and support targeted interventions to increase immunization coverage rates. 
 
Capability Statement/Submission Information 
A response to this SSN will be in the form of a capability statement to demonstrate capability and experience 
in the task areas identified further below. Specifical ly, please provide the following information below to 
demonstrate capabilities: 
 
Cover Page 
Please provide a cover page to include: 
1. Company Name 
2. Company Designation (ISBEE/IEE/SB)  
3. Type of Business – as applicable (e.g. 8(a), Woman Owned Small Business, HUBZone, etc.) 
4. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number 
5. Point of contact, email address, and phone number 
6. Primary NAICS Code(s) 
7. Existing federal contracting vehicle(s) num bers, as applicable (e.g. GSA MAS number, 
NITAAC/CIO SP3, OASIS, Alliant 2, or other Government Wide Agency Contracts, etc.) 
8. System for Award Management (SAM) registration status. Note, all respondents must be registered 
on SAM, located at http://www.sam.gov/ prior to any potential award. 
 
Executive Summary 
Provide a high-level overview of your services and include how it will benefit the Indian Health Service. 
 
Technical Areas 
Respondents are expected to submit a capab ility statement detailing and demonstrating their 
expertise and technical capabilities in the areas outlined further below in this SSN. 
 
Past Performance 
Please provide any past performance information to  support demonstration of your capabilities in the 
relevant technical areas and magnitude of work. 
 
Representation 
If identifying as an IEE/ISBEE, provide with your r esponse to this notice a completed Indian Economic 
Enterprise Representation Form (attached) 

  
Sources Sought Notice 
Immunization Coverage Reporting & GPRA Optimization 
3 
 
 
Other Information (Optional) 
You may include any other information that may be helpful in developing or finalizing the requirements of 
the potential acquisition. 
 
Submission Format 
To assist the Government in an expeditious review of your capabilities, the capability statement should be 
organized as follows: 
 Cover page 
 Executive Summary 
 Technical Areas in the order listed 
 Past Performance 
 Other Information, as applicable 
 
The tailored capability statement should not exceed 10 pages excluding Past Performance 
information. Font must not be less than 10-point and may be submitted in either in either Microsoft Word 
or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) but must  be a standard 8-1/2 by 11 inch paper size. All 
proprietary information should be marked as such.  
 
Generic capability statements are not sufficient and will not be considered compliant with the 
requirements of this notice. 
 
Disclaimer and Important Notes  
This notice does not obligate the Government to awar d a contract. Any information provided by industry 
to the Government as a result of this SSN is stri ctly voluntary. Responses will not be returned. No 
entitlements to payment of direct or indirect costs or  charges to the Government will arise as a result of 
contractor submission of responses or the Government's use of such information. The Government reserves 
the right to use information provided by responde nts for any purpose deem ed necessary and legally 
appropriate. Any organization respondi ng to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and 
sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to de termine the organization’s capabilities to perform the 
work. Respondents are advised that the Government is  under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the 
information received or provide feedback to responden ts with respect to any in formation submitted. After 
a review of the responses received, a pre-solic itation synopsis and solicita tion may be published on a 
government GPE. However, responses to this Notice will not be considered adequate responses to any 
resultant solicitation. 
 
Confidentiality. No classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. 
The Government reserves the right to use any non-pr oprietary technical information in any resultant 
solicitation(s).  
 
Thank you for your interest in IHS programs.  
 
Scope of Work 
The contractor shall provide project management, subject matter coordination, process mapping, and 
documentation development to achieve the following: 
 
Task 1: Project Planning and Stakeholder Engagement 
 Develop and outline specific project workplan and timeline with a Project Management Plan 
 Identify key stakeholders in a Stakeholder Engagement Summary and engage key stakeholders  
 Conduct kickoff and recurring status meetings 

  
Sources Sought Notice 
Immunization Coverage Reporting & GPRA Optimization 
4 
 
 
Task 2: System and Data Source Analysis 
 Analyze immunization reporting systems in c oordination with the HQ immunization team 
including: 
o GPRA 
o CRS 
o iCARE 
o RPMS 
o NIRS/NVC dashboard 
 Document in a Systems Analysis Report: 
o What each system measures 
o Data sources and methodologies 
o Reporting frequency and outputs 
o Limitations and caveats 
 
Task 3: Current State Assessment 
 Identify how reports are currently used at local, area, and national levels 
 Assess gaps, redundancies, and inconsistencies 
 Identify inappropriate or outdated reporting practices 
 Document findings in a Current State Assessment Report 
 
Task 4: Process Mapping 
 Develop end-to-end process maps for immunization reporting and data flow 
 Include decision trees and use-case scenarios 
 Clarify role delineation across levels 
 Document findings in Process Maps and Decision Trees 
 
Task 5: SME Engagement and Validation in Coordination with HQ immunization team  
 Conduct structured interviews and workshops with  subject matter experts (to include IHS HQ 
Immunization Coordinators and Immunization Prog ram contacts) to discuss and validate findings 
from Tasks 2 through 4 and build consensus on best practices 
 
Task 6: Development of Guidance and Tools 
 Create standardized guidance on: 
o When and how to use each reporting system 
o Best practices for improving coverage rates 
 Develop a comprehensive User Operations Guide, which ensures accessibility and usability of each 
key system, for service units and end users including: 
o Flowcharts 
o 
Templates 
o Example reports and screenshots 
o Step-by-step workflows showing how providers and program staff should use the data and 
reports to identify gaps, target interv entions, monitor performance, and improve 
immunization coverage rates 
o Practical examples and step-by-step instructions 
 
Task 7: Training Development and Delivery 
 Develop a training approach/plan for providers, pr ogram staff, and relevant end users on how to 
use the data systems, reports, and guidance products produced from Task 6 

  
Sources Sought Notice 
Immunization Coverage Reporting & GPRA Optimization 
5 
 
 Create step-by-step training, designed to address different learning modalities, including: 
1) a self-paced training module that end-users can take independently and 
2) a guide/curriculum for use by the HQ immuniza tion team to conduct instructor-led in-
person and virtual trainings 
 The training should explain: 
o How to access each report or product 
o How to interpret the data correctly 
o How to identify coverage gaps and missed opportunities 
o How to use the informati on to inform outreach, recall, quality improvement, and 
operational decisions 
o How to monitor progress over time using the appropriate tools 
 Develop training products, which may include: 
o Instructor guide 
o Participant workbook or quick reference guide 
o Slide deck 
o Job aids 
o Case studies and practice scenarios 
 Deliver virtual sessions to HQ immunization team informing how they should present the training 
to end-users 
 Refine training materials based on HQ immunizati on team feedback and provide final training 
package for future use 
 
Task 8: Recommendations and Final Deliverables 
 Provide actionable recommendations for improving  immunization coverage reporting and usage 
via a final briefing and written final report 
 
Deliverables 
1. Project Management Plan - Reference Task 1 
2. Stakeholder Engagement Summary – Reference Task 1 
3. System Analysis Report – Reference Task 2 
4. Current State Assessment Report – Reference Task 3 
5. Process Maps and Decision Trees – Reference Task 4 
6. Standardized Reporting Guidance and User Operations Guide – Reference Task 6 
7. Training Plan and Training Materials/Products – Reference Task 7 
8. Final Recommendations Report and Briefing – Reference Task 8 
 
Period and Place of Performance 
Estimated period of performance: June 30, 2026 – August 29, 2027 
The contract will be performed off-site, at contractor’s facility/place of work. 
 
Government Furnished Information and Property 
The Government will provide access to relevant reporting systems and documentation, access to SMEs and 
stakeholders, and access to relevant existing reports and data sources. 
No Government-Furnished Property (GFP) will be provided under this contract. 
 
Travel 
No travel is required or included in this contract. Should travel become necessary, it shall be in accordance 
with Federal Travel Regulations a nd must be approved in advance by the Contracting Officer and COR 
before any costs are incurred. 
 

  
Sources Sought Notice 
Immunization Coverage Reporting & GPRA Optimization 
6 
 
Special Considerations 
 Coordination across multiple organizational levels is critical 
 Sensitivity to data governance and reporting requirements

The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) is a federal agency within the U.S. 
Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) dedicated to fostering health and well-
being by providing federal leadership, partnership, and resources for the compassionate 
and effective delivery of human services. ACF serves families, children, youth, individuals, 
and communities through funding, policy direction, training, technical assistance, and 
information services. 
The Office of Head Start (OHS), part of ACF, promotes school readiness of young children 
from low-income families by enhancing their cognitive, social, and emotional 
development. OHS provides operating grants to local public and private organizations to 
deliver comprehensive child development services to low-income children (ages birth to 
five years) and their families. 
This acquisition establishes contract support to provide customer service, grants 
management assistance, and data management services in direct support of the ACF and 
OHS missions. The Contractor shall deliver responsive and efficient customer service to 
grant recipients to and in support of federal staff, streamline and support grants

vulnerable populations, including low-income children and families and at-risk youth. 
Founded in 1965, the Head Start program provides comprehensive child development 
services to low-income children and their families. Head Start programs promote school 
readiness by enhancing social and cognitive development of children through educational, 
health, nutritional, social, and other services. Head Start programs engage parents in their

1. Contracting Agency: United States Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal 
Railroad Administration (FRA), Office of Acquisition (RAD-30), 1200 New Jersey, 
Avenue, SE Washington, DC 20590. 
2. Action to be Approved: The FRA awarded a contract to MITRE Corporation for “Rail 
Information Sharing Environment (RISE) Program Development Support Services” without full 
and open competition on September 26, 2024. The current action is a continuation of the subject 
contract 693JJ624C000049 to complete the work outlined in the base award. While the 
foundational work for the subject contract 693JJ624C000049, including a landscape assessment, 
program roadmap, founding documentation, and a technical report of RISE program activities, 
had been completed, much of the developmental work to mature RISE as a data trust, complete 
a demonstration, and engage stakeholders had not been completed. Therefore, it is necessary to 
complete the additional requirements. Due to unforeseen delays in the approval process to 
exercise the option in the original contract, the period of performance for the subject contract 
693JJ624C000049 ended on March 29, 2025. Final approval to continue the work outlined 
herein was received on February 4, 2026. Therefore, a new contract is requested.  
3. Description of Services: FRA requires a contractor to perform the following: (1) Advance and 
mature RISE as a data trust for the railroad industry, consistent with the DOT Order on Data 
Trusts; (2) Demonstrate RISE value through tar geted projects, measurable data-driven 
outcomes, and stakeholder use cases; and, (3) Promote coordination and information exchange 
among industry participants and stakeholders to enhance safety and effectiveness. 
The to tal estimated value of this requirement is $3,000,000.00.  
4. Authority Cited: The statutory authority for this non-competitive action is derived from 41 
U.S.C. § 3304(a)(3), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-3 
“Industrial mobilization; engineering, developmental, or research capability; or expert services.” 
and FAR 6.302-3 (a)(2)(ii) “Competition need not be provided…t o establish or maintain an 
essential engineering, research, or development capability to be provided by an educational or 
other nonprofit institution or a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC).” 
5. A Demonstration that the Proposed Contractor’s Unique Qualifications or the Nature of the 
Acquisition Requires Use of the Authority Cited: FRA has a requirement for program 
development support for RISE. FRA conducted market research on data trust program 
development and found MITRE Corporation. MITRE operates six federally funded research and 
development centers and is a leading expert and possesses unique expertise in transportation. As 


  
such, the statutory authority implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-3, 
“(FAR) 6.302-3 Industrial mobilization; engineering, developmental, or research capability; or 
expert services.” is applicable to this proposed acquisition because MITRE Corporation will 
perform the work through one of its federally funded research and development centers. MITRE 
has noted expertise in the establishment and development of two existing DOT data trusts for 
DOT, Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) Aviation Safety Information Analysis and 
Sharing (ASIAS) program and National Highway Transportation Safety Administration’s 
(NHTSA) Partnership for Analytics Research in Traffic Safety (PARTS) programs in which 
MITRE has served as the Program Developer. If this J&A is not approved and, consequently, the 
required service not provided, then FRA’s RISE program will not fulfill its mission to address 
complex railroad safety challenges through data sharing and collaboration with railroad 
stakeholders and will ultimately be unable to further FRA’s overall mission to enable the safe, 
reliable, and efficient movement of people and goods for a strong America, now and in the future. 
 
6. Description of the Effort Made to Ensure that Offers are Solicited from as many Potential 
Sources as Practicable: In accordance with the exception provided in FAR 5.202(a)(10), the 
Contracting Officer need not submit a notice of a proposed contract action when “the 
proposed contract action is made under conditions described in FAR 6.302-3 a
nd  advance notice 
is not appropriate or reasonable.” 
7. Determination by the Contracting Officer that the Anticipated Cost to the Government will 
be fair and reasonable: The Contracting Officer determines that the anticipated cost will be fair 
and reasonable based on market research, previous acquisition history on similar requirements at 
DOT, and a price analysis that the Contracting Officer will conduct on the Contractor’s quotation 
using a combination of the techniques provided under FAR Subpart 15.404-1. 
8. Market Research: Market research methods used include conversations and interviews with 
Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs) on similar 
requirements of NHTSA’s PARTS and FAA’s ASIAS, and discussions with MITRE to determine 
their capabilities. After thorough analysis, FRA has determined that MITRE, as an expert in the 
program development of data trusts within DOT, is the most qualified vendor this requirement. 
9. Other Facts Supporting the Use of Other Than Full and Open Competition : The Center for 
Advanced Aviation System Development (CAASD) FFRDC, in which MITRE is the contractor, 
was established by the FAA and is available to any organization within DOT. 
10. A List of Sources, If Any, that Expressed, in Writing, An Interest in the Acquisition: None.

Barriers to Competition Before Any Subsequent Acquisition for the Supplies or Services

STATEMENT OF WORK

Lone Worker Devices and Monitoring Services

GENERAL: Central Arkansas Veterans Health Care System has a requirement for 140 lone worker safety monitoring devices for home care and community worker programs with 24/7/365 monitoring. This procurement is necessary to address the increase in safety events which include assaults, battery and aggressive animal attacks on home care staff. In addition, the lone worker safety monitoring device will improve timely notification of police and other emergency services while staff are out in the community and experience a disruptive event that increases the risk of harm to staff. 

BACKGROUND: Home Care and Community Workers are required to travel frequently throughout the community which increases the risk of encountering situations that places them at risk for harm (Bussing & Hoge, 2004). Civil unrest, violence in a home environment or entering environments where other VA staff or police are not present increases the likelihood of delayed awareness when a staff member is harmed or in danger. Staff are dependent on the ability to grab a VA issued smart phone, unlock the phone and then dial 911 while trying to flee from an unsafe situation. The lone worker safety monitoring device allows staff to push a button on device which is located on lanyard or on a badge holder on the outside of their shirt. The silent alarm does not emit an audible signal which prevents others from being aware that help was activated and does not further escalate the situation. The monitoring company will listen in and call for help when signs of struggles, distress or silence are detected.

With expanding demand for increased in-home care, little research and evidence is available that demonstrates proven techniques to increase personal safety.  Central Arkansas Veterans Health Care System Community Worker programs currently report to various service lines and information on safety events is not well known outside of individual programs. Community based programs are comprised of front-line staff and leadership representation. This facility is working towards standardization of processes, policies and safety precautions.

SCOPE: Central Arkansas Veterans Health Care system is requesting contractors provide specific equipment due to the listed salient characteristics in this section that meets the safety requirements of home care and community worker program needs. 

A Base plus 4-Year Option. 

      Base Year: POP  06/15/2026 – 06/14/2027

Option Year 1: POP 06/15/2027 – 06/14/2028

Option Year 2: POP 06/15/2028 – 06/14/2029

Option Year 3: POP 06/15/2029 – 06/14/2030

Option Year 4: POP 06/15/2030 – 06/14/2031

PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS: Equipment must have the physical characteristics needed for utilization with lone worker monitoring devices. The implementation of safety devices for lone workers in the community will have far reaching implications for direct care staff. This project impacts multiple services that will experience increased staff satisfaction related to enhanced personal safety. There may be an opportunity to use data to better understand the number of safety events occurring on an on-going basis.    

FUNCTIONAL AND PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS: Equipment must provide the following functional and performance capability based on evidenced based research on personal safety standards, using recommendations from home care and emergency management experts, and endorsed by local end-users.  Additional function, performance and salient characteristics include:

Must come with 24/7/365 monitoring.

Check-in/Check-out feature.

Incapacitation/Man-Down detection.

Silent notification signal.

Global Positioning System/Global Navigation Satellite System (GPS/GNSS) dual signal detection and reporting.

Badge holder appearance to the public.

Immediate notification to emergency services.

Escalation notification to Veteran Health Administration when safety alert sent or man-down detected.

Ongoing customer support.

Design:   Badge holder design

PERFORMANCE MONITORING: Employee safety device will operate on charge and allow for GPS/GNSS location detection when powered on.

The Government reserves the right to include additional staff and Service Lines within Central Arkansas Veterans Healthcare System as required and funding becomes available.  In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.212-4, any changes in the terms and conditions of this contract may be made only by written agreement of the Contractor and Contracting Officer.  The price for services for additional Service Lines are to be determined upon agreement between the Contractor and the Contracting Officer via bi-lateral modification at the Government’s request.

PLACE OF DELIVERY AND PERFORMANCE:

DELIVERY SCHEDULE: All items to be delivered within 30 days of purchase order processing and order placement.  

WARRANTY OF EQUIPMENT: Contractor must provide any manufacturer(s) warranty on devices.

SECURITY: The C&A requirements do not apply, and the Security Accreditation Pages is not required.

INFORMATION SECURITY: The contractors, their personnel, and their subcontractors shall be subject to the Federal laws, regulations, standards and VA Directives and Handbooks regarding information and information system security as delineated in this contract.

ACCESS TO VA INFORMATION AND VA INFORMATION SYSTEMS:  Custom software development and outsourced operations must be located in the U.S. to the maximum extent practical.  If such services are proposed to be performed abroad and are not disallowed by other VA policy or mandates, the contractor/subcontractor must state where all non-U.S. services are provided and detail a security plan, deemed to be acceptable by VA, specifically to address mitigation of the resulting problems of communication, control, data protection and so forth. 1. Identification of the agency and the contracting activity, and specific identification of the

This justification was prepared in accordance with FAR 16.505 by the Federal Communications
Commission {FCC), Headquarters {HQ), Office of the Managing Director {OMD), Enterprise
Acquisition Center {EAC) located at 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554. The managing
program is the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau {PSHSB).
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
To effectively manage risks to the U.S. communications sector and all dependent critical
infrastructure sectors and resources, the FCC requires an integrated solution enabling FCC staff
to analyze data from disparate sources and identify entities, equipment, and services that are
potentially owned, controlled, or influenced by foreign adversarial countries.
The Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2021 directed the Federal 
Communications Commission {FCC) to publish and update on its website a list of any 
communications equipment or service that poses an unacceptable risk to the national security 
of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons. These determinations 
are made by executive branch interagency bodies with appropriate national security expertise, 
including the Federal Acquisition Security Council {FASC); by the Department of Commerce 
pursuant to Executive Order No. 13873; by an appropriate national security agency; or for any 
communications equipment or services defined as covered telecommunications equipment or 
services under section 889{f){3) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act of 
2019. Updating this list-particularly identifying subsidiaries and affiliates of entities on the 
covered list-requires the ability to access and analyze official company filings and other public 
data available across hundreds of thousands of sources in multiple formats. 
Further, PSHSB is responsible for responding to requests for information from the determining 
bodies mentioned in the STCNA, the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States 
{CFIUS), and the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in the U.S. 
Telecommunications Services Sector {Team Telecom) which may solicit FCC feedback on 
investigations and cases which assess the national security risks of certain communications 
companies, equipment, and services. These requests for support require a rapid response in 
order to meet statutory deadlines. For these purposes, the FCC is in need of one or more 
solutions enabling the expedited analysis of aggregated data from multiple data streams and 
sources. Data sources would provide insights into company ownership; investment and investor 
stakeholders and percentages; consumers; tariff or sanction data. 

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs (i ncluding the
estimated value).
Product: Quantifind GraphyteSearch Licenses
Description: Quantifind is a readily-available, Artificial Intelligence-enabled research database
that persistently inventories publicly available information relating to business ownership,
investment, trade, tariff, sanction data, and media information relating to specific businesses,
people, research entities, and academic institutions. Quantifind automatically scans across a
broad range of public and online data including on line news sources, company registration data,
and leaks databases; seeds queries with minimally available information as a name or email
address to cultivate analyses leading to the discovery of supply chain risk factors on transaction
counterparties and other non-customers; assesses risk relationships by revealing the entities

A. Introduction 
 
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NC IA) is conducting market 
research to identify potential sources  and gather information regarding industry 
capabilities, through eliciting industry views on the envisioned services for transfer of 
ISR data outlined at Annex B - to inform the project requirements . This Request for 
Information (RFI) is issued solely for informational purposes and does not constitute a 
Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or invitation for bid.  
B. Purpose 
 
1. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain input from industry to help inform the NCIA’s 
acquisition planning. Responses to this RFI will assist in refining requirements, 
identifying capabilities, and shaping the strategy for any future solicitation. 
C. Background 
 
1. ISR Functional Services programme represents NATO's commitment to establish a 
common digital data platform to manage multi-source/domain data from ingest through 
to dissemination from an unclassified to a classified environment and the provision of 
reusable core services to manage linkages and dependencies for both the Intelligence 
community and other Communities of Interests (CoIs). 
2. DMS-T will provide a data transfer capability to transfer collected ISR data on the 
unclassified network, classified network and cross-domain.  
3. The Service is envisaged to support Data Management Service capabilities already 
established within Alliance Persistence Surveillance from Space (APSS) programme, 
adopt and enhance them accordingly if needed.  
4. A High-Level Summary of the DMS-T requirements are contained within Annex B. 
5. The RFI seeks to elicit the view of industry partners on the scope of the envisioned 
services and facilitate the Agency’s insight into best -in-class industry solutions , 
including current market capabilities, and pricing models of Services offered. 
6. A full list of questions that the Agency would like to canvass industry views on are 
contained within Annex C 
D. Submission Instructions 
 
1. Interested parties are invited to respond in accordance with the instructions below: 
 
a. Submit responses via the email address in section H no later than 12:00 hours 
Central European Time (CET) on 07 May 2026. 
b. Responses should be submitted in PDF or Word format and must not exceed 10 
pages, including:

excluding:

1. Background 
 
The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA)  aims to support the data 
management service within ISR Functional Services.  
NCIA requires a contractual mechanism that comprises of best -in-class industry solutions to 
provide this type of data management support services  
 
2. Scope 
 
The overall scope of the DMS-T is to support the Data Management Service , which is 
composed of  ingestion service  capabilities and a transfer service . Both services  are 
established within APSS program, through enhancing these service s for the usage of a 
multitude of ISR data transfer requirements.  
 
The responsibilities of the service provider are the following: 
 
a. Data Modelling & Pipelines 
i. Develop data flows that can collect data from different data sources, process 
and transform the data and deliver/provide data to consuming systems using 
data flow tool Apache NIFI. 
b. System Management & Troubleshooting 
i. Operate, maintain and support the system 
ii. Coordinate with underlying services and service delivery managers  
iii. Investigate, reporting and resolve data flow bottlenecks and technical issues 
in production environments 
c. System continuous improvements  
i. Design, implement and document a monitoring solution based on existing 
agency approved software such as Prometheus and Grafana 
d. Configuration Control and Documentation 
i. Provide configuration control and change management of the configuration 
(e.g. data flows) following the Agency directives and guidance. 
ii. Support with accreditation of new versions and releases  
e. Admin Training 
i. Provide on-the-job training and corresponding documentation to admin 
support engineers

As stated in the Objectives section, the Agency envisages the DMS-T capability to be 
supported by the successful Contractor in any subsequent NATO Competitive Procurement 
procedure.

provisions. The service provider is invited to propose a comprehensive service that

1. INTRODUCTION 
Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation (HQ SACT) is issuing this 
Request for Information (RFI) to engage with industry to conduct a current state of abilities 
for commercial industry to provide solutions to NATO capability requirements. The intention 
is to evaluate what could be immediately available, the art-of-the-possible, and current 
state-of-the-art capabilities with respect to eTacC capability, products, services, 
technologies, and methodologies. 
 
This Request for Information (RFI) does not constitute a commitment to issue a future 
request for proposal (RFP). The purpose of this request is to involve industry through 
collaboration, in an examination of future capabilities and an analysis of potential 
alternatives related to the implementation of the eTacC Capability Program Plan (CPP). 
 
Further, respondents are advised that HQ SACT will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in responding to this RFI. The costs for responding to this RFI 
shall be borne solely by the responding party. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude 
participation in any subsequent RFP if issued in the future. All information shared with ACT 
might be shared with contracted third parties to support the capability development process 
as needed. Provision of data, or lack of, will not prejudice any respondent if there is a 
competitive bidding process later as part of NATO Common-Funded Capability 
Development. 
2. BACKGROUND 
2.1. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is exploring communication, networking, and data 
transformation solutions that will enable increased connectivity at the tactical edge across 
a multitude of legacy and emergent bearers, waveforms, and protocols.   
2.2. NATO's Enhanced Tactical Connectivity (eTacC) capability is envisioned to be a node 
which acts as a relay, gateway, and translator enabling the realization of Multi-Domain 
Operations through the bridging of heterogenous tactical networks based on operational 
demands. 
 
This is not a formal request for submissions as part of a procurement; but rather a 
general request intended to determine whether any possible solutions exist that 
should be included in one or many alternatives during the development. 
 
3. PROJECT DESCRIPTION 
3.1. Vision 
3.1.1. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is exploring communication, networking, 
and data transformation solutions that will enable increased connectivity at the 
tactical edge across a multitude of legacy and emergent bearers, waveforms, 
and protocols.  NATO's Enhanced Tactical Connectivity (eTacC) capability is 
envisioned to be a node which acts as a relay, gateway, and translator enabling 
the realization of Multi-Domain Operations through the bridging of heterogenous 
tactical networks based on operational demands. The intent of this RFI is to 
solicit feedback from industry to help shape NATO's ambition. 

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
HQ Supreme Allied Commander Transformation 
RFI-ACT-SACT-04-2026 
 
Page 4 of 9  
3.1.2. The eTacC capability seeks to enhance NATO’s ability to execute duties across 
the SACEUR AOR to provide the capability to communicate beyond line of sight 
during multidomain operations.  The eTacC capability will use a meshed 
communications capability enabling operations in a contested environment and 
bring spaced based information to the tactical level. 
 
3.1.3. The implementation of eTacC requires coherent alignment with other related 
and interconnected work strands. Therefore, based on eTacC operational and 
associated Capability Requirements (CRs), NATO is issuing this RFI to gain a 
better understanding of the national capabilities (GOTS/MOTS solutions) and of 
the commercial market and that is to provide this capability that NATO could 
potentially use to acquire eTacC solutions that meet the CRs. 
 
3.2. Objectives 
3.2.1. NATO has started developing the capabilities required for eTacC to align with 
the ORs which were stated in the ORS. 
 
3.2.2. With the development of capabilities, eTacC implementation efforts will neither 
supersede any existing NATO processes, nor impact initiatives that are not the 
responsibility of NATO AFSC. NATO eTacC efforts will support these processes 
and initiatives where applicable, thus avoiding any duplication of efforts. 
 
3.2.3. The eTacC capability seeks to identify broad areas of connectivity and 
communications gaps and lead to their rapid closure. This RFI will provide the 
ability to leverage assets and resources coming from related NATO 
Programmes capabilities, assets, and resources coming from Nations, their 
Industry, and their Academia, and finally filling the gaps of missing capabilities, 
assets, resources needed to achieve tactical level interoperability and 
connectivity.

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
HQ Supreme Allied Commander Transformation 
RFI-ACT-SACT-04-2026 
 
Page 5 of 9  
 
3.2.4. Allied Command Transformation (ACT) is surveying Industry and Academia to 
understand what solutions may be able to support eTacC requirements. 
 
3.2.5. This survey seeks to gather information from Industry and Academia on existing 
eTacC solutions, as well as those in development that could potentially be 
procured by NATO. 
 
3.3. Expected Benefits to Respondents 
3.3.1. Market research to increase services provided that could broaden future 
markets and client base. 
3.3.2. Potential to broaden into military sector and international market. 
 
3.4. Expected Benefits to NATO 
3.4.1. Resilient and persistent eTacC capability solutions that meet current NATO 
Operational and Capability Requirements. 
3.4.2. Increased operational and tactical advantages over potential threats. 
 
4. REQUESTED INFORMATION 
4.1. The response(s) to this RFI shall be submitted by e-mail. 
Submissions must include both the Contracting and Technical POCs 
listed on page 2. The responses shall not contain proprietary and/or classified 
information. HQ SACT reserves the right to seek clarification on submissions. 
 
4.2. Eligibility to Respond: 
Only NATO Nations, Industry, and Academia that originate or are chartered/incorporated 
within NATO Nations are eligible to respond to this RFI. Companies from Partner Nations 
who want to participate should collaborate with a primary company headquartered within 
a NATO Nation. 
 
4.3. Response Template: 
4.3.1. Provide name, mailing address, overnight delivery address (if different from 
mailing address), designated point of contact (phone number, e-mail). 
 
4.3.2. Respondents can collaborate with other providers, but all 
companies/organizations must be clearly identified and their role/services clearly 
stated. 
 
4.3.3. Identify current services your company offers, which most closely match the 
capabilities, specified in this RFI and the questionnaire posted on HQ SACT P&C 
website (https://www.act.nato.int/opportunities/contracting) with the same title of

technical descriptions that describe your company’s current services are welcome. 
Companies are encouraged not to include marketing informational materials that do 
not relate to the services described in this RFI as they will be discarded; however, 
responses may include URL links to technical documentation materials (i.e., technical 
data sheets for products) are welcome. 
 
4.3.5. Response limited to a single main document and enclosures for a total not-to- 
exceed 15 pages (material provided as per paragraph above not included). 
 
4.3.6. The document should be single-spaced, have one-inch margins, assume US

4.4. Price Estimates 
 
HQ SACT does not seek any non-binding Rough Order Magnitude (ROM) price

JUSTIFICATION FOR AN EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY 
1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) 
     Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics

      2 3 Christopher Way

2. Description of Action: 
 
The proposed action is for a firm-fixed price (FFP) order to be issued under National 
Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solutions for Enterprise-Wide 
Procurement (SEWP) V Government-Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) for brand 
name Laurel Bridge enterprise products supporting VA Office of Information & 
Technology (OIT) Health, Clinical Imaging, Digital Imaging and Communication in 
Medicine (DICOM) facility operations teams by supporting routing of image data, 
streamlining workflow processes through automation, enables robust DICOM message 
handling in VistA, and ensures historical and new imaging studies remain accessible at 
the point of care throughout VA’s nationside modernization efforts. 
 
Facility Operations: 
1. Lighthouse Licenses 
2. Compass Store DICOM Router Licenses 
 
3. Description of the Supplies or Services: 
 
The VA, OIT, Health, Clinical Imaging, has a requirement for renewal of existing 
maintenance license subscriptions for compass routers, Lighthouse licenses, and 
support services current fielded brand name Laurel Bridge products that supports 
imaging facility operations and technical development/implementation.  The base period 
will include the Laurel Bridge operational DICOM compass routers and Lighthouse 
perpetual licenses maintenance supporting enterprise-wide image data activities among 
VA facilities, community providers, and Department of War (DOW). Required software 
maintenance and support includes periodic updates, enhancements, and corrections to 
the software as well as technical/help desk support.  The period of performance for this 
action will include a 12-month base, and the total estimated price of the proposed action 
is  
   
4. Statutory Authority:  
 
Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 16.505(a)(4), the following brand 
name requirement is being justified and approved as an exception to fair opportunity 
under the statutory authority of Section 41 U.S.C. 4106(c)(2) as implemented by FAR 
16.505(b)(2)(i)(B), entitled “Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or 
services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services 
ordered are unique or highly specialized”. 
 


  CONTROL NUMBER VA-26-00047245 
Page 2 of 5 
JA Template_FAR 16.5_(08-AUG-2024) 
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above:  
 
Based on the market research, as described in Section 8 of this justification, it has been 
determined that limited competition is available among resellers of the required annual 
maintenance for the existing VA owned Laurel Bridge DICOM DCF local server runtime 
licenses, compass routers, Run-time licenses, PowerTool Suite, developer toolkits, 
Lighthouse licenses, and support services. VA utilizes Laurel Bridge DCF software to 
develop VistA Imaging applications for all VHA facilities. VA anticipates the need to 
utilize these Laurel Bridge products for for at least the next six (6) years. The required 
annual maintenance for products supports the Government daily imaging activites 
required to support critical health care services to Veterans timely and efficiently 
ensuring the VistA Imaging applications are operational and accessible with minimal 
interruption for patient care services. 
 
To maintain the existing Laurel Bridge products, a source must have access to its 
proprietary source code to provide the required support, configuration, and software 
updates.  No other source has the capability of developing/issuing software updates for 
the Laurel Bridge software due to the proprietary nature of the source code.  In addition, 
any other source would need access to this code to ensure all services provided are 
properly configured.  Therefore, only Laurel Bridge, or its authorized resellers, can 
provide the required maintenance support services for the currently fielded software and 
the annual maintenance of the Laurel Bridge DCF products and services required for 
VistA Imaging.  
 
If Laurel Bridge DCF is not procured, reengineering VistA Imaging to use an alternate 
toolkit is currently estimated to cost approximately $7M for the first year and take a 
minimum of 12 months to complete, in addition to the cost of the alternate toolkit 
estimated at $660,000 per year. This estimate is based on previous acquisition history, 
and it is not expected these duplicative costs would be recovered through competition. 
 
Failure to procure the required annual maintenance of the existing Government owned 
Laurel Bridge products and services would result in VA’s inability to evoke existing VistA 
Imaging applications to acquire, store and provide DICOM medical images among 150+ 
VA Medical Centers, the Department of War (DOW) medical care system and 
community providers resulting in negative outcomes from delays of health care services 
to Veterans. 
 
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:  
 
Market research was conducted, details of which are in section 8 of this justification. 
This effort did not yield any additional sources that can meet the Government’s 
requirements. However, the undersigned VA technical representative determined 
that limited competition is available among authorized resellers for brand name 
Laurel Bridge, as well as software maintenance and support. In accordance with 
FAR 16.505(a)(4)(iii)(A)(1), this justification will be provided with the solicitation to all 
appropriate NASA SEWP V GWAC holders.  Furthermore, in accordance with FAR 
5.301, 16.505(b)(2)(ii)(D), and 16.505(a)(4)(iii), the award notice for this action will 

  CONTROL NUMBER VA-26-00047245 
Page 3 of 5 
JA Template_FAR 16.5_(08-AUG-2024) 
be synopsized on the Contract Opportunities website and this justification will be 
made publicly available within 14 days of award. 
 
7. Actions to Increase Competition:  
 
The Government will continue to conduct market research to ascertain if there are 
changes in the market place that would enable future actions to be competed. 
 
8. Mar
ket Research:  
 
The Government’s technical experts conducted market research from February to 
March 2026 by reviewing maintenance support services available from resellers of 
Laurel Bridge software.  Specifically, the Government’s technical experts reviewed 
products/services available from resellers (Minburn, V3 Gate) and Laurel Bridge to 
determine which sources can provide software maintenance licenses and support on 
the existing Laurel Bridge software.  Based on this review, it was determined that no 
other source could provide required licenses and maintenance support for Laurel 
Bridge software other than Laurel Bridge or one of its resellers because they lacked 
access to the proprietary source code necessary to provide the required support, 
configuration, and software updates.  Only Laurel Bridge or its resellers can access 
the proprietary source code to maintain the current fielded Laurel Bridge licenses. As 
described in Section 5 above, use of any other brand of software is not tenable due 
to the embedded code in the current infrastructure that is currently used at VA sites. 
 
The Government’s technical experts also reviewed public data to determine if 
applications developed by other vendors utilizing the Laurel Bridge products could 
be evoked either without using Laurel Bridge products or using an alternate 
manufacturer’s (Medical Connections, Ltd, MicroDicom, LeadTools, Merge 
Healthcare by IBM, Intelerad, DICOM Systems, AGFA, Sectra and Fujifilm Medical 
Systems, etc.) products, to which the results were inconclusive. As described above 
in section 5, the VistA Imaging software components that leverage the Laurel Bridge 
DICOM toolkit would need significant redesign to use another toolkit.  VistA Imaging 
neither has the funding, nor the development flexibility to support this redesign at 
this time. 
 
Given the VA legacy version of the Laurel Bridge software is proprietary or closed 
sourced, meaning the code is not made available to the general public for use, 
market research confirms that only Laurel Bridge (or its authorized resellers) can 
provide the annual maintenance requirements for the usage of the fielded Laurel 
Bridge products.  VA currently has government-owned copies of Laurel Bridge 
products, but these copies still rely on Laurel Bridge’s proprietary DCF SDK, which is 
embedded inside VistA Imaging. Even though the VA owns the deployed software 
version, the intellectual property inside it still belongs to Laurel Bridge.
