1.  Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR

2.  Contract Title 

GLAVA Radio Communications System Expansion with Additional Motorola APX NEXT & Lifecycle Support Services.

3.  Background  

The VA Police Service at the Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System operates one of the largest federal law enforcement agencies within the Veterans Health Administration, providing law enforcement and emergency response services across multiple VA medical centers, outpatient clinics, and veteran housing facilities throughout the Greater Los Angeles region. Current operations require the expansion of radio communications infrastructure and dispatch capabilities to support growing mission requirements, officer safety, and interoperability with local, state, and federal law enforcement partners including the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD), Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

This procurement effort is also in support of the Executive Order on the National Center for Warrior Independence (NCWI), which necessitates enhanced communication capabilities to ensure efficient coordination and secure communications. The procurement includes adding 100 new Motorola APX NEXT portable radios to the existing fleet to meet the demands of increased personnel and expanded operational requirements.

The expansion aligns with the goals of the National Emergency Communications Plan (NECP) to ensure effective interoperability, coordination, lifecycle management, and strengthening the cybersecurity posture of public safety communications as a whole.

4.Objective

The objective of this procurement is to expand the existing radio communications system and dispatch capability with modern, secure, fully interoperable equipment that meets federal law enforcement standards and supports VA Police operational requirements for the next five years. The system expansion shall provide:

Secure, encrypted voice communications for additional VA Police personnel

Seamless integration with existing ASTRO 25 infrastructure

Advanced digital features including voice control, smart programming, and connectivity management

Lifecycle support ensuring system reliability, security patching, and operational readiness

Compliance with federal information security standards and VA policy requirements

5. Scope

This Statement of Work / Performance Work Statement (SOW/PWS) defines the requirements for the procurement, implementation, and lifecycle support of 100 additional Motorola APX NEXT portable radio communications equipment. The Contractor shall provide all equipment, software, licensing, installation support, training, maintenance, and technical support necessary to establish and sustain a fully operational, secure, interoperable radio communications system supporting VA Police operations at the Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System (GLA).

6. Specific Tasks 

6.1  Task 1 (Phase 1):  Procurement of Additional Portable Radios, Console and Accessories

6.1 Task 1: Procurement of Additional Portable Radios and Accessories

The Contractor shall procure and deliver the following Motorola equipment in quantities specified:

6.1.1 Portable Radios

The Contractor shall provide one hundred (100) Motorola APX NEXT portable radios configured to VA Police specifications and programmed for integration with the existing ASTRO 25 system. Each portable radio shall include:

Model: Motorola APX NEXT (or equal)

Frequency bands: VHF, UHF, 700 MHz, and 800 MHz capability

LTE and Wi-Fi connectivity enabled

AES-256 encryption capability

Over-The-Air-Rekeying (OTAR) support

P25 Phase II trunking capability

Integrated GPS

Bluetooth connectivity

Voice control (ViQi) capability

Smart Programming and Smart Connect features

Minimum IP68 environmental rating

Mission Critical Push-to-Talk (MCPTT) ready

Complete codeplug development and programming for integration with existing GLA ASTRO 25 system

              6.1.2 Console

APEX 8500 (2)

Frequency bands: VHF, UHF, 700 MHz, and 800 MHz capability

LTE and Wi-Fi connectivity enabled

AES-256 encryption capability

Over-The-Air-Rekeying (OTAR) support

P25 Phase II trunking capability

Integrated GPS

Bluetooth connectivity

Voice control (ViQi) capability

Smart Programming and Smart Connect features

Minimum IP68 environmental rating

Mission Critical Push-to-Talk (MCPTT) ready

Complete codeplug development and programming for integration with existing GLA ASTRO 25 system

Programming cables and interfaces (as needed for Government programming capability)

Install Antenna, coax and all other cabling to R65 standards from roof to console location within the police station.

6.1.2 Portable Radio Accessories

The Contractor shall provide accessories and support equipment for all 100 portable radios including:

High-capacity smart batteries (minimum two per portable radio)

Multi-unit charging systems (sufficient capacity for 100 radios)

Belt clips and carrying accessories

Remote speaker microphones with emergency button

Earpieces and acoustic tube kits

Vehicular charging adapters

Programming cables and interfaces (as needed for Government programming capability)

Replacement antennas

Protective cases

All accessories shall be Motorola-branded, genuine equipment compatible with APX NEXT platform (or equal)

6.2 Task 2: Software, Licensing, and Programming

6.2.1 Radio Management Platform

The Contractor shall provide enterprise-level radio management software licensing sufficient to support the expanded VA Police GLA fleet. Software licensing shall include:

Fleet-wide device management and monitoring

Remote diagnostics and troubleshooting

Software distribution and update management

Configuration template management

Usage reporting and analytics

Security policy enforcement

6.2.2 Feature Licensing

The Contractor shall enable and license the following advanced features on all radios:

ViQi voice control system

Smart Programming (over-the-air configuration updates)

Smart Connect (automatic network switching)

Text messaging capability

GPS location services

Emergency alert and lone worker protection features

6.2.3 Programming and Provisioning

The Contractor shall provide:

Complete codeplug development and programming for all 100 portable radios and console to VA Police operational templates

Integration with existing ASTRO 25 system talk groups, zones, and system parameters

System key provisioning and encryption key loading

Talk group and zone configuration per VA Police requirements coordinated with Government technical staff

Documentation of all programming parameters and configurations

6.3 Task 3: Installation and Integration

6.3.1 Integration with Existing ASTRO 25 Infrastructure

The Contractor shall configure all equipment to seamlessly integrate with the existing GLA ASTRO 25 trunked radio system, ensuring compatibility with existing encryption key management and network integration.

6.3.2 System Installation Services

The Contractor shall provide installation technicians to perform physical installation, cabling, and equipment setup, coordination with Government facilities staff for site access, and post-installation verification and testing.

6.4 Task 4: Professional Services and Project Management

6.4.1 Project Management

The Contractor shall provide comprehensive project management services including:

Dedicated Project Manager

Coordination of all Contractor resources and subcontractors

Development and maintenance of detailed project schedule

Regular status reporting

Management of all deliverables to ensure on-time, on-budget completion

Resolution of technical and administrative issues

6.4.2 System Engineering

The Contractor shall provide system engineering services for technical design validation, finalization of system design, and support during installation, integration, and acceptance testing.

6.4.3 Training Services

The Contractor shall provide training for VA Police personnel on operation and basic troubleshooting of APX NEXT portable radios, covering user operation, emergency features, and basic troubleshooting.

6.4.4 Technical Training

The Contractor shall provide technical training for VA Police communications

The purpose of this contract is to acquire updated two-way communications equipment, which in-turn shall enhance and improve the existing equipment and system used by the Northern Arizona Veterans Affairs Health Care System (NAVAHCS) Police Department.  The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, supervision, equipment supplies, materials, materials, and travel to provide the equipment at NAVAHCS.  Furthermore, the NAVAHCS Police Department is seeking a portable radio, created specifically for mission-critical first responders who need to communicate across all frequency bands using the same device.  In order to maintain 100% complete compatibility with other VAPD stations within District 2, the Motorola model APX 8500 compatible with Programming over Project 25 (POP-25) that currently is in use within the district should be used.

BACKGROUND:


The United States Department of Veterans Affairs Police (VA Police) is the uniformed law enforcement service of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, responsible for the protection of the VA Medical Centers (VAMC) and other facilities such as Outpatient Clinics (OPC) and Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOC) operated by United States Department of Veterans Affairs and its subsidiary components of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), as well as the National Cemetery Administration (NCA) and the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) respectively. 

The Department of Veterans (VA) requires VA Police Officers to carry communications equipment. Full Text Announcement 
I. Program Description: Air Force Research Laboratory, Sensors Directorate 
(AFRL/RY) is announcing its intent to solicit proposals under this “ARA with Calls”. 
Solicitations for white papers/proposals will be accomplished via calls. The calls will 
encompass the following effort: 
 
1. Statement of Objective/Description of Technical Area(s): 
The TEMPEST program will investigate, develop, mature, prototype and 
demonstrate methodologies, tools, techniques, and capabilities to identify 
susceptibilities and mitigate vulnerabilities in avionics systems, protect those 
systems against cyber-attack, provide simulation capabilities required to develop, 
mature and transition advanced avionics and sensor technologies, develop 
platform architecture technologies that enable revolutionary and agile capabilities, 
and expand emerging open system architecture (OSA) standards and approaches 
for existing and next-generation Air Force and Department of Defense (DoD) 
weapon systems in multi-domain environments. 
 
Calls issued against this ARA will: 
• Develop experimental programs that prototype, integrate and demonstrate 
promising cyber security and cognitive avionics technologies to increase our 
platforms’ and weapon systems’ survivability and resiliency in the face of multi- 
domain threats and attacks. 
• Develop, experiment, prototype and integrate, in a laboratory environment, 
new cognitive, cyber hardened and high speed, flexible system architectures. 
• Cooperate across the Air Force, DoD, and the Intelligence Community, to 
develop experimental programs that integrate advanced cyber security and 
cognitive sensor technologies, techniques, systems and developmental 
algorithms, new cyber hardened and high speed, flexible system architectures, 
and advanced avionics, sensors, processing, and exploitation capabilities 
focused on Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, 
Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR) onto various weapon systems to 
create revolutionary capabilities. 
• Develop experimental programs that implement OSA-based reference 

Page 5 of 26  
architectures to demonstrate the cost and time benefits of applying OSA 
techniques and align multiple open architecture (OA) standards to prove the 
interoperability of various standards. Apply and demonstrate tools, 
technologies, and techniques to more rapidly document, model, simulate, and 
analyze new OSA-based system capabilities to determine the benefits for 
individual platforms and the warfighter. 
Calls to be issued against the TEMPEST ARA must a) fall under at least one of the 
Technical Areas of Interest detailed in paragraph I.1.a. below, and b) involve at 
least one of the types of work detailed in paragraph I.1.b. below. 
 
a. Technical Areas of Interest: 
 
1) Technologies for Assessing Platform Cyber Security: 
Focuses on the design and development of technologies that provide tools 
to test and experimentation (T&E) units and Cyber units (such as Mission 
Defense Teams or Red Teams) to assess cyber vulnerabilities in weapon 
systems with embedded computers. 
2) Technologies for Cyber-Hardened Platforms: 
Focuses on the design and development of technologies that reduce 
weapon system vulnerability to cyber-attack. 
3) Technologies for Cyber-Resilient Platforms: 
Focuses on the design and development of technologies that counter both 
known and unknown attack vectors that occur during mission operations to 
maintain mission capability in cyber contested environments. 
4) Agile System Architecture Development and Integration: 
Focuses on the design/procurement, development and demonstration of 
tools, technologies, and advanced component prototypes to enable 
affordable, rapid development and integration of new and emerging 
warfighting capability. Characteristics of these systems include, but are not 
limited to: capable of performing multiple functions (e.g., radar, 
communications, and electronic warfare), capable of fusing different types 
of data collections (i.e., multiple intelligence (multi-INT)), inherently cyber 
secure and/or resilient to cyber-attack, and compliant with open system 
architecture standards and approaches. 
5) Open System Architectures for Trusted and Agile Platforms: 
Focuses on investigation, through analysis, demonstration and advanced 
component prototyping, the viability and relevance of current and emerging 
open system architecture standards and approaches to enable new 
capability for cyber trusted and agile platforms. This technology area seeks 
to determine the viability of an OSA implementation prior to system design 
and development. This technical area shall identify technological advances 
in open system architecture standards, software, processing, and hardware 
to demonstrate the viability of modular open system architectures. 

Page 6 of 26  
6) Technologies for Modeling & Simulation: 
Focuses on the discovery, design and implementation of novel technologies 
to advance the state-of-the-art in modeling/simulation to faithfully 
represent transmitters, receivers, electronic systems, hostile and friendly 
radars, and radio frequency propagation algorithms for use with advanced 
models and simulations. 
7) Technologies to Advance RF Simulation: 
Focuses on defining simulation requirements for accurately demonstrating 
and evaluating sensor technologies. This technology area includes the 
design and implementation of prototype hardware (commercial or custom) 
and corresponding operating software tools to conduct demonstrations of 
radio frequency receiving or transmitting systems. 
8) Techniques, methods and technologies for measuring sensor 
system performance: 
Focuses on developing simulation techniques and methods to rapidly evolve 
and evaluate advanced sensors and electronic warfare (EW) technologies 
demonstrated in laboratory environments. Work under this technical area 
of interest will develop and employ M&S methods to specify requirements, 
define architectures, conduct design trades, and report assessment and 
demonstration results.

Draft Statement of Work (SOW) 
Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) Implementation 
Indian Health Service (IHS) 
Division of Information Technology (DIT) 
 
1. INTRODUCTION 
The Indian Health Service (IHS), an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human 
Services (HHS), is initiating a strategic modernization program to establish a Cloud Center of 
Excellence (CCoE). The CCoE will utilize Cloud (GovCloud - FedRAMP) to centralize, secure, 
and automate cloud operations while supporting mission-critical health IT objectives. 
This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the tasks, deliverables, roles, and performance 
expectations for designing, implementing, and sustaining the CCoE in alignment with federal 
compliance frameworks including: 
• FedRAMP (High Baseline) 
• NIST 800-53 Rev 5 
• Executive Order 14028 
• OMB M-22-09, M-24-04 
• CISA’s Zero Trust Maturity Model (ZTMM) 
• Post Quantum Computing (PQC) Readiness meeting PQC Mandate Enablement   
• Secure AI ready platform  
 
2. BACKGROUND 
IHS currently operates in a decentralized IT environment that contributes to fragmented 
infrastructure, inconsistent security enforcement, and risk exposure. GAO Report GAO-21-20 
identified several deficiencies in cloud governance, visibility, and cybersecurity readiness. 
To address these gaps, IHS will implement a secure Cloud GovCloud-based environment that 
consolidates infrastructure, automates security workflows, and incorporates role-based AI tools. 
The CCoE will enable continuous compliance, reduce operational overhead, and support 
innovation across IHS facilities. 
 
3. SCOPE OF WORK 
The Contractor shall provide a comprehensive solution that includes, but is not limited to, the 
following capabilities: 

• Cloud Landing Zone Design & Deployment 
o Multi-account Cloud architecture with governance controls 
o Use of Cloud Control Tower, Service Catalog, and Cloud Organizations 
o Identity and access management aligned with Zero Trust principles 
• Secure Enclave Provisioning 
o Configured enclaves for development, staging, and production workloads 
o FedRAMP-compliant storage, compute, and networking (e.g., EC2, S3, VPC, 
PrivateLink) 
o Hardened environments using CIS benchmarks and Cloud best practices 
• Automation and Orchestration 
o Automated workflows for ATO lifecycle management 
o Continuous POA&M generation, patch validation, and compliance reporting 
o Integration with SIEM (e.g., Splunk), SOAR tools, and Cloud Security Hub 
• Data Engineering and ETL 
o Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) pipelines for ingesting and transforming log and 
event data 
o Integration with Cloud   native telemetry (e.g., CloudTrail, GuardDuty) and third-
party tools 
o Masking and classification of PHI/PII in compliance with HIPAA and FISMA 
• Large Language Model (LLM) Enablement 
o On-premise or enclave-deployed LLMs for secure, role-based inference 
o AI-assisted document generation (e.g., SSP, SAR, RAR, POA&M) 
o Local semantic search and summarization of compliance materials 
o Use of containerized, GPU-accelerated inference in isolated VPCs 
• Compliance Dashboards and Risk Analytics 
o Real-time compliance status dashboards for executive reporting 
o Dashboards showing ATO progress, open vulnerabilities, audit readiness 
o Integration with natural language interfaces for querying compliance data 
• Zero Trust Architecture Implementation 
o Aligned with CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model (ZTMM) 
o Support for microsegmentation, encrypted remote access, and continuous 
validation 
o Maturity benchmarking and optimization across all ZTA pillars 
• Security Operations and Monitoring 
o Centralized log aggregation and threat detection via SIEM 
o Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), vulnerability management 
o Continuous diagnostics and mitigation (CDM) support 
• Secure Data Vault and Metadata Governance 
o Encrypted storage with tagging and classification aligned with NIST 800-60 
o Role-based tagging, automated metadata parsing, and retention policies 
o AI-assisted classification and redaction for secure document handling 
• Stakeholder Support and Role-Based Toolkits 
o Interfaces and workflows tailored to ISSOs, POA&M Analysts, Auditors, System 
Owners 
o Embedded help systems and LLM-based support assistants 
o Training materials and job aids customized per role 

 
4. OBJECTIVES 
The objectives of the Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) initiative are to modernize, secure, and 
automate IHS cloud operations across the enterprise, in alignment with federal mandates, audit 
recommendations, and the agency’s mission to improve healthcare delivery through digital 
transformation. This section outlines the business, technical, security, and strategic outcomes the 
initiative is expected to achieve. 
4.1 Business Objectives 
• Establish a centralized cloud governance model to address findings in GAO Report 
GAO-21-20 and reduce operational fragmentation. 
• Enable secure, compliant testing and deployment of mission-critical applications through 
standardized Cloud environments. 
• Implement a cost accountability framework via a chargeback model supported by Cloud 
Budgets and Cost Explorer. 
• Reduce total cost of ownership through tool rationalization, license consolidation, and 
automation of manual compliance functions. 
• Improve leadership visibility into risk posture, operational performance, and compliance 
status through real-time executive dashboards. 
4.2 Technical Objectives 
• Design and deploy a secure Cloud Landing Zone architecture with multi-account 
governance, VPC segmentation, and centralized identity and access management. 
• Automate core compliance and operational workflows including: 
o ATO package generation 
o POA&M lifecycle tracking 
o Patch deployment validation 
o Security incident ticketing and audit response 
• Integrate telemetry, logs, and vulnerability scan results into a unified SIEM and 
dashboarding platform. 
• Establish secure ETL pipelines from Cloud  and third-party telemetry sources into 
centralized compliance dashboards and data lakes. 
• Deploy GPU-enabled container environments for operating fine-tuned, enclave-hosted 
LLMs in support of documentation generation, compliance analytics, and secure 
information retrieval. 
4.3 Security and Compliance Objectives 
• Achieve continuous compliance monitoring and FedRAMP alignment across deployed 
systems and workflows. 
• Implement Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles throughout the environment in 
accordance with CISA’s ZTMM framework. 

• Provide role-specific support tools for ISSOs, Security Control Assessors, POA&M 
Analysts, and System Owners, enhancing their efficiency and audit-readiness. 
• Enable enclave-based LLMs to support automated generation of SSPs, SARs, SAPs, and 
other required documentation with no data egress. 
• Monitor compliance posture in real-time through dashboards that provide insights into 
ATO progression, vulnerability resolution, patch coverage, and audit gaps. 
4.4 Strategic Outcomes 
• Empower IHS leadership with defensible, data-driven insights into cybersecurity, 
operations, and cloud utilization. 
• Institutionalize a scalable, repeatable cloud operations model that supports future IHS 
initiatives, including EHR modernization and AI-driven analytics. 
• Reduce the burden on IHS security and compliance staff by automating routine 
workflows and documentation tasks using enclave-secured LLMs. 
• Increase IHS agility in adopting and securing commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) tools by 
establishing pre-authorization environments. 
• Create a foundation for continual innovation by deploying cloud-native and AI-native 
technologies in a secure and governed manner. 
 
5. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
One Year. All core implementation phases (enclave setup, automations, training) are to be 
completed within the Base Year. 
 
6. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
All work shall be performed remotely unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer. The 
Contractor shall use IHS-approved virtual collaboration platforms for meetings, training, and 
reviews. 
 
7. PHASED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN & DELIVERABLES 
The CCoE shall be delivered in three integrated phases. Each phase builds on the previous to 
ensure secure design, operational automation, and sustainable cloud governance. All activities 
will comply with IHS, HHS, and federal cybersecurity mandates. 
7.1 Phase 1: Foundation — Secure Enclave and Cloud  Infrastructure 
Deployment 

Objective: 
Establish the secure Cloud GovCloud infrastructure, deploy baseline logging, identity, and ETL 
capabilities, and prepare for authorization under FedRAMP and IHS-specific requirements. 
Key Activities: 
• Deploy Cloud Landing Zone using Cloud Control Tower and multi-account best practices 
• Configure core services: EC2, S3 (Standard, Glacier IR, Deep Archive), IAM, VPC, and 
PrivateLink 
• Enable centralized logging, auditing, and threat detection with Cloud CloudTrail,

DARPA-SN-26-57 
Page 1 of 4 
 
Special Notice DARPA-SN-26-57 
Strategic Technology Office (STO) Office-wide Industry Day 
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) 
 
Posting Date: April 9, 2026 
Event Date: June 8-9, 2026 
Registration Deadline: May 15, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) 
Registration Website: https://cvent.me/e9mAMw  
Technical POC: Dr. John Paschkewitz, Office Director 
E-mail: DARPA-SN-26-57@darpa.mil  
 
DESCRIPTION: 
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Strategic Technology Office (STO) 
will host a STO Office-wide Industry Day event on June 8-9, 2026. The event will be held at the 
DARPA Conference Center (DCC) located at 675 N. Randolph St., Arlington, VA 22203. 
Advance registration is required. There will be no on-site registration. This event will be 
hosted in-person only. The event will include presentations by the STO Director and Program 
Managers (PM), panel discussions, and an opportunity for one-on-one engagement with STO 
PMs via sidebar meetings.  
The purpose of the event is to (1) familiarize attendees with STO’s vision, problem spaces, PMs, 
and technology interests; and (2) facilitate technical discussion between STO PMs and attendees 
that explore innovative and impactful solution ideas for strategic national security challenges. 
This meeting will be held at the SECRET collateral level.  
 
STO MISSION AND FOCUS AREAS: 
STO is DARPA’s systems warfare office pursuing innovative and disruptive technologies for 
existing and future battlespaces. With peer competitors able to develop and field new capabilities 
at speeds unmatched by prior U.S. adversaries, STO focuses on the ability to provide warfighters 
with systems that enable superior adaptation at speed and scale and that create new opportunities 
for deterrence and overmatch.  
STO’s technical focus areas include: 
• Multi-Domain Mission Systems – new systems and resilient architectures with the ability 
to sense and sense-make; includes AI-native planning & execution systems to provide 
orchestrating effects  
• Maritime – maritime capabilities that leverage U.S. asymmetric advantages and create 
novel operational dilemmas for competitors and adversaries 
• Space – space systems that leverage scaling provided by America’s rapidly growing 
commercial space industry  
• Industry, Infrastructure, and Information – strengthening U.S. assets and ecosystems, 
creating complexity to stymie potential adversaries, and accelerating our own ability to 
field new capabilities 

DARPA-SN-26-57 
Page 2 of 4 
 
 
REGISTRATION INFORMATION: 
The STO Office-wide Industry Day will be held on June 8-9, 2026, at the DARPA Conference 
Center (DCC) located at 675 N. Randolph St., Arlington, VA 22203. Advance registration is 
required and there will be no on-site registration. 
Attendance is open to registrants with at least a SECRET clearance, on a first-come, first-served 
basis with no more than two representatives per business unit of an organization until venue 
capacity is reached. The determination of what constitutes a business unit will be made by 
DARPA. Interested parties are encouraged to coordinate attendance internally within their 
organizations prior to registration. 
Registration closes at 1:00 pm ET on May 15, 2026. Visit requests, security clearances, and 
other applicable documents must be sent to DARPA by this time. 
Participants must register prior to registration close at https://cvent.me/e9mAMw. 
 
SIDEBAR MEETINGS: 
Registered attendees will have the option to request 15-minute sidebar meetings with STO PMs 
to further elaborate their specific technical fields. Only a limited number of meeting times are 
available and there is no guarantee all attendees will be scheduled for sidebar meetings. 
To best align the research interests of participants with those of STO PMs, interested 
parties must submit the request form provided at the end of this Special Notice prior to 
registration close. 
Attendees will be notified of their meeting time and on-site instructions. No additional sidebar 
meetings will be scheduled during the event. No more than 2 representatives may join in a single 
sidebar meeting. 
Please note that no competition-sensitive information will be shared or discussed in the sidebar 
meetings. 
Sidebar meetings may require additional clearances to be sent to DARPA. DARPA will notify 
the participants of their meeting time and classification of discussion. At that time, participants 
will have 5 business days to submit any additional clearance visit request. For those requesting 
an SCI-level sidebar discussion, SCI-level visit request can be sent proactively, prior to being 
notified of sidebar selection. 
 
SECURITY INFORMATION:  
All attendees must transmit their security clearances to DARPA. Clearances must be received 
prior to the registration close. Failure to complete and submit the required forms prior to the 
registration deadline may result in the cancellation of existing registration.  
• For collateral-level visits to DARPA, please have the Facilities Security Officer (FSO) 
send a visit request via Defense Information System for Security (DISS) using the SMO 
Code: DDAAUS4. You may also fax your clearance/visit request to DARPA at (703) 

DARPA-SN-26-57 
Page 3 of 4 
 
528-3655 or send it via encrypted e-mail to SID-CPC@darpa.mil. The Technical POC is 
John Paschkewitz at (571) 218-4322 and the Security POC is Jamie Bugett. The purpose 
is to attend the STO Office-wide Industry Day 2026 DARPA-SN-26-57.   
For additional instructions on sending visit requests and security clearances to DARPA, please 
visit http://www.darpa.mil/policy/visitor-information.  
The optional sidebar meetings will be held at DARPA and may be offered up to the TOP 
SECRET/SCI-level classification. Attendees invited to sidebar meetings will be notified prior to 
the event, anticipated by 26th of May 2026. Based on highest classification requested by 
participants, classified meetings may require additional security clearance transmittal.  
In anticipation of an SCI-level visits: Please fax your clearance/visit request to the SSO at 703-
528-3655 (unclassified). You may also send your SCI visit requests as follows: 
o Via JWICS, the requesting SSO may send a message with the visit information to 
SSO DARPA. 
o Via DISS, the requesting SSO may send a visit request using the SMO Code 
DDAAUS2. 
 
TEAMING: 
To assist those wanting to establish collaborative teaming efforts and business relationships, 
participants may indicate on the registration website that they authorize their contact information 
to be shared among meeting participants. For organizations new to DARPA, this may be of use 
in connecting with potential partners. Team formation, communications, and networking are the 
sole responsibility of the participants.  
 
DISCLAIMERS: 
This Special Notice is issued solely for information and program planning purposes and does not 
constitute a formal solicitation for proposals or proposal abstracts; any so sent will be 
disregarded. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this Special Notice are not offers 
and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Attendance is strictly 
voluntary and is not required to propose to subsequent Announcements (if any) or Solicitations 
(if any) on this topic. DARPA will not provide reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to 
this Special Notice. Respondents are advised that DARPA is under no obligation to acknowledge 
receipt of any information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any 
information submitted under this Special Notice. 
  

DARPA-SN-26-57 
Page 4 of 4 
 
Strategic Technology Office (STO) Office-wide Industry Day 
Request for Program Manager Sidebar Form 
 
Responses are expected to be UNCLASSIFIED and should be submitted via email attachment to 
DARPA-SN-26-57@darpa.mil. No classified submissions should be emailed to this inbox.  
To submit a classified response, interested participants must pre-coordinate via UNCLASSIFIED 
email request to DARPA-SN-26-57@darpa.mil. Email subject should read: “Request to submit 
classified sidebar materials.” Email request should also include the intended classification of the 
content. At least one week prior to deadline for pre-coordination is recommended, for material to 
be received at DARPA prior to registration close. 
Any responses received by DARPA after registration close may be rejected from consideration. 
 
SUBMISSION FORMAT: 
Responses should provide the information requested below and adhere to the following 
formatting specifications: 11- or 12-point font, single-spacing, 8.5 by 11-inch paper, 1-inch 
margins, either Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format. Responses are limited to a cover page 
and one paragraph, half page maximum description. Each response may only address a single 
idea. 
A. Cover Page:  
a. Respondent name, organization, telephone number, and email address 
b. Relevant STO technical focus area (Multi-Domain Mission Systems; Maritime; 
Space; Industry, Infrastructure, & Information) 
c. Program manager(s) best aligned to your research interests. You may select up to 
3 PMs but must indicate at least one. Information on STO PMs may be found at 
https://www.darpa.mil/about/offices/sto#pm  
d. Desired classification of sidebar meeting: SECRET, TOP SECRET, or SCI-level 
B. Description: In a brief paragraph (6-8 sentences max), describe your unique capability or 
insight and the national security capability the idea may help create. Explain what risk 
reduction is still required.

Special Operations Forces General Services Delivery (SOF GSD)

IDIQ Level Statement of Work (SOW)

1.0 Background.  The United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) is a Unified Combatant Command of the Department of Defense (DoD).  USSOCOM’s mission is to “Provide fully capable Special Operations Forces to defend the United States and its interests.”  This also includes five command priorities: “Compete and Win for the Nation; Preserve and Grow Readiness; Innovate for Future Threats; Advance Partnerships; and Strengthen our Force and Family”.  These priorities support USSOCOM’s ongoing efforts to ensure SOF are highly trained, properly equipped and deployed to the right places at the right times for the right missions.  

1.1 Services Imperatives.  In addition to the command priorities, USSOCOM SOF AT&L’s PEO-Services focuses on three “imperatives” in providing the command with professional services support: Stability, Agility, and Reach.  The Command considers these qualities to be essential in accomplishing the requirements of this SOW.  In a “Ways / Means / Ends” paradigm, these imperatives are “Ends”.   As they apply to this SOW, these imperatives are defined as follows:

1.1.1 STABILITY is primarily about mission continuity.  While there are multiple ways to achieve and sustain continuity, USSOCOM is specifically interested in retaining high quality and applicable institutional knowledge and minimizing workforce turbulence.  Stability is catalyzed by respectable and credible management and leadership and is enabled by discrete and dedicated resources in support of any contract/task-order transition.  It requires competitive compensation plans that incentivize on-the-job performance and loyalty to mission support.  It includes an ability to solve personnel issues efficiently and effectively and enables opportunities for individual growth and development.

1.1.2 AGILITY is the ability to manage a professional workforce in USSOCOM’s dynamic environment that evolves at the “speed of SOF”.  It includes an ability to surge capacity, manage change, and respond to issues.  It requires a balance between simplicity and complexity that ensures necessary complex tools are available, but simple to find and apply.  Agile management is available to the customer, and proximate to issues to which it must respond.  Such management has organic resources that can be directly applied in support of the mission, with minimum (or no) need to secure additional permissions to apply them.

1.1.3 REACH is manifested by applying the network and knowledge of the entire enterprise(s) of the team.  It includes a demonstrated ability to place and care for employees in remote places worldwide, and access to established nodes that holistically interconnect USSOCOM’s global tasks.  Reach is both functional and physical – it can positively impact logistics as well as provide external perspectives that contribute to solution development.

1.2 Location.  For the purposes of this SOW when support to the USSOCOM Enterprise is specified this shall include HQ USSOCOM - MacDill AFB FL and its subordinate Component Commands and all of their requisite locations (both CONUS and OCONUS), United States Army Special Operations Command (USASOC) - Fort Bragg, NC; Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) - Fort Bragg, NC; Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) - Hurlburt Field, FL; Marine Special Operations Command (MARSOC) - Camp Lejeune, NC; Naval Special Warfare Command (NAVSPECWARCOM) - Coronado, CA; and the Theater Special Operations Commands (TSOCs) in various locations. 

2.0 Purpose. The purpose of this contract is to provide subject matter expertise and knowledge-based services in support of USSOCOM’s enterprise requirements for U.S. based and globally assigned Special Operations Forces (SOF) missions.

3.0 Requirements and Responsibilities. The contractor shall meet all requirements and responsibilities in support of USSOCOM and shall ensure quality work performance in accordance with the SOW. The contractor shall provide all personnel, training, certifications and supervision necessary to perform the services.

4.0 Scope of Support. The requirements included in this SOW support the government in the following areas: Education and Training Services, Management Support Services, Program Management, Engineering, Technical and Professional Services, and Administrative & Other Services.

5.0 Requirements.  This section describes general requirements to be supported. Specific requirements will be identified at the task order (TO) level.

5.1 Education and Training Services: These services shall provide support to USSOCOM organizations involved in training SOF in both garrison and field environments. This includes providing vocational and technical training at the individual, collective, or staff level on a variety of subjects, conducting lectures, performing testing, curriculum development, and other related training and military exercises. Also included in the scope of Education and Training services are translation services to support various Command activities. Below are representative tasks which may be required. The following is a representative sampling, not an all-inclusive listing of the Education and Training Services tasks and is provided to assist with planning for and supporting these services:

USSOCOM Organization Specific Internal Training Support. Typical efforts include monitoring and tracking command training, assisting in preparing core SOF/SOF-unique training materials and course preparation, as well as coordination of materials throughout the command.

Operational and Education/Training Support. The contractor may be required to provide operational and education/training support. Typical efforts include developing and maintaining web page and database content associated with monitoring training, developing and maintaining lesson plans, and conducting classes (e.g. week-long management seminars or specialty training classes to small groups of 10-20 personnel) locally or virtually; developing and reviewing draft training, doctrine and operational publications; producing training and education support materials; and reviewing and maintaining the SOF Joint Mission Essential Task List (JMETL).

Education Policy Analysis and Revision. The contractor may support staff revisions of applicable USSOCOM policy directives and memoranda.   This may include analysis of previous joint education studies conducted for the Joint Staff, USSOCOM, the Joint Special Operations University or other organizations. Also required may be analyses of historical, current, and proposed policies, lessons learned resident in the Joint Lessons Learned Information System (JLLIS), instructions, guidance and directive letters with applicability to special operations and joint education issues. Collecting and assessing emerging or major revisions to Department of Defense, Joint Staff, or Services’ education visions, goals, or recommended guidelines which would impact joint education for SOF. Based on analysis and government review the contractor shall provide revised USSOCOM Directives as required to support Joint Special Operations Education.

Cultural and Language Training Support. The contractor may be required to provide foreign language instruction, regional expertise, and culture instruction and culture emersion in foreign host nations. The contractor may be required to conduct professional study and analysis to continue and build on previous long-range studies to analyze the varied culture and language training programs and efforts within the command and identify areas for improvement by extending it to new and modified initiatives while continuing coverage of traditional programs. Training effectiveness efforts may be initiated to examine language and culture training and deliver the training by the joint SOF Teletraining System or other prescribed means. The contractor shall collect valid and reliable data, analyze it appropriately to yield actionable recommendations, and produce reports, presentations and/or suggested training curriculum. Reports shall provide the SOF Language Office (or other designated offices) with discrete, targeted analysis and recommendations tailored to specific language or cultural programs.

Translation Services. The contractor may be required to provide multilingual translation services via native speakers, or the certified native proficiency equivalent at the professional level for languages to conduct translation activities from target languages to the English language and from English into target languages and Cultural/Ideology Analysis in consonance with open source intelligence (OSINT) production requirements supporting a full range of Irregular Warfare and Unconventional Warfare (IW/UW) production tasks commensurate with USSOCOM intelligence priorities. Additionally, Services may be required when translation is necessary for the integration and delivery of final products or requirements such as texts, magazines, or videos. The contractor may be required to provide translation support to include but not limited to the translation of audio clips, website content, print, video, graphic, electronic, multi-media and any additional forms of communication. In addition, the contractor may be required to provide multilingual interpretation services via native speakers, or the certified native proficiency equivalent at the professional level from target languages to the English language and from English into target languages as required for meetings, conferences, briefings, and various other forums of voice communications. The contractor may be required to provide broadcast quality voice talent as required. Target Languages include but are not limited to all dialects of the following languages: Arabic, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Indonesian, Thai, Korean, Chinese, Urdu, Farsi, UK English, Swahili, Filipino, Hindi, Pashtu, Russian, and German.

Combat Modeling, Simulation and Wargaming. The contractor may be required to develop, modify or support existing data models, wargames and simulations to assist in the testing of concepts and decisions, exploration of issues, and development and data content maintenance of databases to support models, training, games and simulations.

Exercise Planning Support. The contractor may be required to provide subject matter experts with a combination of skills and experiences, including SOF ground, maritime, and air operations, Joint SOF operational experience, as well as, intelligence and interagency operations to participate in exercises (2 -10 week-long episodic training exercises possibly employing up to 150 role players) and battle staff events as determined by USSOCOM. The contractor may be required to participate in the Joint Exercise Control Group (JECG) throughout the duration of each event under the guidance of the USSOCOM-Exercise Director, Lead Planner, and JECG Director. The contractor also may be required to participate in the Semi-Annual Exercise Conference (SAEC).

Exercise Execution Support. The contractor may be required to assist in the delivery of command post exercises, tabletop exercises with role players, subject matter experts and other products and services as identified in supporting exercise documents and material on the U.S. government’s timeline. This process includes working in collaboration with the other Commands or Agencies in developing exercise design and execution.

Training and Mission Rehearsal Support. The contractor may be required to provide support and expertise in the areas of SOF operational mission sets, their applicability to training, and technical knowledge of the requirements generation system, simulation development, acquisition, implementation of these mission sets, and network architectures. This includes the ability to analyze and update current training requirements. These efforts are related to the identification, analysis, user evaluations, and generation of training requirements to support time- critical training system needs for SOF. This support also may involve the identification, assessment, or coordination with the acquisition or other applicable communities to develop or modify training materials or strategies to take advantage of advanced technologies. This support may be conducted with non-standard users and at non-standard locations.

5.2 Management Support Services: These services involve providing advice and assistance with the management and operation SOF organizations that are closely associated with the basic responsibilities and missions of SOF organizations. These services include strategic planning, SOF capability and structuring analysis and advice, with a broad array of deliverables such as data collection, writing services, public relations support and media analysis. While these tasks are not all inclusive, they represent support that assists enterprise planning and support for these services. 1 INTRODUCTION 
1.1 BACKGROUND 
Cyberspace Operations are the employment of cyberspace capabilities where the primary purpose is to 
achieve objectives in or through the cyberspace domain.  This domain is defined by the Secretary of 
Defense (SecDef) as "a global domain within the information environment consisting of the 
interdependent network of information technology infrastructures, including the internet, 
telecommunications networks, computer systems and embedded processors and controllers." The 
successful execution of Cyberspace Operations requires the integrated and synchronized employment of 
offensive, defensive, and Department of Defense Information Network (DODIN) operations, underpinned 
by effective and timely operational preparation of the Operating Environment. Cyberspace Operations 
missions encompass Offensive Cyberspace Operations (OCO), Defensive Cyberspace Operations (DCO), 
and DODIN Operations, based on their intent, not on the specific effects created, or the capabilities used.  
OCO are intended to project power by the application of force in and through cyberspace; they include 
operations to attack automated systems (e.g., Command, Control, Communications, Computers, 
Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR)), and the interaction between the physical, social 
and biological networks that define human-machine interaction.  DCO are intended to defend DoD or 
other friendly cyberspace domains, including network operations that encompass friendly C4ISR and 
Information Operations (IO) functions that occur within the cyberspace domain.  DODIN Operations are 
actions taken to design, build, configure, secure, operate, maintain, and sustain DoD communications 
systems and networks in a way that creates and preserves data availability, integrity, and confidentiality, 
as well as user/entity authentication, authorization, and non-repudiation.  DODIN Operations includes 
cyber security activities, security engineering, and all other activities and actions taken to ensure the 
integrity of systems, networks, and nodes that enable friendly use of the cyberspace domain.  These 
missions are planned and executed at all levels of military operations, and commanders use Joint 
Functions concepts to integrate cyberspace capabilities into operational planning and execution, and to 
synchronize Cyberspace Operations with other operations and effects within the battlespace.   
 
The Naval Information Warfare Center, Pacific (NIWC Pacific), as the principle Navy Research, 
Development, Test and Evaluation (RDT&E) and Acquisition Center for C4ISR and IO is responsible for 
functions that include: mission analysis, assessment and development of technology base, basic and 
applied research, demonstration of technology, engineering in support of production, support to operating 
forces; supporting doctrine, policy, and strategy development; and integration of numerous National and 
Tactical systems in the area of Cyberspace Operations. 
 
Increasingly, NIWC Pacific, DoD and other Government customers require advice, assistance, 
coordination and products necessary to support operational planning, assessment, integration, execution 
and technology development to assure superiority for the warfighter in the cyberspace domain. Specific 
activities of interest required to achieve superiority in cyberspace include, but are not limited to:  
 
- Cyberspace Operations (e.g., Offensive, Defensive, DoD Information Network, and ISR, 
Operational Preparation of the Environment (OPE), and other supporting functions) as they relate

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING 
ACTIVITY 
Department of 
State Contracting 
Activity  
    Acquisition Management 
    Foreign Service Institute  
    Office of Foreign Missions 
    U.S. Mission to the United Nations  
    Overseas Post  
Requiring 
Activity 
Ceiling increase for IDIQ 19AQMM20D0138 
RightDirection Technology Solutions 
Human Resource Bureau (HR), formerly PERT 
SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING 
APPROVED 
Approval is requested to modify the ceiling of IDIQ 19AQMM20D0138 to RightDirection 
Technology Solutions, LLC, located at: 300 E Lombard St, Ste 840, Baltimore, MD 21202;  
for the supplies and/or services described in Section 3 on behalf of the Requiring Activity. 
Offered to the 8(a) program – September 27, 2020 
Acceptance provided by SBA’s District Office on September 27, 2020 
IDIQ Contract # 19AQMM20D0138 
SBA Requirement #: 0373/20/ZA1600008305Z 
Last day for current J&A: March 27, 2026 
The requested modification will increase the IDIQ ceiling by $1,200,000.00, from 
$4,000,000.00 to $5,200,000.00 due to an increase in estimated hours under the Task Orders  
necessary to address evolving operational needs. This is an IDIQ for Administrative Services 
(Time and Materials (T&M)/Labor Hour). 
This modification is solely to increase the contract ceiling from $4,000,000 to $5,200,000 . 
This increase is necessary to allow the continuation of critical administrative services 
through current open four (4) task orders issued in this IDIQ ending on September 18, 
2026, ensuring uninterrupted support while the Department conducts a full and open 
competition for a follow-on contract before September 18, 2026. No changes to the scope of 
work, period of performance, or terms and conditions are being made to the IDIQ .  
SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED

SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE 
AGENCY’S NEEDS 
The Department of State requires ongoing administrative support to maintain uninterrupted 
operations for the Bureau of Human Resources front office. Support includes program 
management, clerical assistance, data entry, records management, and related administrative 
functions. 
SECTION 4:  IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING 
OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 USC 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.103 
and substantiated by the following: 
 FAR 6.103-2 – Unusual and compelling urgency. 
SECTION 5:  DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR’S 
UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES 
USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED 
RightDirection Technology Solutions, LLC is uniquely qualified to provide these services 
based upon the following: 
a. Experience and Knowledge:
RightDirection Technology Solutions, LLC has provided consistent, high-quality administrative
support under the current IDIQ. Their personnel possess the required security clearances,
institutional knowledge, and familiarity with Department of State processes and systems.
b. Unusual and Compelling Urgency:
The current contract ceiling will be reached before the end of the required period of
performance. Without this ceiling increase, there will be a lapse in critical administrative
services, which would disrupt essential Department operations. The requested ceiling increase
is strictly limited to the amount necessary to maintain uninterrupted service through
September 18, 2026. This extension is critical to allow the Bureau sufficient time to complete a
new competitive contract, therefore allowing sufficient time for a thorough process before the
end of FY26.
SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE 
SOLICITED FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, 
Page 2 of 4 
SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED

INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS 
REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION UNDER 
FAR 5.201 APPLIES 
Per FAR 5.201 – EXCEPTION 5.202(4) Small Business Administration (SBA) using the 
authority of the Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act. The local small business office 
provided approval to modify the contract as requested with no change is scope, to be exercised 
by the “Procurement Contracting Officer”. This approval was granted on 03/12/2026. Approval 
letter on file.  
SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE 
ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE  
The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated $1,200,000.00 to the Government of the 
services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on the proposed labor rates and 
level of effort estimated by the requestor for the remaining period of performance for the Task 
Orders. The proposed additional level of effort was reviewed in the form of an IGCE in 
consultation with the technical team and found to be realistic and appropriate for meeting the 
Governments’ requirements. No changes to the hours or new labor categories were added . The 
cost structure reflects a reasonable relationship between the current labor mix, hours, and the 
technical approach. Nothing changed. This is the best value to the Government given the 
circumstances.  
SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE 
PART 10) AND THE RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET 
RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED 
No additional market research was conducted for this action because the modification is strictly 
limited to increasing the ceiling of the existing IDIQ contract. The scope of work, period of 
performance, and contract terms remain unchanged. The purpose of this increase is to allow the 
continuation of services through September 18, 2026, ensuring uninterrupted support while 
providing sufficient time to conduct a new recompete process before the end of FY26. As no new 
requirements or changes to the nature of the work are being introduced, further market research 
was not warranted for this modification. 
SECTION 9.  ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER 
THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
The original contract was competed under the 8(a) program as a sole source. This justification 
is not for a new requirement, but solely to increase the contract ceiling only to allow the 
current contractor to continue providing essential services until September 18, 2026. This will 
prevent a disruption in mission-critical support and provide the necessary time to conduct a full 
and open competition for a new contract before the end of FY26. Attempting to re-compete the 
Page 3 of 4
SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED

requirement immediately would risk a gap in service and would not allow for a thorough and 
competitive procurement process. 
SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN 
WRITING, AN INTEREST IN THE ACQUISITION  
To date, no other sources have written to express an interest in this acquisition. 
This action is limited to increasing the ceiling of the existing IDIQ contract with RightDirection 
Technology Solutions, LLC. No new solicitation or market research was conducted, as the 
scope and contractor remain unchanged. No additional sources were contacted or considered 
for this modification. 
SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE 
TO REMOVE OR OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY 
SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED  
The Department is committed to full and open competition for future requirements. The 
requested ceiling increase is a temporary measure to ensure continuity of service while the 
Department prepares and executes a new competitive procurement. The recompete process is 
expected to be completed before the end of FY26, with the new contract in place immediately 
following the expiration of the current IDIQ on September 18, 2026.

SUBJECT: Indefinite Delivery Contract (IDC), Multiple Award Task Order Contract 
(MATOC) for Services to support the Builder Sustainable Management System (SMS) 
Quality Assurance (QA) Program, Mobile District, South Atlantic Division (SAD) 
1.0 DESCRIPTION 
This contract shall consist of IDC MATOCs for Services for USACE SAD, Mobile District 
to support the Builder SMS QA Program. The required services include all planning, 
supervision, labor, subcontracts, travel, and all other things necessary to perform quality 
assurance through on-site analysis of facilities and analysis of data contained in the 
Builder SMS database in support of the Builder SMS QA implementation at various 
Department of Defense (DoD) Army Agencies, as well as other military, civil, and 
Federal agencies located throughout CONUS and OCONUS. This acquisition strategy 
consists of one (1) solicitation resulting in at least three (3) contract awards with a five-
year ordering period and a total procurement capacity of $9,000,000. 
2.0 OBJECTIVE 
The anticipated IDC MATOCs are intended to provide a full range of comprehensive 
support for the Builder SMS QA Program. Mobile District was designated in 2017 as the 
Program Manager for the Builder SMS Program for the Installation Management 
Command (IMCOM) and has subsequently executed agreements for similar services 
with other stakeholders that may include the Army Materiel Command (AMC), Army 
National Guard (ARNG), Army Reserve Command (USARC), US Air Force (USAF), 
Veterans Administration (VA), Defense Health Agency (DHA), and other DoD and 
Federal stakeholders as assigned. The objective of this acquisition is to acquire 
qualified Firms to perform services to support the BUILDER SMS QA Program. 
Evaluation and selection of firms will be based on a broad range of qualifications and 
demonstration of successful past performance. The selection will identify those highly 
qualified firms with expertise and experience with projects of similar scope, magnitude, 
and complexity as those anticipated under this MATOC. 
3.0 SCOPE OF WORK 
Mobile District will utilize this IDC MATOC to support the Builder SMS QA Program.  
Contractors shall be required to provide services to conduct QA oversight on Facility 
Condition Assessments performed by disparate AE firms awarded separately from this 
contract and which are not a requirement of this contract. 
Additional services performed on this contract may include, but is not limited to: QA 
planning and support by reviewing the assessment plans for site visits, assisting in 
planning and review of assessment QC plans; validating Builder compliance and 
assessment requirements are met in accordance with the ARMY BUILDER SMS 
Inventory and Assessment Guide, published in July 2025 by ERDC, USACE; collecting 

 
 
independent field data to validate compliance, compare collected data to the uploaded 
data into the Builder database notating any discrepancies and/or omissions, and 
reporting assessment discrepancies found either in the field or during review.  
Coordinate travel and building access schedules with the AE firm under separate 
contracts. Obtain access permissions to various DoD installations, facilities and secured 
rooms that require secret clearance as necessary. 
The contractors selected for this contract shall furnish all labor, materials, and 
equipment to perform all work in strict accordance with the project specific task orders. 
The requirements for each specific project will be identified in each task order’s 
statement of work. 
Each task order statement of work shall require the firm to report manpower. All firms 
under this contract shall report ALL contractor labor hours (including subcontractor labor 
hours) required for performance of services provided under this contract for the 
Department of War via a secure data collection site.  
The contractor is required to completely fill in all required data fields using the following 
web address: http://sam.gov/. Reporting inputs will be for the labor executed during the 
period of performance during each Government fiscal year (FY), which runs October 01 
through September 30. While inputs may be reported at any time during the FY, all data 
shall be reported no later than October 31 of each calendar year.  
Contractors may direct questions to the help desk at: http://sam.gov.  
The particular projects are not known at this time but are anticipated to include all items 
as listed in the objectives paragraph.  
IDC contract awardees shall share the total capacity. The ordering period of the IDCs 
shall be five years from the date of award.  
Selection of firms is not based upon competitive bidding procedures, but rather upon the 
qualifications necessary for the performance of the required effort.  
A written determination which documents the selection and justification rationale will be 
maintained in each task order file.

NATIONAL ARCHIVES AND RECORDS ADMINISTRATION  
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION   
DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM  
1.0 Introduction  
The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) is an independent federal agency 
that helps safeguard and preserve our nation's history by overseeing the management of all 
federal records. The mission is to ensure ready access to the essential evidence that documents 
the rights of American citizens, the actions of federal officials, and the national experience.  
The purpose of this RFI is to obtain technical information about approaches and commercially  
available software products that can be used to manage several categories of audio-visual 
assets used for multiple purposes.  
 
This RFI requests information on potential tools and price points for two related use 
cases. We are interested in responses that address both use cases together if feasible, 
or separately if the combination results in significant price and capability variations.  
 
1. The first use case is limited to internally-accessed audiovisual business 
records and associated metadata. This approach has an estimated storage 
requirement of 120 TB over five years.  
2. The second use case builds on the first, adding the maintenance and external 
distribution of high quality digital reproduction masters of accessioned 
records. This approach would require approximately 1330 TB over five 
years. Additionally, all users and access for this use case would need to be 
managed separately from the first. 
NARA is a small agency with limited internal IT development and systems 
engineering resources, so we are interested in solutions that:   
 
● Do not require extensive technology configuration and integration efforts  
● Can support migration and ingest of approximately 65 terabytes of existing 
data from the current system, if limited to use case one. 
● Can support ingest of an initial 400 TB of existing data from various storage 
solutions for use case two. 
 
2.0 Description/Objective  
NARA requires a system to efficiently manage audiovisual business records so that they remain 
authentic, accessible, usable, and retrievable throughout the records’ lifecycle. Any solution shall 
have the capability to manage working files as well as implement records schedules and 
associated dispositions on agency electronic photo, video, graphic design, and audio records. The 
system will need to migrate NARA corporate records from the current system to a new one that 
will maintain, store, and access all of NARA's photo, video, audio, and graphic corporate 
records. Current storage is 49 TB. The estimated storage requirement is 120 TB over five years. 
A second use case would be to maintain, manage, and distribute high quality reproduction 
masters of Moving Image and Sound accessioned records. These files are currently stored on 

Linear Tape Open (LTO) tape, various networked on-premise storage servers, and NARA’s 
Google Drive. There is no distribution solution; when files are needed they are exchanged by 
external hard drive. Estimated base volume is 400 TB with projected annual additions of 
approximately 230 TB per year. The estimated storage requirement is 1330 TB over five years.  
The objectives are to:   
● Ensure that authentic, accessible, and usable audiovisual records and accompanying 
metadata are available to all appropriate NARA staff whenever needed 
● The areas of content that need to be addressed are: photos, graphics, audio and video 
productions, and if possible .csv, .dat, .txt, .cdf files, and proprietary formats for 
scientific instruments such as FTIR, XRF and GCMS. 
2.1 Requirements  
NARA is seeking a flexible long-term digital asset management system (DAMS) that will 
serve as both a continually accessible repository for audiovisual working files and high 
quality digital reproduction masters  of accessioned holdings, as well as a reliable digital 
records management system for federal records prior to archival accessioning.  
NARA requires a solution that has the ability to:   
● Provide file storage, management, discovery, and sharing functionality for NARA’s photo, 
video, audio, text, graphic design, CSV, and proprietary scientific instrument data. 
● Allow employees to upload, view, and download working assets as needed to accomplish 
their work.   
● Ingest records and manage them according to their records lifecycle, and apply a full range 
of retention rules and other records management functionalities to the records.  
● Support agency-wide audiovisual corporate records management and be available to 
designated users in every office, totalling at least 100 accounts. 
● For the second use case, system should support an additional 10 accounts for external 
users. 
● Incorporate policies to govern the metadata and transfer of assets, enrich the value of the 
assets in perpetuity, and create an organized pipeline for eligible digital assets to be 
transferred into the holdings of the National Archives for permanent preservation. 
● Connect to Amazon Web Services S3 buckets. 
● Migrate approximately 65 terabytes (TB) of existing audiovisual data currently in the 
system.  
● Reliably manage a total of 1450-2000 TB of data over the next five years,  
 
2.2 Functional Requirements  
NARA seeks to obtain from prospective contractors how their proposed digital asset 
management system meets and/or exceeds the following high-level functional requirements 
and complies with all requirements listed as Requirement Priority “MUST” within 
Attachment 1: ADAMS_RVTM_v.2.0_2026Feb26. 
2.2.1 Access: The solution shall provide timely, efficient, and accurate access to records, 

including the capability by individual or administrative users to set access permissions for 
actions such as preventing unauthorized access, modifying, uploading, or deleting  
records.   
2.2.2 Administration. The solution shall provide insight into user behavior through 
reporting and audit trail logs and allow user account creation at varying permission levels. 
Appropriate user tiers will have the ability to control, configure, and manage all records 
management-related features and functionalities (including the final classification of business 
records).   
2.2.3  Upload Assets. Authorized internal and external users shall be able to upload 
digital special media assets and their associated metadata in the user interface, both 
individually and in bulk. The solution shall support secure and encrypted data transfer 
capabilities using a NARA-approved protocol.  
2.2.4 Download Assets. Authorized internal and external users shall be able to export 
(download) digital special media assets in any format and file size from the system, both 
individually and in bulk. 
2.2.5 Scheduling and Disposition. The solution shall provide the capability to schedule, 
manage, and retain records for the approved time frames (based on NARA Records Control 
Schedule and General Records Schedules) and take appropriate retention and disposition 
actions (such as secure deletion or transfer) at the appropriate time. This also includes the 
ability to retain records approved for destruction beyond the period outlined in the records 
schedule if the records in question pertain to a court order, executive order, law, or approved 
business justification.   
2.2.6 Metadata. The solution shall collect and manage metadata about objects under 
management control (to include file extension, file size, creator name, date created, location 
created, unique identifier, access and use restrictions, captions, record disposition instructions, 
keywords, and checksum). Metadata may consist of descriptive data, structural data, 
administrative data, reference data, statistical data, or legal data about objects without including 
the content of the object itself.  See NARA guidance on metadata, all of which is applicable.   
2.2.7 Search. Authorized users shall be able to perform searches for digital special media assets 
within the system, based on keywords, associated metadata, embedded metadata, advanced 
search filters, file type, file name, record format, disposition status, and folder name. 
2.2.8 Organization Authorized users shall be able to organize digital special media content 
within the system using folders or collections. The solution shall control access to folders of 
corporate digital special media assets separately from folders of archival digital special 
media assets. 
2.2.9 Storage. The solution shall provide data storage and/or integration with existing cloud-
based NARA data stores. 
2.2.10 Integration. The solution shall integrate with existing NARA IT solutions (i.e., 
Google  Suite, AWS, etc.).  
2.2.11 Support. The provider shall support the system from development through disposition,  
to include (documentation, training, configuration management, business rules development  
and implementation, change management, security patching, and data migration).  

2.2.12 Data Migration. The provider shall manage the data migration from the existing DAMS. 
2.2.13 Training. The provider shall fully develop, implement, and train NARA users and  
administrators on the selected product.  
3.0 RFI Content  
3.1 RFI Questions  
Interested and capable vendors should respond detailing the following: 
1. Describe your DAMS solution(s) and indicate ability to meet each of the functional 
requirements of Section 2.2 and Attachment 1, RVTM. Provide any feedback on 
NARA’s functional requirements and identify whether any cannot be implemented 
without modifying the COTS software. Identify any possible constraints or potential 
risks to NARA’s stated objectives. 
2. Is your proposed DAMS product capable of providing the total dual-use case solution 
(managing both business records and separate archival holdings, with separate access 
and use restrictions, up to a total of 1450-2000 TB of data) without modification? If not, 
or if combining the two functions would result in a significant variation in pricing and 
functionality, please provide a separate estimated cost breakout for the different system 
or solution types you propose to meet these two needs individually. If your system is 
able to meet only one or the other use case, please explain the technical limitations that 
NARA should consider in addressing these related needs. 
3. Describe your customary commercial practices for your DAMS solution in terms of 
pricing structure and approach for implementation, licensing, support, and any unique  
circumstances wherein those would change. Describe whether your DAMS solution has 
been deployed within other Federal Civilian Agencies. Describe your experience and 
approach  to deploying and maintaining your DAMS solution (i.e., installation, 
configuration, customization, and enhancements, maintenance, technical support). 
Provide any comments or recommendations on the most suitable acquisition approach 
for this type of requirement, along with a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Cost 
estimate for the different components of any identified solutions to include licensing, 
maintenance, technical support and any professional services that should be considered 
as part of any new system implementation. 
4. Indicate whether your product is commercially available or is on the General Services 
Administration Federal Supply Schedule or other Governmentwide Acquisition 
Contract (GWAC).  
5.  What tools and metrics do you use to measure system performance?   
6. Does the SaaS provider have Voluntary Product Accessibility Template(s) version 2 
published to demonstrate how it meets the updated Section 508 accessibility 
requirements? If yes, please provide a link. If not, please explain how your product 
meets the updated Section 508 accessibility requirements.  
7. Is the solution IPv6 compliant?   
8. Would your firm be interested in giving an informational presentation to the 

government?  
9. What are the common risks and issues encountered when implementing and/or 
integrating a DAMS?  
3.1 RFI Submission Instructions  
1. Responses shall include a brief description of your company, products and services, history,
