Jennie Conroy, COR III 
9609 Medical Center Dr/1E606 
Rockville, MD 20892 
Email: Jennie.conroy@nih.gov  
Phone: 301-594-8165 
 
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved, including a description of 
the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs and the estimated 
value. 
a. Acquisition purpose and objectives.  
On August 15, 2025, the NIH Director’s Priorities 
https://www.nih.gov/aboutnih/nih-director/statements/advancing-nihs-mission-
through-unified-strategy were published with specific reference to a Real-World 
Data Platform. The priority states “Real-World Data Platform: NIH is 
establishing a robust and secure national infrastructure to integrate and link 
data from various real-world sources consistent with a deep respect for 
individual privacy rights. This new Real-World Data Platform will provide 
advanced computational analysis resources for investigators across numerous 
research areas, including neurodevelopmental disorders and chronic 
diseases.” Rather than creating a new system, it has been determined to be in 
the best interest of the government to utilize and enhance existing 
infrastructure that exists within N3C and Data COUNTS. 
During this transition phase, the Palantir platform that hosts the N3C was 
abruptly taken offline while HHS determined its acquisitions strategy for 
Palantir software. HHS recently executed a contract with Palantir allowing N3C 
to come back online publicly, reopening March 2, 2026. Based on these 
negotiations, N3C is now hosted within a different cloud provider with a 
different set of features. These changes required NCATS to pivot its focus 
away from the original objectives of integrating N3C and Data COUNTS.  
Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) Sole 
Source Justification (SSJ) 

Page 2 of 13  
The purpose of this acquisition is to provide NCATS and the community of N3C 
contributors and researchers continuity. The abrupt shutdown of the N3C 
platform was highly disruptive to researchers utilizing the N3C to fulfill 
commitments on grants, write their dissertations, and continue working on 
projects built over the past six years.  
The overarching objective of this work has been reduced from fifteen objectives 
to nine. These core objectives of integrating N3C and Data COUNTS, while 
transitioning N3C to a Dynamic Workspaces architecture, ensuring operational 
continuity, enhancing data utility for the research community, and achieving full 
compliance with all CADR requirements. To accomplish this, NCATS has 
identified objectives across nine workstreams that will need to be run by the 
Awardee. Therefore, objectives are written in alignment with the workstreams: 
Program Strategy, Governance, and Leadership: This objective provides for 
expert leadership and strategic consultation to NCATS during the bridge 
period. The work will focus on supporting NCATS in ideation, strategy, and 
planning for the future-state platform and the successful transition to a new 
vendor. This includes developing strategic roadmaps, advising on the technical 
and governance requirements for the platform recompete, and leading 
community and stakeholder engagement to manage expectations and ensure 
alignment with the new program direction. 
Modular Application Development: This objective involves the design, 
development, testing, and documentation of a set of modular, platform-agnostic 
web applications. This work is focused on creating standalone user-facing tools 
for core N3C services, including applications for registration and data access 
management, a concept set explorer, and a phenotype builder. These 
components will be built as portable, flexible applications, designed to be 
deployed on any future platform and to address CADR security and access 
control requirements. 
Platform-Agnostic Data Infrastructure: This objective focuses on the 
operations and maintenance of platform-agnostic data infrastructure. This work 
represents the comprehensive oversite of the data lifecycle, intended to be a 
portable, efficient, and well-documented service. This includes engineering 
data acquisition, data quality, linkage, and OMOP harmonization pipelines. 
Scientific and Technical Research and Support: To showcase the power of 
the N3C model, a team of Real World Evidence (RWE) Subject Matter Experts 
(SMEs) is needed to create high-caliber studies, tools, and resources. This 
objective includes providing these scientific services and supporting other high-
impact special projects that leverage the unique capabilities of the N3C 
platform. 
N3C Education and Training: Rebuilding and advancing N3C Education to 
support the evolving needs of the research community as the program 
transitions to a new platform and Dynamic Workspace model. It includes 
providing pedagogical leadership, recovering and redesigning legacy training 
materials, and developing a scalable, platform-agnostic education 
infrastructure. Core activities involve creating new registration processes, 
training tools, and a synthetic dataset; integrating updated resources such as 

Page 3 of 13  
data visualization and phenotype tools; and implementing modern content and 
learning management systems. The effort ensures that educational materials 
and training programs remain aligned with NCATS priorities, are easily 
accessible, and effectively equip users to leverage the new N3C environment.  
Enhance Capabilities of the Data COUNTS Initiative: In partnership with 
data contributing healthcare organizations, enhance the current capabilities of 
the Data COUNTS initiative to facilitate delivery of EHR data to NIH.  
Enhance Coordination of the Data COUNTS Ecosystem: Provide 
coordination and engagement of the Data COUNTS partner health institutions 
with NIH. 
Facilitate Prize Competitions: Facilitating prize competitions require a group 
of SMEs to be able to manage, evaluate, and give recommendations on 
targeted public health questions that require a high level of methodological 
rigor to answer. 
 
b. Project background.  
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is the Nation's leading Medical Research 
Agency and the primary Federal Agency whose mission is to seek fundamental 
knowledge about the nature and behavior of living systems and apply that 
knowledge to enhance health, lengthen life, and reduce illness and disability by 
supporting and making medical discoveries. The National Center for Advancing 
Translational Science (NCATS) at the NIH focuses on all aspects of the translation 
of research with an innovative pipeline of treatment discoveries for all diseases. 
NCATS' mission is to improve health through smarter science that results in more 
treatments for all people more quickly.  
 
The National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) began as a collaborative vision 
for a national data resource that turned real-world evidence into the knowledge 
urgently needed to address the pandemic. It systematically collected data derived 
from electronic health records (EHRs) and other important repositories from 
different institutions and harmonized these data in a centralized resource available 
for collaborative research. The program has since expanded beyond its initial 
narrow focus to be a resource ready to leverage real world evidence based data to 
answer questions about any disease. 
 
Building upon this successful foundation, N3C has transitioned to be composed of 
a set of robust, scalable, and secure platform-agnostic components and data 
infrastructure. These include portable data pipelines, reusable knowledge objects 
(such as phenotypes and concept sets), and modular web applications (such as for 
data access management). This approach ensures all components are designed 
for compliance with stringent government requirements for Controlled-Access Data 
Repositories (CADR). This work also focuses on preserving the core principles of 
centralized data harmonization and a secure analytical environment while 
supporting capabilities that grant institutions granular control over the use of their 
data. 
 
The Data COUNTS initiative serves as a foundational EHR data collection engine 
that ensures full provenance, traceability, and minimal data loss from health 

Page 4 of 13  
systems. Data COUNTS provides federated collection of EHR and other clinical 
data, as well as data and transmission architecture based on open-industry data 
and interoperability standards. It supports a broad array of use cases across HHS 
with appropriate adherence to data privacy, security, and data access policies. 
Together with the Data Collect Once Use Numerous TimeS (COUNTS) Initiative, 
N3C forms the foundational infrastructure of the NIH wide real-world evidence-
based research. The infrastructure will integrate vast amounts of real-world data 
from EHRs, insurance claims, pharmacies, and other sources. Building on prior 
NIH-funded efforts, the combined N3C and Data COUNTS efforts will eliminate 
redundancies from data collection, linkage, and analysis infrastructures, and will 
dramatically reduce administrative overhead by relying on a unified set of data use 
and governance agreements. It will provide direct access to advanced 
computational resources to support cutting-edge artificial intelligence/machine 
learning (AI/ML) modeling, petabyte-scale storage/compute, and high-throughput 
analytics. 
In FY 2024 the scientific and technical support services for the N3C and Data 
COUNTS were procured together on GS35F023GA-75N95023A00001 BO 14 
National Clinical Data Collaborative COUNTS (NacDacC). Procuring these 
services through one vendor on one task order has allowed the NCATS and 
ODSS to begin working together and creating efficiencies across N3C and Data 
COUNTS. In FY 2025 a 6-month sole source logical follow-on contract (GS-35F-
023GA/75N95025F00079) was awarded under FAR Subpart 8.405-6(a)(1)(i)(C). 
By continuing under one unified task, NCATS and ODSS could economically and 
efficiently make changes to the N3C and Data COUNTS programs to allow them 
to fulfil the vision of the NIH Director’s Real- World Data Platform priority.  
During this transition phase, the Palantir platform that hosts the N3C was 
abruptly taken offline while HHS determined its acquisitions strategy for Palantir 
software. HHS recently executed a contract with Palantir allowing N3C to come 
back online publicly, reopening March 2, 2026. Based on these negotiations, 
N3C is now hosted within a different cloud provider with a different set of 
features. These changes required NCATS to pivot its focus away from the 
original objectives of integrating N3C and Data COUNTS. A sole-source award to 
the existing vendor through the same GSA contract is needed to allow time to 
accomplish the initial integration objectives while also rebuilding N3C based on 
HHS’s new requirements for Palantir environments. Competing the requirement 
now would add unacceptable additional cost, delay, complexity, or uncertainty of 
execution.

Attachment B – Business Associate Agreement 
 
 
I. Authority: 
 
Pursuant to 45 C.F.R. § 164.502(e), the Indian Health Service (IHS), as a covered entity, is 
required to enter into an agreement with a “business associate,” as defined by 45 C.F.R. § 
160.103, under which the business associate must agree to appropriately safeguard Protected 
Health Information (PHI) that it will use and disclose when performing functions, activities or 
services pursuant to its contract with the IHS.   
 
By signing Number/Task Order Number> <Vendor Name                                 >                              
agrees that it is a Business Associate and will comply with the terms below, in addition to other 
applicable Contract terms and conditions, and applicable law, relating to the safekeeping, use, 
and disclosure of PHI.  This Appendix comprises the Business Associate Agreement. 
 
II. Definitions : 
 
The following terms shall have the same meaning as those terms in 45 C.F.R. Part 160 and Part 
164, which are the federal regulations implementing the Health Insurance Portability and 
Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), as amended: Breach, Designated Record Set, Disclosure, 
Health Care Operations, Individual, Minimum Necessary, Notice of Privacy Practices, PHI, 
Required by Law, Secretary, Security Incident, Subcontractor, Unsecured PHI, and Use. 
 
A.  Business Associate. “Business Associate” shall generally have the same meaning as the 
term “business associate” at 45 C.F.R. § 160.103, and in reference to the party to this 
Agreement shall mean <Vendor Name>. 
 
B.  Covered Entity.  “Covered Entity” shall generally have the same meaning as the term 
“covered entity” at 45 C.F.R. § 160.103, and in reference to the party to this Agreement, 
shall mean the IHS. 
 
C.  HIPAA Rules.  “HIPAA Rules” shall mean the Privacy, Security, Breach Notification, and 
Enforcement Rules at 45 C.F.R. Part 160 and Part 164. 
 
D.  Master Patient Index (MPI). The “Master Patient Index” or “MPI” is composed of a 
unique list of patients and a current list of medical centers where each patient has been 
seen. This enables the sharing of patient data between operationally and regionally diverse 
systems. Each record (or index entry) on the MPI contains a small amount of patient data 
used to identify individual entries. 
 
The mission of the MPI is to uniquely identify a patient and to “link” that patient’s data 
throughout the IHS facilities using the Integration Control Number (ICN). The MPI is the 
authoritative source of a patient’s ICN, the enterprise-wide identifier for IHS facilities and 
the key to accessing a patient’s record. The accuracy of patient information and patient 
identification directly affects clinical, administrative, billing, and interdepartmental 
processes. 
 
III. Obligations and Activities of Business Associate: 
 
A.  Compliance: Business Associate agrees not use or disclose PHI other than as authorized 
by the Agreement or as required by law.  Business Associate acknowledges that it is 
directly liable under the HIPAA Rules and subject to civil and, in some cases, criminal  
penalties for making uses and disclosures of PHI that are not authorized by the Agreement 
or required by law.  Business Associate agrees that it will require all of its agents, 

2 
Attachment B – Business Associate Agreement 
 
employees, subsidiaries, and affiliates, to whom Business Associate provides PHI, or who 
create or receive PHI on behalf of Business Associate for Covered Entity, to comply with 
the HIPAA Rules and to enter into written agreements with Business Associate that 
provide the same restrictions, terms, and conditions as set forth in the Agreement. 
 
B.  Subcontractors: In accordance with 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(e) (1) (ii) and 
164.308(b)(2), which govern relations with subcontractors, Business Associate agrees to 
ensure that any subcontractors that create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI on behalf of 
Business Associate agree to the same restrictions, terms, and conditions that apply to 
Business Associate with respect to such PHI. 
 
C.  Safeguarding PHI: Business Associate shall develop and use appropriate procedural, 
physical, and electronic safeguards to protect against the use or disclosure of PHI in a 
manner not authorized by this Agreement or required by law. Business Associate will limit 
any use, disclosure, or request for use or disclosure of PHI to the minimum amount 
necessary to accomplish the intended purpose of the use, disclosure, or request. 
 
D.  Safeguarding Electronic PHI: Business Associate agrees to use appropriate safeguards, 
as set forth in Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to electronic PHI, to prevent 
use or disclosure of electronic PHI other than as authorized by this Agreement or required 
by law. 
 
E.  Reporting Use or Disclosures Not Authorized By this Agreement or Required by 
Law: Business Associate agrees to report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI 
not authorized by this Agreement or required by law within thirty (30) days of discovering 
the use or disclosure, or any security incident of which it becomes aware.  In addition, 
Business Associate shall mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect that is 
known to Business Associate of the use, disclosure, or security incident. 
 
F.  Reporting of Breach: In accordance with the policy of the Department of Health and 
Human Services, Business Associate will report, within one hour of discovery, all 
suspected or confirmed breaches to Covered Entity. 
 
G. Notification of Breach of Unsecured PHI: In addition to the above, Business Associate 
shall notify Covered Entity of a breach, as set forth in 45 C.F.R. §164.410, of the security 
of any unsecured PHI that Business Associate received from, or created or received on 
behalf of, Covered Entity within thirty (30) calendar days after the discovery of the breach 
by Business Associate, its employees, officers, and/or other agents, unless notification is 
specifically excepted by 45 C.F.R. § 164.412. 
 
1. Requirements of Notice. Such notice shall include, to the extent possible, the 
identification of each individual whose unsecured PHI has been, or is reasonably 
believed by Business Associate to have been, accessed, acquired, or disclosed 
during such breach; a brief description of the circumstances of the breach of 
security, including the date of the breach and the date of Business Associate’s 
discovery of the breach; and the type of unsecured PHI involved in the breach. 
Business Associate agrees to provide any other available information that 
Covered Entity is required to include in notification to the individual under 45 
§164.404(c). In the event notification is delayed, evidence demonstrating the 
necessity of the delay shall accompany the notification. 
 
H. Individual Access to PHI: Business Associate shall maintain a designated record set for 
each individual for whom it maintains PHI. In accordance with an individual’s right to 

3 
Attachment B – Business Associate Agreement 
 
access his or her PHI, Business Associate shall make available all PHI in the individual’s 
designated record set to the individual to whom that information pertains, or, upon the 
request of the individual, to that individual’s authorized representative, as necessary to 
satisfy Covered Entity’s obligations under 45 C.F.R. § 164.524. Availability to access PHI 
shall be made within five (5) calendar days of receipt of a valid request. 
 
I. Accounting of Disclosures: Business Associate shall maintain records of PHI received 
from, or created or received on behalf of, Covered Entity and shall document subsequent 
uses and disclosures of such information by Business Associate. Business Associate shall, 
within five (5) calendar days after receiving a request from Covered Entity, provide to 
Covered Entity such information as Covered Entity may require to fulfill its obligations to 
account for disclosures of PHI pursuant to 45 C.F.R. § 164.528. 
 
J.   Amendment of PHI: Business Associate shall, within five (5) calendar days of a request 
by Covered Entity, make PHI available to Covered Entity for Covered Entity to fulfill its 
obligations under 45 C.F.R. § 164.526 to amend PHI and shall, as directed by Covered 
Entity, within five (5) calendar days of receipt of such direction, incorporate any 
amendments into PHI held by Business Associate. In addition, Business Associate shall 
ensure incorporation of any such amendments into PHI held by its agents or subcontractors 
within ten (10) days of such direction, and shall notify Covered Entity within five (5) 
calendar days of when those agents or subcontractors have completed the incorporation of 
the amendments. Business Associate shall forward to Covered Entity all requests to amend 
PHI that it receives directly from individuals within five (5) calendar days of its receipt of 
a request. 
 
K. Carrying out Covered Entity’s Obligations: To the extent Business Associate is to carry 
out one or more of Covered Entity’s obligation(s) under Subpart E of 45 C.F.R. Part 164, 
Business Associate agrees to comply with the requirements of Subpart E that apply to 
Covered Entity in the performance of such obligation(s). 
 
L.  Disclosures for Verifying Compliance: Upon request, Business Associate shall permit 
access by the Secretary and Covered Entity during normal business hours to its facilities, 
books, records, accounts, and any other sources of information, including PHI and any 
agreements that it has with subcontractors, vendors, and/or other agents relating to the use 
and disclosure of PHI received from Covered Entity, or created or received by Business 
Associate on behalf of Covered Entity, for purposes of determining both Business 
Associate’s and Covered Entity’s compliance with the HIPAA Rules. 
 
IV. Permitted Uses and Disclosures by Business Associate: 
 
A.  Business Associate shall not use or disclose PHI except to perform functions, activities, or 
services on behalf of Covered Entity as provided for in the Contract, this Agreement, the 
HIPAA Rules, or other applicable law. 
 
B.  Business Associate agrees that it may use or disclose PHI on behalf of Covered 
Entity only:

2.   For the purposes of treatment, payment or health care operations unless Covered

C.F.R. § 164.522; or 
3.   Without an authorization or consent, if in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.510, 45 
C.F.R. § 164.512, 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e), 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(f), or 45 C.F.R. §

C.  Business Associate shall use and disclose PHI in compliance with each applicable

D.  Business Associate agrees to make uses, disclosures, and requests for PHI consistent with

The intended procurement is classified under NAICS code 541990 with a Size Standard $19.5M 
 
REGULATORY AUTHORITY  
 

Synopsis No.   75N98026Q00190 
 
Page 3 of 4  
The resultant contract will include all applicable provisions and clauses in effect through the 
Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2005-99-1, July 16, 2018. This acquisition is conducted under 
the procedures as prescribed in FAR subpart 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures at an amount 
not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold ($350,000). 
 
STATUTORY AUTHORITY  
This acquisition is conducted under the authority of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 
Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures, Subpart 13.106-1 (b) (1), Soliciting from a single 
source and is not expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. Contracts awarded using 
FAR Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6-
Competition Requirements. 
 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
       Title: Genomic Regulatory Network of the Retina 
 
Background and Purpose 
 
Precise gene expression patterns, which are critical for maintaining structure and function in 
the retinal cells, are controlled by regulatory networks that comprise of multiple levels 
including topology of the genome, regulatory sequences, transcription factors and signaling 
proteins. Next generation sequencing methods have now made it possible to perform genome-
wide studies of gene expression, genetic variations and corresponding regulatory proteins. We 
are interested in elucidating the nature of gene regulatory networks during development and 
how these are disrupted in aging and disease to help us design novel treatment paradigms for 
blinding largely incurable retinal and macular degenerative diseases. A major goal of our 
research is to integrate diverse molecular genomic datasets on genome-wide gene expression 
with regulatory factor binding, topological information and other changes in the retina during normal 
development, aging and disease conditions in humans and mice. These networks will be used to 
explore genomic regulations in the retina and understand the effect of human genetic 
generations that are associated with retinal and macular degeneration 
 
The contractor will pre-process diverse raw data generated in the lab by Next Generation 
Sequencing methods as well as those from relevant public datasets. The contractor will integrate data 
using state-of-the-art statistical modeling. 
             The contractor will generate genomic regulatory networks from this data 
- and will develop user-friendly tools to allow biologists to explore the data. 
- The contractor will identify retina-specific genomic features and explore biological and 
medical significance. 
- Finally, the contractor will attend regular meetings with the people involved in the project and 
participate in the publication of this work in peer-review journals. 
- The draft of a manuscript ready for submission is expected by the end of the period of performance. 
 
 
CLOSING STATEMENT 
 
This synopsis is not a request for competitive proposals. However, interested parties may identify 
their interest and capability to respond to this notice. Responses to this notice shall contain

A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses 
to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The information received will

will not be accepted.

DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY 
NAVAL FACILITIES ENGINEERING SYSTEMS COMMAND SOUTHWEST 
750 PACIFIC HIGHWAY 
SAN DIEGO CA 92132-5190 
 
 
IN REPLY REFER TO 
            
           J&A No. 26-221 
 
JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL 
FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
1. Contracting Activity.  
Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southwest (NAVFAC SW), 
Facilities Engineering Acquisition Division (FEAD), San Diego, California. 
2. Description of the Action Being Approved:   
Request authority to award a sole source contract, without the use of full and competition procedures, to 
Energy Technology and Service, Inc. located at 2637 Ariane Drive, San Diego, CA 92117 in support of 
the Metro Energy Generation System (MEGS).    
3. Description of Supplies/Services:   
The proposed contract will provide services to operate and maintain the MEGS for the Navy Medical 
Center San Diego (NMCSD) within the NAVFAC SW area of responsibility (AOR).  The period of 
performance for the proposed contract is an extension for 6-months. 
The MEGS is an Iconics Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System (SCADA).  MEGS provides a 
control system that continuously monitors the operation and performance of the NMCSD Co-Generation 
(COGEN) utility system.  The COGEN system provides continuous, reliable, on-site utilities (electrical 
power, water, steam, compressed air) for the NMCSD.  The system includes generation units, control 
systems, automatic transfer switching, emissions and compliance equipment, and integration with 
NMCSD’s existing electrical infrastructure.   
          E s t i m a t e d  D o l l a r  V a l u e  
The estimated dollar value of this contract action is approximately $255,00.00 based on the Independent 
Government Estimate (IGE), utilizing historical data, input from subject matter experts, and market 
research. The Government estimate and period of performance are described below: 
 
PERIOD 
PERIOD OF 
PERFORMANCE 
 
LABOR

TOTAL 
BASE  3/25/26 – 9/30/2026 $215,000.00 $40,000.00 $255,000.00 
     
TOTAL    $255,000.00 
 
 
 


J&A No. 26-221 
2 
4. Statutory Authority Permitting Other Than Full and Open Competition: 
The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 USC § 3204 (a)(2), as 
implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, 
which permits contracting without providing for full and open competition in situations where (1) an 
unusual and compelling urgency precludes full and open competition and (2) delay in award of a contract 
would result in serious injury, financial or other, to the Government. 
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority:  
NMCSD is a 24/7 critical medical facility supporting active-duty service members, veterans, and their 
families.  The facility requires an on-site generation system capable of delivering uninterrupted utilities 
(electrical power, water, steam, compressed air) to critical care areas, operating rooms, and life-support. 
The MEGS must seamlessly integrate all utility systems without operational downtime, while providing 
redundant and load-balanced power generation with automated fault detection and correction. The risk of 
failure to meet these mission critical requirements to the support Naval Medical Center San Diego would 
pose unacceptable risk to the health and safety of patients and Government personnel. 
Historically, MEGS support has been provided via contract N6247325P3803, awarded by FEAD San 
Diego on 25 SEP 2025.  That contract is set to expire on 24 MAR 2026.  The prior MEGS support was 
provided via contract W912DY-18-D-0003/P0003, awarded by the USACE on 18 NOV 2015.  That 
contract expired 03 DEC 2020.  Following the USACE contract, MEGS support has been provided as a 
rider to various NMCSD construction and maintenance contracts. For example, the NMCSD Automated 
Transfer Switch (ATS) upgrade and maintenance contract (N62473-22-F-4456) provided MEGS support.   
The period of performance of the proposed contract is six (6) months, which does not exceed the 
maximum time allowed for sole source acquisitions based on the unusual and compelling urgency 
statutory authority.  The proposed contract action will allow sufficient time to conduct a competitive 
acquisition via the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) existing Utility Monitoring and Control 
System (UMCS) Programmatic Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) V. 
A site survey is underway to assess the existing MEGS conditions.  The results of the survey will 
determine the best, most cost effective way to define the requirement and implement needed 
improvements.    
The incumbent contractor, Energy Technology and Service, Inc. (ETS), has been the primary provider of 
MEGS support.  Consequently, ETS has unique and specialized knowledge of the system to ensure 
mission critical requirements are met.  No other contractor could provide the localized knowledge and 
immediate services necessary to operate and maintain the existing MEGS System without a significant 
lead time and unacceptable delay.  Such a delay would result in serious injury to the Government by 
creating an undue risk of loss of vital services at the Naval Medical Center San Diego.   
Pursuant to the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(2), as implemented by FAR 6.302-2, this Justification & 
Approval (J&A) requests the authority to limit competition to this contractor and award a one-time 
contract based on the unusual and compelling urgency to provide services without disruption or impact to 
the mission for Navy installations within the NAVFAC SW AOR. The contractor is capable of satisfying 
the agency’s unusual and compelling requirement starting on March 25, 2026. 
 

J&A No. 26-221 
3 
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable:  
 
NAVFAC conducted a limited market survey, including outreach to several energy generation and 
engineering firms, review of GSA Schedule offerings, and analysis of similar government procurements.  
No other vendor or manufacturer demonstrated the ability to meet all NMCSD’s technical, environmental, 
and mission resiliency requirements without significant phase-in/ramp-up time.  Due to the urgency of 
this project, standard market research procedures for other qualified firms could not be conducted in 
accordance with FAR Part 10.  Other than full and open competition is necessitated by an unusual or 
compelling urgency under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 3204(a)(2) as implemented in FAR 6.302-2 and 
offers were requested from as many potential sources as was practicable under the circumstances in 
accordance with FAR 6.302-2(c)(2). The planned action covered by this J&A meets an exception to the 
synopsis requirements per FAR Part 5.202(a)(2). The approved J&A will be released in accordance with 
FAR 6.305(b).   
 
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost:  
The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the services covered by 
this J&A will be fair and reasonable. 
 
8. Actions taken to Remove Barriers to Future Competition:  
 
NAVFAC will utilize the pending COGEN Site Survey assessing the existing SCADA system’s 
conditions to the best, most cost effective way to implement any new improvements.   This is a one-time 
extension of the existing contract that is necessary to avoid delay that would cause serious injury, 
financial or other, to the Government, and is necessary to provide immediate, continuous, reliable, and 
compliant on-site electrical power generation for the NMCSD. It is anticipated that the Government will 
utilize US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMCS) 
Programmatic MATOC V contract vehicle for this requirement, which will be competitively awarded.

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS

INSTITUTE FOR LEARNING, EDUCATION AND DEVELOPMENT 

CLOSED CAPTION PRO ENCORDER SUPPORT SERVICES

Version 2.0

Dated

April 6, 2026

Background:    The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Institute for Learning, Education, and Development (ILEAD) maintains a broadcast facility in St. Louis Missouri, to include live satellite video delivery. ILEAD uses EEG closed caption encoders and the EEG iCAP caption delivery service to provide real-time closed captioning for live satellite video delivery.

ILEAD previously replaced their EEG HD490 caption encoders with a total of (5) EEG HD492-O-O1G Closed Caption Pro Encoders that requires annual support.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is currently undergoing a reorganization that may result in future changes to its organizational structure, processes, responsibilities, and priorities. Such changes could affect the customers, services, or support described in this Product Description (PD). Accordingly, the Contractor shall remain adaptable and responsive to evolving VA requirements and work in close coordination with the Government to assess and implement necessary adjustments, as needed. Any resulting changes will be completed by bilateral contract modification.

Applicable Documents: No documents.

Product Specifications and Deliverables:  

  

The Contractor shall provide annual Encoder Pro HD492 and Encoder Pro Card OpenGear Annual Support and firmware updates on (5) EEG HD492-O-O1G Closed Caption Pro Encoders.  The EEG HD492-O-O1G Closed Caption Pro Encoders salient characteristics:

• EEG iCap connectivity for secure real-time captioning over a standard broadband connection without the use of dial-up phone lines or external audio couplers.

• Connectivity to EEG’s Cloud-hosted Automatic Captioning service, Lexi.

• Encoding of caption data sourced from previously encoded video sources, two RS232 serial ports, or a dial-up modem (optional)

• CCMatch™ module for perfect synchronization of captions and program A/V (Add-On)

• Encoding of CTA-708 standard closed captions from native 708 or legacy 608 (SD) sources

• Caption relocation from configurable GPI triggers

• Modules for web-streaming and scoreboard connectivity

• Local logging of caption input for future reference

• Relay-bypassed master video and auxiliary video paths

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS)

1. Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR).  

  

a. Primary COR.  See DITCO Additional Text G1 - Points of Contact (POC) 

b. Alternate COR (ACOR).  See DITCO Additional Text G1 - POC

c. Property Administrator (PA) See DITCO Additional Text G1 - POC 

2. Contract Title.  Continuous Monitoring Analytical Tool Set (CMATS) Development and Sustainment

3. Background.  The Department of Defense (DoD) implements a multi-tiered cybersecurity risk management process to protect United States (U.S.) interests, spanning from the enterprise level DoD to individual Information Systems (IS). This process is guided by DoD Instruction (DoDI) 8500.1, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-39, and the Cybersecurity Risk Management Construct (CSRMC), previously the Risk Management Framework (RMF) established in DoDI 8510.01. 

CMATS Is a suite of Government off-the-shelf (GOTS) software that provides data which contributes to global and organizational views of inventory, compliance, vulnerability, and risk. CMATS enables near-real-time cybersecurity visualization by integrating data from various DoD Enterprise Cyber Security applications, and it supports automated processes used in support of cyber blue force tracking, risk management, near-real time awareness of devices and software inventory and configuration compliance. CMATS enables the Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy as part of the DoD Continuous Monitoring Strategy, and it provides DoD decision makers with device attribution data required for mission systems to enable ISCM. The attribution data provides Situational Awareness (SA) and Command and Control (C2) at all levels of the DoD such that system property custodians, users, and administrators can visualize data for endpoints under their purview and maintain attribution information meaningful to them, but that same data can be used to build SA and C2 capabilities at all higher echelons, up to the Secretary of Defense (SECDEF). 

The tools within the CMATS suite are: 

The Continuous Monitoring Risk Scoring (CMRS) system which aggregates, correlates and normalizes the vulnerability and configuration state of DoD Information Technology (IT) systems by providing measures of security control deployments and compliance including Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG), patch compliance and deployed configuration settings.  The current CMRS system is a Microsoft (MS) Structure Query Language (SQL) / Internet Information Server (IIS) application. The plan is to migrate the application to Platform as a Service (PaaS) in a Joint Warfighter Cloud Capability (JWCC) Azure Cloud environment.

The Cyber Operational Attribute Management System (COAMS) contains a central repository of a dynamically maintained hierarchies of names used in reporting of cyber data which are dynamically exposed in Application Program Interfaces (APIs) as updates are made. COAMS currently contains hierarchies of organization, location, system, and other names. The current COAMS system is an MS SQL Server / IIS application. The plan is to migrate the application to PaaS in a JWCC Azure Cloud environment.

The Enterprise User Management (EUM) system is a central permission store register that manages user and non-user COAMS-based permissions for CMATS portfolio applications. EUM maintains the last login time, per user, as well as providing account lockout status and enabling account resets.  The EUM system is an MS application that creates and manages user attributes and permissions. The plan is to migrate the application to PaaS in a JWCC Azure Cloud environment.

The Information Assurance Vulnerability Management (IAVM) system is a capability used by analysts in DoD Cyber Defense Command (DCDC) and its components to analyze, filter, prioritize, and disseminate US Cyber Command directives (“IAVMs”) that require DoD agencies to apply certain patches to remediate high-risk vulnerabilities. The title and business logic currently implemented by the IAVM system will change in the coming years and both the name and the functionality of the IAVM system will need to change to address the changes.  The current IAVM system uses an IIS application back end. The plan is to migrate the application to PaaS in a JWCC Azure Cloud environment.

DATT is an endpoint application that brands and maintains C2 (C2 metadata, selected from COAMS hierarchies on individual DoD devices where it is exposed to enterprise sensors.   

Central Attribution Management Portal (CAMP) will allow users to centrally manage asset attribution data across multiple enterprise reporting systems and endpoint management solutions. CAMP will aggregate and standardize tag data from multiple DoD enterprise systems, to include DATT endpoint attributes and provide users with tools to fill gaps in missing attribution data, resolve tag discrepancies, automate and simplify tagging of endpoints, map existing datapoints to accurate tag values, and report on existing endpoints. In future iterations CAMP will integrate with endpoint management tools to synchronize with DATT endpoint attributes. The CAMP application is a PaaS SQL/IIS.

Data Analytics Test Lab is primarily used in support of Configuration Management (CM) and concept development/validation for the production systems within the Program Acquisition Executive( PAE) -Cyber, Cyber Analytics Division (ID6) portfolio of capabilities. The ID6 lab also supports research, development, testing, and evaluation of technologies in the Cyber Analytics space, interoperability between current and possible future solutions, and advanced troubleshooting of production representative system baselines in support of resolving operational issues. The Data Analytics lab hosts on-premises and a JWCC Azure Cloud presence.

The Endpoint Patch Management Service (EPMS) receives automated updates from the software vendors (Original Equipment Manufacturers) via a patch-packaging vendor solution from the Internet onto the Non-Secure Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNET) and then utilizing Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) supplied infrastructure to move these patches to Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNET) for availability to DoD for all DoD Information Network (DoDIN) customers

Date:  August 27, 2024  
To:  Ece Kilic, AOC Project Manager Work Order Number:  90305.018 
From:  Lonnie Hovey, AIA, FAPT Contract Number:  AOC19C3007 
Subject:  Comments on ICR Final Report Project:  President’s Rm. Advisory Panel 
CC:  M. Oehrlein, B. Ramsay, T. Williams, File  
 
Members of the President’s Room Advisory Panel reviewed the PHASE 1-3 DRAFT REPORT on the PRESIDENT’S 
ROOM CEILING ANALYSIS submitted August 2, 2024 by Integrated Conservation Resources, Inc. (ICR), and 
provided the following overall and specific comments and suggestions to improve the report for the project record. 
Overall comments: 
• The ICR report needs more explanation to develop a compelling case for the recommendation to shore the 
ceiling. The slides shown in the August 16 presentation will bolster this explanation, but more is likely 
needed.  
• The ICR report needs an Executive Summary to concisely describe the reasons for testing, the testing done, 
findings, and recommendations.  
• Similarly, the goals of paint analysis should be described in the final ICR report to focus the information 
presented. Slides in the GPS presentation outlined their goals and findings very clearly. 
• The report should answer the question: Which NDT methods are reliable predictors of voids behind the 
plaster, and which are not? 
• The entire ICR report needs copy editing to eliminate spelling errors and other typographical errors. 
• The recommendation is reiterated that CUA’s report be updated to provide greater clarity in what they are 
measuring (mobility) vs. what they are inferring (delamination). The report mischaracterizes their findings in 
the absence of physical data (which they did not have at the time of their testing). If this is not updated, ICR’s 
report needs to make a clear statement prior to CUA’s report explaining this difference.  
• The report needs a prioritized and clear list of recommendations, including clarification of what constitutes 
“monitoring,” recommended frequency of “regular monitoring,” and by whom. Clear, actionable steps for AOC 
must be provided. 
• Put bookmarks in the final report pdf, in order to navigate 300+ pages. 
Specific comments: 
• Page 3: Brumidi worked in the Capitol primarily between 1855-60 and intermittently after. 
• Page 4, para. 1: “The ceiling is assumed to be a brick vault 12” deep” – did ICR receive original drawings, 
and can we update to state what drawings show? 
• Page 4, para. 2 and Fig. 3: can we update based on recent testing? 
• Page 7: what is the difference between “deflected” and “detached” plaster as defined here?  
• Page 7: SLDV definition – add that it uses sound to create the displacement.

• Page 9: Not certain why you have reached this conclusion re: alterations of the interstitial space. Re: 
systems in the ceiling of the room. MO indicates that there are none except electrical and old gas piping. 
There is no plumbing in the space above, the roof drains are vertical and located in exterior wall chases. 
Those that have been rerouted to the interior are still vertical, not concealed in the floors.  
• Page 11: 1921: At some undocumented point in time after the failure of the plaster at the center of the ceiling 
a painted canvas was installed to cover the new plaster. The painting was apparently not well executed and 
with the permission of the prior curator, Barbara Wolanin, the canvas was removed during the 1995 
conservation work. It was left in the curator’s office, current disposition unknown. 
• Page 11: 1920-28 The fresco repairs by Comins would have required removal of the damaged plaster. Text 
in GPS report indicates “repainting.” 
• Page 13: “Any offsets in the cracks were smaller than the density of the laser scan” – what was the density? 
Please provide the density of the laser scanning. There is no description anywhere in the document. 
• Page 14: somewhere please indicate that all photographs taken during the investigation have been 
submitted to the AOC. We assume, but it is not stated. 
• Page 14, Fig. 7: Use an arrow to clarify area of retouching (or clarify in caption)  
• Page 15, Fig. 8: Use arrows to identify areas of efflorescence (professionals know, but others don’t)  as it 
looks quite similar to the figure’s veil. 
• Page 15, Figs 9-10: Need arrows (maybe multiple colors for Fig. 10 if multiple conditions shown)  
• Fig. 11: Please document the locations of the reveals in an overall plan.  
• Page 18, Fig. 12: Fix caption to be more precise about red and orange areas. Fig. 12 is a map of sounds, not 
a map of attachment/detachment. 
• Page 19, 20, Fig. 13 & 14: Is this the 2003 data or the most recent data? Please add date and clarify that 
the mapping represents only vibration differentials not areas of detached plaster. 
• Page 19, 20, Fig. 13 & 14: Need units on scale. I don’t see any colors in the range besides blue and red. No 
purple. Even the light red in the image isn’t represented on the scale. Clarify.  
• Page 20, Fig. 14 – remove “detachment” from caption, as this hasn’t been shown. This is the same image as 
in Fig 13, showing mobility/vibration – not detachment. 
• Page 20: Discussion of 2003 (page 19) or 04 (?) and 2023 comparison again characterizes the scans as 
detachment. Please correct. 
• Page 21, para. 1 – plaster ceiling is 1-1.5” thick. 
• Page 21, Crack Mapping, Methodology: what about cracks between 0.14-0.016” thick? (typo?) 
o How do you differentiate between “cracks”, “crazing”, and “fissures”? 
• Page 21, Findings: “suspected” correlation between sounding and giornata is unfounded per Figure 14, 
which shows giornata in blue and red areas. The giornata are in both low and high areas and cross over both 
areas. 
• Page 22 and 25: “signs of water infiltration” these have not been previously described or discussed. Where 
are these locations and what are the indicators of moister infiltration?

• Page 26-27: Reference Figs 21 and 22 in the text. Clarify that “LM” and “MM” are the low and medium 
mobility samples. Please include the photos of the high mobility sample removal. Please use the sample 
numbers in the text and figures and provide a full ceiling image to show the sample locations.  
• Page 26 Findings: mortar remained attached to the back of the plaster sample, but the base coat did not 
appear keyed into the mortar joints. How can this be? 
• Page 28: Does the petrography help us understand the causes of observed cracking?  
• Page 29: Isn’t high mobility also correlated to plaster thickness? 
• Page 29, para. 2: Water entering plaster from the brick? New information – what is the basis? Need to 
explain earlier in the report. The signs of water infiltration have not been previously described. The posit that 
moisture from the brick has weakened the plaster is not substantiated.  
• Page 29: Fig. 25 seems out of place and comes from nowhere. Figure 25 is unexplained, what surface 
conditions? Should be back in Observations/Findings, not analysis. What is the basis for this? What “surface 
conditions” lead to the inference of moisture infiltration? “substantial portions of the ceiling are detached” is 
not substantiated. 
• Page 29, para. 3: “though substantial portions of the ceiling are detached” – this is not supported by the data. 
Rewrite. 
• Page 29: detachment was between brick and base coat. Not consistent w/photos, which show thin layer of 
base coat on brick. 
• Page 30, Fig. 26: last column – find other words for “attached”, “damaged”, and “borderline” – these are NDT 
results and need to describe vibration, not inferred attachment. 
• Page 30, Fig. 26: Samples 10, 12, and 13 do not have good correlation. 3 out of 13.  
• Page 30, Fig. 26: Add plaster thickness as a column. 
• Page 30, Fig. 26: Sample 13: what does “(AP)” mean? Include all samples in the chart. 
• Page 30: Fix caption of Fig. 27 – does not indicate detachment; indicates sound and vibration, respectively. 
Include locations of drills on both images in Fig 27. 
• Page 31, Fig. 28: remove “attached” from caption. Does not indicate attachment; indicates sound.  
• Page 30-32, Figs. 27 - 29: correct descriptions. The mapping does not indicate detachment or compromised 
plaster. Detachment is being surmised by interpretation of all data. 
• Page 31: “worsening conditions” – change to “possible” or “apparently worsening conditions”. Some areas 
look like they got better! Are you sure the scales and density of data are the same? (scales should be 
displayed in image) 
• Page 31, Fig. 29: remove “attachment” and “detachment” from caption. These are sounds and vibrations.  
• Page 32: Re: “plaster was likely the same across the whole ceiling,” add “…but this has not been confirmed 
by sampling plaster in the areas of fresco. 
• Page 32: We suggest more rigor in describing how plaster findings relate to observations: cracking, etc. 
Plaster has “deficiencies”, but how does this impact its appearance or performance?

August 27, 2024 Page 4 90305.018 
  
UNCLASSIFIED // For Official Use Only 
Document2 
• Page 33 Recommendations: We suggest more drilling in the frescos to provide more data and correlation to 
support shoring ceiling. What is the significance of more voids? 
o Describe in detail why vibration and environmental monitoring is needed. What information will be 
provided, how will it be used, and why is it important?  
o How do you propose to install monitors in the brick vault? 
o GPR at Press Room above needs to include drilling to understand substrates.  
o Two months of monitoring is insufficient. Environmental needs to be through a full cycle of heating 
and air conditioning; measurement of air flow and resulting micro-conditions in the room could also 
be useful. Vibration during only a recess period when few people are in the building would be almost 
useless. 
o Installing shoring of the ceiling is unlikely to be palatable to AOC or the Senate leadership. An 
alternative may be to suspend use of the room until further investigation or treatment can be 
completed, realizing that this will provide only life safety and not ensure preservation of the  historic 
decorative work. 
o Provide details of a long-term monitoring program for the ceiling; what, how, and who. 
• ANA Report: Appendix A and B need clarity in results reported: not attachment but sounds. (Attachment is 
inferred, but sound is what’s measured.) 
• Page 216 (CUA report): Abstract: SLDV identifies areas of higher mobility, not detachment. Detachment is 
inferred. Need clarity in this language. (That hasn’t been shown yet.)  
• Explain why areas of plaster sampling and drilling were infilled with Plaster of Paris, as opposed to another 
material.  
• Page 289: Highbridge report Exec summary states there is shrinkage cracking in the plaster but that it’s 
normal. Fully carbonated and cured. Put in ICR report; currently, it doesn’t fully characterize the plaster the 
way the ICR report does.  
• Page 293: “the base of each layer is a cohesive break within the scratch coat” – this is worth noting that in all 
4”x4” samples, there were no voids. Need to present this data somehow/somewhere, perhaps at end of table 
in ICR report. 
• Page 342: reviewed plan and section of Press Gallery S-316: what did you find? Is it consistent with ANA’s 
sketch? 
• Page 345: what did you find re: MEP in President’s Room ceiling? (Or no info?)  
• Page 357: recommend providing plan with just drilling and samples (red) to focus on plaster (keep plan with 
red and green for comprehensive picture of phase 3 sampling) 
• Page 357: We have 14 drill holes, plus calibration, plus 4 samples to show mobility vs voids, thickness, etc. 
Show all in one table. (Table currently has only 13 drill locations.) Section is missing data for HM2 without 
explanation. Explain function of “calibration” hole and whether we have data from that to include. 
• Page 357: PR-W4 “removed from analysis”. Any explanation for observed anomalies? Possible repairs? 
Does it correlate to any data from previous analyses or reports? 
• Need a map of attached, detached (voids)

Respectfully submitted.

Amendment 1
I. Opportunity Description
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Defense Sciences Office (DSO) is 
issuing a Disruption Opportunity (DO), inviting submissions of innovative basic or applied 
research concepts in the technical domain of high assurance artificial intelligence systems. This 
DO is issued under the Program Announcement for Disruptioneering, DARPA-PA-25-07. All 
awards will be made in the form of an Other Transaction (OT) for Prototype project. The total 
award value for the combined Phase 1 base (Feasibility Study) and Phase 2 option (Proof of 
Concept) is limited to $2,000,000. This total award value includes Government funding and 
performer cost share if required or proposed.
To view the DARPA Program Announcement (PA) for Disruptioneering, visit SAM.gov
under solicitation number DARPA-PA-25-07:
https://sam.gov/opp/bae5fa32f4ee4cdb9a070a14309b2c66/view. 
A. Introduction
CLARA is an exploratory, fundamental research program that aims to create high assurance, 
broadly applicable AI systems of systems. This will be accomplished by creating a scientific, 
theory-driven architectural foundation for the hierarchical composition of a wide variety of 
both Machine Learning (ML) and Automated Reasoning (AR), also known as Knowledge 
Representation and Reasoning, subsystems. CLARA seeks to create a foundation that is 
algorithmic, highly reusable, and computationally scalable. For CLARA, AI systems of systems 
means systems that are hierarchically composed of constituent subsystems that employ ML and 
AR techniques and also contain both ML and AR models whose outputs are composed to create 
the overall system response. Assurance here means verifiability with strong explainability to 
humans, based on automated logical proofs and hierarchical, vetted logic building blocks. 
DARPA anticipates that successful performers in this program will combine innovations such as 
higher order logic, probabilistic logic, logical expressivity, hierarchically structured knowledge 
representation, and interoperable integration of AR and ML. The range of practically important 
ML and AR techniques and associated model families (termed “kinds” here and fully listed out 
in section I.H.) that will be explored within this program as constituents for hierarchical 
composition includes, but is not limited to, Neural Networks (NN), Bayesian ML, Reinforcement 
Learning (RL), Generalized Additive Models (GAM), Logic Programs (LP), Classical logic, and 
Answer Set Programs (ASP). Here, LP, Classical, and ASP might also be extended by constraints, 
a.k.a. constraint programming. 
Specifically excluded from CLARA are families that do not have a viable path to computational 
scalability of model inferencing and (ML) training. An example of such a family would be 
unrestricted higher-order Classical logic. Also excluded is research that primarily results in 
evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice.
B. Background

DARPA-PA-25-07-02 CLARA Disruption Opportunity 2
While there has been extensive progress in AI systems of systems over the decades, widespread 
adoption has been impeded by the need for high assurance that has in turn been impeded by 
the stark trade-off today between ML and AR with respect to assurance and applicability. ML 
has broad applicability, i.e., low marginal cost per new functional task. A person not trained in 
AI or programming can effectively utilize an ML-based Large Language Model (LLM) system like 
ChatGPT and, using natural language, ask it to take on a new task. However, ML overall has 
weak assurance, particularly weak explainability. In contrast, AR has verifiability, with some 
kinds having strong explainability and, thus, high assurance. However, AR has relatively narrow 
applicability. A fundamental cause of this weakness in applicability is AR’s struggle with 
tractability (i.e., computational scalability) when expressiveness is high enough to encompass 
the forms of knowledge and the patterns of inferencing that ML can do. Expressiveness here 
means flexibility in the form of knowledge statements and in the patterns of reasoning with 
that knowledge.
A notable example of AR with high assurance is Logic Programs, which dominate enterprise IT 
areas such as data management, ontologies, knowledge graphs, and rule-based systems. This 
cluster of areas and associated systems has strong composability, including strong 
interoperability via automated translations and Web standards, underpinned by a theory-
driven foundation. This foundation includes mathematical results and associated analytic 
guarantees about generalizations/specializations, semantics, equivalences, proof theory, and 
computational complexity. CLARA seeks to emulate the success of DARPA’s DAML1 program 
(2000-2005), which pioneered standards and design for the semantic web through a similar 
theory-driven foundation, but in a new arena – AR-based ML. 
AR-based ML means that ML is achieved via AR where the ML is put onto a logical footing, 
including both ML inferencing and training. One way to view ML as being AR-based is that 
induction (in the sense of inductive reasoning with probabilistic generalization, rather than in 
the sense of mathematical induction/deduction) is viewed as deduction in a high-
expressiveness form of logic/AR. 
The dual requirements of high assurance and broad applicability for AR-based ML pose two key 
technical challenges for the program. The first, Applicability, is how to extend high assurance 
(of the type available for Logic Programs) widely to various ML/AR kinds and across a 
composition of heterogeneous subsystems that are based on those kinds. The second, 
Tractability, is how to break the tension between expressiveness and tractability in the relevant 
kinds of high assurance AR. 
There are several examples of systems that give preliminary hope that AR-based ML systems 
can be built, but they have significant limitations and have yet to fully overcome the 
Applicability and Tractability challenges. The DeepProbLog2 system and subsequent follow-up 
DeepStochLog3 system show how to do ML inferencing based on Bayesian probabilistic Logic 
Programs (“Bayesian-LP”) and how to do limited integration of that with Neural Networks ML.

C. Technical Areas
CLARA is composed of two Technical Areas (TAs). Each proposal should address only one 
Technical Area. An institution/organization (e.g., a single university or a single organization ) 
may not be selected for both TA1 and TA2. A program-wide set of activities will be developed 
and supported by an Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) team, who will also 
perform reviews and evaluations of many of the performers’ deliverables. IV&V will be 
separately competed and is not part of this solicitation. 
TA1 is the primary area of work. Each TA1 performer will create one or more new approaches 
for high assurance ML/AR, which are AR-based ML based. Each approach will modify and tightly 
compose a few kinds of ML and AR selected from those listed in section I.H. During this 
program, TA1 performers will: 
Develop a theory for high assurance ML/AR approaches, including algorithms; 
expressive and syntactic generalizations/extensions and specializations/restrictions, 
with corresponding characterizations and guarantees for verifiability (including strong 
explainability and the corresponding logical explainability properties discussed in section 
I.E.); computational tractability/scalability; and translations among ML and AR kinds
Create initial open-source software implementing algorithms for experiments about and 
demonstrations of their approach, including AR-based ML inferencing and training 
Exhibit the enhancements of their approach per the phase metrics listed in Figure 1 
Work with the IV&V team to identify specific inter-performer-team approach 
compositions that would be most fruitful to explore in Hackathons, discussed later in 
this section 
Tackle AR-based-ML training in a computationally feasible manner for large problem 
sizes and demonstrate scalability of this training
Ensure AR-based-ML models can be rapidly adapted to previously unseen data through 
means such as, but not limited to, minimal additional training data or human/manual 
editing/updating of model knowledge (e.g., of model rules and facts)
TA2 will develop a software composition library that will support inter-approach compositions, 
performing low-lift integration of the IV&V team validated TA1 tools and other software into a 
central hub. TA2 will have significantly fewer performers than TA1, with performers working 
closely with the IV&V team. During this program, TA2 performers will:
Integrate the IV&V team validated TA1 performer approaches into a common software 
library of tools. This TA2 created library should implement common structures between 
differing performer approaches, such as common terminology, theoretical/conceptual 
elements, standardized data formats, software functionalities such as interfaces, and 
end-to-end explanations, where each step of explanation would be provided by the 
relevant TA1 componentry. The low-lift integration of TA1 tools by TA2 may include 
refactoring the tools to integrate into the common library but should not include new 
development of TA1 theory or algorithms nor of other TA1 outputs/products.

NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT AND AGREEMENT FOR RECEPTION AND CONTROL OF CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION

FOR INTERESTED CONTRACTORS FOR UNITED STATES TRANSPORTATION COMMAND (USTRANSCOM) CONTRACTS

NOTE: This Agreement is a standard agreement designed for use by contractor (including sub-contractor) employees preparing proposals for USTRANSCOM contracts.  Its use is designed to protect non-public Government information from disclosure, identify potential conflicts of interest, and prevent violations of federal statutes/regulations.  The restrictions contained in this agreement also serve contractors by promoting compliant behavior that keeps contractors eligible to compete for Government contracts.  In addition to the potential impact on future business opportunities, failure to abide by this agreement could result in administrative, civil, or criminal penalties specified by statute or regulation.

I, 	, currently an employee of 	, hereby agree to the terms and conditions set forth below. I further agree that any company or entity by whom I am employed, represent, or act of its behalf, is also bound by this agreement.

2.  I understand that I will have access to controlled unclassified information provided as a result of my request for the Technical Data Package for the HTC71125QD039 Transportation Command "Medical" Regulating and Command & Control Evacuation System (TRAC2ES) Request for Quote. I fully understand that such information is sensitive and must be protected in accordance with 41 U.S.C. §2101-§2107 and FAR 3.1.  

3. As used in this agreement and as defined in 32 CFR Part 2002, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) is information the Government creates or possesses, or that an entity creates or possesses for or on behalf of the Government, that a law, regulation, or Government-wide policy (LRGWP) requires or permits an agency to handle using safeguarding or dissemination controls. However, CUI does not include classified information [Information that Executive Order 13526, Classified National Security Information, December 29, 2009 (3 CFR, 2010 Comp., p. 298), any predecessor or successor order, or the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, requires agencies to mark with classified markings and protect against unauthorized disclosure] or information a non-executive branch entity possesses and maintains in its own systems that did not come from, or was not created or possessed by or for, an executive branch agency or an entity acting for an agency. 

The government may require or permit safeguarding or dissemination controls in three ways: (1) Requiring or permitting agencies to control or protect the information but providing no specific controls, which makes the information CUI Basic; (2) Requiring or permitting agencies to control or protect the information and providing specific controls for doing so, which makes the information CUI Specified; or (3) Requiring or permitting agencies to control the information and specifying only some of those controls, which makes the information CUI Specified, but with CUI Basic controls where the authority does not specify. 

3.	I agree to the following:

Non-disclosure: I agree to not disclose any CUI (in whole or in part, alone or in combination with other information, directly, indirectly, or derivatively)  to which I am granted access to anyone who, or anything that, is not granted such access pursuant to an applicable lawful Government purpose. I understand my responsibilities to protect and not disclose CUI except for, and to people with, an appropriate lawful Government purpose and also possess a fully executed NDA. To ascertain whether someone or something is authorized access, pursuant to an applicable lawful Government purpose, to CUI that is under my control or in my possession, I will do so according to 32 CFR Part 2002, Department of Defense guidance, USTRANSCOM Guidance and applicable procedures. 

I agree not to disclose the CUI by any means to any person except to an individual (non-Government person including, but not limited to, a person in my company, affiliated companies, sub-contractors, etc.) who has a need to know related to the immediate proposal, has executed a valid form of this non-disclosure agreement, and I understand that misuse of non-public information is subject to penalties established in applicable laws, regulations, or Government-wide policies.  All distribution of the documents will be controlled with the concurrence of the Contracting Officer.  

Scope of CUI: I understand that the CUI to which I am granted access includes any CUI I create or use on behalf of or for the Government proposal, CUI I receive from the Government to maintain, handle, transmit, or use (for research, in derivative documents, etc.), or CUI originating from another source (such as CUI generated for the Government by a contractor or research entity).

I agree to not use such information for any non-Governmental purposes or government purpose not being TRAC2ES including, but not limited to, the preparation of bids or proposals for work not in support of this specified requirement, or the development or execution of other business or commercial ventures.

Security/control: I am obligated to protect CUI to which I am granted access from unauthorized disclosure, in accordance with the terms of this agreement, 32 CFR Part 2002, Department of Defense guidance, USTRANSCOM Guidance and the applicable procedures to the specific categories of CUI to which I am granted access.

I agree to store the information in such a manner as to prevent inadvertent disclosure or releases to individuals who have not been authorized access to it.

I agree to delete and destroy the information upon notification from the contracting officer and am obligated to provide a response upon completion. 

Reporting breaches: I agree that I shall promptly report to appropriate officials, in accordance with the guidance issued for the applicable category of CUI, any unauthorized disclosure that I have knowledge of whether or not I am personally involved. I also understand that my anonymity will be preserved to the extent possible when reporting such violations.

Time: I understand that all conditions and obligations imposed upon me by this agreement apply during the time I am granted access to CUI, and at all times thereafter while such information remains controlled. These conditions and obligations may no longer apply if I am explicitly released in writing by an authorized representative of USTRANSCOM or the United States Government. 

Breach: If I violate the terms and conditions of this agreement, such violation may result in cancellation of my access to CUI, and may result in civil and criminal sanctions. This may also serve as a basis for denying me access to other types of information under USTRANSCOM’s control or result in the disqualification from submitting an TRAC2ES  offer.

Assignee: I assign to the United States Government all royalties, remunerations, and emoluments that have resulted, will result, or may result from any disclosure, publication, or revelation of CUI to which I am granted access that is inconsistent with the terms of this agreement.

Remedies: This agreement is made and intended for the benefit of the United States Government and may be enforced by the United States Government or the authorized non-Federal entity. By granting me access to CUI in this context, the United States Government may seek any remedy available to it to enforce this agreement, including, but not limited to, application for a court order prohibiting disclosure of CUI in breach of this agreement. I understand that if I violate the terms and conditions of this agreement, I could be subjected to civil, or criminal action, as appropriate, under the procedures applicable to the category of CUI involved, and neither the United States Government nor the non-Federal authorized entity have waived any statutory or common law evidentiary privileges or protections that they may assert in any administrative or court proceeding to protect any CUI to which I have been given access under the terms of this agreement.

Severability: Each provision of this agreement is severable. If a court should find any provision of this agreement to be unenforceable, all other provisions shall remain in full force and effect. 

Other agreements: My execution of this agreement shall not nullify or affect in any manner any other secrecy or non-disclosure agreement(s) that I have executed or may execute with USTRANSCOM, the United States Government, or any of its other departments or agencies.

4.  I understand that this agreement is personal to me and shall survive and remain in full force and effect notwithstanding any change in current employment. I read this agreement carefully and my questions, if any, were answered. I have had an opportunity and/or the benefit of private counsel and hereby knowingly and informatively accept the terms of this Non-Disclosure Agreement.

By signing below, I certify that I have read and understand the terms of this Non-Disclosure Agreement and voluntarily agree to be bound by its terms.

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

1. INTRODUCTION: THIS IS A TOTAL 100% SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (SDVOSB) SET-ASIDE in accordance with Public Law 109-461.  This is a Request for SF330s for Architect/Engineer (A/E) Design Services for Project Number 541-24-101, A/E Design Renovate PACU and Cath Lab Commissioning at the Louis Stokes VA Medical Center, 10701 East Boulevard, Cleveland, OH 44106.  

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO SOLICITATION PACKAGE WILL BE ISSUED VIA SAM.GOV. A request for proposal will be issued directly to the highest ranked firm for which negotiations will commence in accordance with FAR Subpart 36.6. The anticipated A/E design services, to be awarded, will be procured in accordance with the Selection of Architects and Engineers Act (Public Law 92- 582), Federal Acquisition Regulation Subpart 36.6, and VA Acquisition Regulation Subpart 836.6.

2. DESCRIPTION: The AE firm shall provide all programming, design Submissions, Site Investigation/Field Verification Services, Asbestos Testing, Construction Documents, Technical Specifications, Cost Estimates, Reports, and Construction Administration Services for the project A/E Renovate PACU and Cath Lab Commissioning, located on the Louis Stokes Veterans Affairs Medical Center, 10701 East Boulevard, Cleveland, OH 44106.

See attached Statement of Work for further requirements

Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price

Estimated Cost of Construction is: $16,000,000.00

NAICS Code: 541330

Size Standard: $25.5 Million

(1) SDVOSB eligible firm;

(3) Deviation – [Certified] SDVOSB/VOSB [listed in] the [SBA certification database (aka DSBS SBA) at https://search.certifications.sba.gov/advanced?page=0  

If registration is required, visit https://search.certifications.sba.gov/advanced?page=0 

Additionally, all eligible firms must be registered and current in the System for Award Management (SAM) database in order to be evaluated and eligible for contract award. If the firm is not registered in SAM, you may register online at https://www.sam.gov. 

4) SET ASIDE FACTOR

This procurement is a Total Set-Aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB)

AE firms. The primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541330,

Engineering Services are also required as this is a multi-disciplinary Engineering requirement and

therefore experience and qualifications for the Engineering services are being evaluated as part of

this solicitation. Offerors that are not an SDVOSB firm will be ineligible for consideration. Verification
